```
    53→    cli_exclusions = getattr(args, "exclude", None) or []
    54→    persisted = config.get("exclude", [])
    55→    combined = list(cli_exclusions) + [e for e in persisted if e not in cli_exclusions]
    56→    if not combined:

    76→    For the review command, the last scan path (stored in state) is used as the

   121→    """Handle explicit help command when present in parser config."""
   122→    topic = list(getattr(args, "topic", []) or [])
   123→    try:

   131→    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
   132→        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
   133→            try:

   135→            except (AttributeError, OSError):
```

```
    50→class ImportPayloadLoadError(ValueError):
    51→    """Raised when review import payload parsing/validation fails."""
    52→
    53→    def __init__(self, errors: list[str]) -> None:
    54→        cleaned = [str(error).strip() for error in errors if str(error).strip()]
    55→        self.errors = cleaned
    56→        message = "; ".join(cleaned) if cleaned else "import payload validation failed"
    57→        super().__init__(message)

    60→def _normalize_import_payload_shape(
    61→    payload: dict[str, Any],
    62→) -> tuple[ReviewImportPayload | None, list[str]]:
    63→    """Normalize payload into required-key contract with strict type checks."""
    64→    errors: list[str] = []
    65→    findings = payload.get("findings")
    66→    if not isinstance(findings, list):
    67→        errors.append("findings must be a JSON array")
    68→        findings = []
    69→
    70→    assessments = payload.get("assessments")
    71→    if assessments is None:
    72→        assessments = {}
    73→    elif not isinstance(assessments, dict):
    74→        errors.append("assessments must be an object when provided")
    75→        assessments = {}
    76→
    77→    reviewed_files = payload.get("reviewed_files")
    78→    normalized_reviewed_files: list[str] = []
    79→    if reviewed_files is None:
    80→        normalized_reviewed_files = []
    81→    elif isinstance(reviewed_files, list):
    82→        normalized_reviewed_files = [
    83→            str(item).strip()
    84→            for item in reviewed_files
    85→            if isinstance(item, str) and str(item).strip()
    86→        ]
    87→    else:
    88→        errors.append("reviewed_files must be an array when provided")
    89→
    90→    review_scope = payload.get("review_scope")
    91→    if review_scope is None:
    92→        review_scope = {}
    93→    elif not isinstance(review_scope, dict):
    94→        errors.append("review_scope must be an object when provided")
    95→        review_scope = {}
    96→
    97→    provenance = payload.get("provenance")
    98→    if provenance is None:
    99→        provenance = {}
   100→    elif not isinstance(provenance, dict):
   101→        errors.append("provenance must be an object when provided")
   102→        provenance = {}
   103→
   104→    dimension_notes = payload.get("dimension_notes")
   105→    if dimension_notes is None:
   106→        dimension_notes = {}
   107→    elif not isinstance(dimension_notes, dict):
   108→        errors.append("dimension_notes must be an object when provided")
   109→        dimension_notes = {}
   110→
   111→    policy = payload.get(_ASSESSMENT_POLICY_KEY)
   112→    normalized_policy = (
   113→        policy if isinstance(policy, dict) else AssessmentImportPolicyModel().to_dict()
   114→    )
   115→    if errors:
   116→        return None, errors
   117→    return (
   118→        {
   119→            "findings": findings,
   120→            "assessments": assessments,
   121→            "reviewed_files": normalized_reviewed_files,
   122→            "review_scope": review_scope,
   123→            "provenance": provenance,
   124→            "dimension_notes": dimension_notes,
   125→            [REDACTED],
   126→        },
   127→        [],
   128→    )

   131→def _assessment_provenance_status(
   132→    findings_data: ReviewImportPayload,
   133→    *,
   134→    import_file: str,
   135→) -> AssessmentProvenanceModel:
   136→    """Evaluate whether assessments come from a trusted blind batch artifact."""
   137→    return _policy_assessment_provenance_status(
   138→        findings_data,
   139→        import_file=import_file,
   140→    )
   141→
   142→
   143→def _validate_attested_external_attestation(attest: str | None) -> str | None:
   144→    """Validate and normalize attestation text for attested external imports."""
   145→    if not isinstance(attest, str) or not attest.strip():
   146→        return None
   147→    text = attest.strip()
   148→    lowered = text.lower()
   149→    if all(phrase in lowered for phrase in _ATTESTED_EXTERNAL_REQUIRED_PHRASES):
   150→        return text
   151→    return None
   152→
   153→
   154→def _apply_assessment_import_policy(
   155→    findings_data: ReviewImportPayload,
   156→    *,
   157→    import_file: str,
   158→    attested_external: bool,
   159→    attested_attest: str | None,
   160→    manual_override: bool,
   161→    manual_attest: str | None,
   162→    trusted_assessment_source: bool,
   163→    trusted_assessment_label: str | None,
   164→) -> tuple[ReviewImportPayload | None, list[str]]:
   165→    """Apply trust gating for assessment imports (findings import always allowed)."""
   166→    assessments = findings_data["assessments"]
   167→    has_assessments = bool(assessments)
   168→    assessment_count = len(assessments) if has_assessments else 0
   169→    provenance_status = _assessment_provenance_status(
   170→        findings_data, import_file=import_file
   171→    )
   172→    policy = AssessmentImportPolicyModel(
   173→        assessments_present=has_assessments,
   174→        assessment_count=int(assessment_count),
   175→        trusted=False,
   176→        mode="none",
   177→        reason="",
   178→        provenance=provenance_status,
   179→    )
   180→
   181→    def _attach_policy(payload: ReviewImportPayload) -> ReviewImportPayload:
   182→        normalized = dict(payload)
   183→        normalized[_ASSESSMENT_POLICY_KEY] = policy.to_dict()
   184→        return normalized
   185→
   186→    if not has_assessments:
   187→        return _attach_policy(findings_data), []
   188→
   189→    if trusted_assessment_source:
   190→        policy = replace(
   191→            policy,
   192→            mode="trusted_internal",
   193→            trusted=True,
   194→            reason=(trusted_assessment_label or "trusted internal run-batches import"),
   195→        )
   196→        return _attach_policy(findings_data), []
   197→
   198→    if attested_external:
   199→        normalized_attest = _validate_attested_external_attestation(attested_attest)
   200→        if normalized_attest is None:
   201→            return None, [
   202→                "--attested-external requires --attest containing both "
   203→                "'without awareness' and 'unbiased'"
   204→            ]
   205→        if provenance_status.trusted is not True:
   206→            return None, [
   207→                "--attested-external requires valid blind packet provenance "
   208→                f"(current status: {provenance_status.reason or 'untrusted provenance'})"
   209→            ]
   210→        runner = provenance_status.runner.strip().lower()
   211→        if runner not in _ATTESTED_EXTERNAL_RUNNERS:
   212→            return None, [
   213→                "--attested-external currently supports runner='claude' provenance only"
   214→            ]
   215→        policy = replace(
   216→            policy,
   217→            mode="attested_external",
   218→            trusted=True,
   219→            reason="attested external blind subagent provenance",
   220→            attest=normalized_attest,
   221→        )
   222→        return _attach_policy(findings_data), []
   223→
   224→    if manual_override:
   225→        if not isinstance(manual_attest, str) or not manual_attest.strip():
   226→            return None, ["--manual-override requires --attest"]
   227→        policy = replace(
   228→            policy,
   229→            mode="manual_override",
   230→            reason="manual override attested by operator",
   231→            attest=manual_attest.strip(),
   232→        )
   233→        return _attach_policy(findings_data), []
   234→
   235→    policy = replace(policy, mode="findings_only")
   236→    if findings_data["provenance"]:
   237→        provenance_reason = provenance_status.reason.strip()
   238→        if provenance_status.trusted is True:
   239→            policy = replace(
   240→                policy,
   241→                reason=(
   242→                    "external imports cannot self-attest trust even when provenance appears valid; "
   243→                    "run review --run-batches to apply assessments automatically"
   244→                ),
   245→            )
   246→        elif provenance_reason:
   247→            policy = replace(
   248→                policy,
   249→                reason=(
   250→                    "external imports cannot self-attest trust "
   251→                    f"({provenance_reason}); run review --run-batches to apply assessments automatically"
   252→                ),
   253→            )
   254→        else:
   255→            policy = replace(
   256→                policy,
   257→                reason=(
   258→                    "external imports cannot self-attest trust; "
   259→                    "run review --run-batches to apply assessments automatically"
   260→                ),
   261→            )
   262→    else:
   263→        policy = replace(
   264→            policy,
   265→            reason="missing trusted run-batches source; imported findings only",
   266→        )
   267→    payload = dict(findings_data)
   268→    payload["assessments"] = {}
   269→    payload[_ASSESSMENT_POLICY_KEY] = policy.to_dict()
   270→    return payload, []

   272→
   273→def _parse_and_validate_import(
   274→    import_file: str,
   275→    *,
   276→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   277→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   278→    trusted_assessment_source: bool = False,
   279→    trusted_assessment_label: str | None = None,
   280→    attested_external: bool = False,
   281→    manual_override: bool = False,
   282→    manual_attest: str | None = None,
   283→    assessment_override: bool = False,
   284→    assessment_note: str | None = None,
   285→) -> tuple[ReviewImportPayload | None, list[str]]:
   286→    """Parse and validate a review import file (pure function).
   287→
   288→    Returns ``(data, errors)`` where *data* is the normalized payload on
   289→    success, or ``None`` when errors prevent import.
   290→    """
   291→    findings_path = Path(import_file)
   292→    if not findings_path.exists():
   293→        return None, [f"file not found: {import_file}"]
   294→    try:
   295→        findings_data = json.loads(findings_path.read_text())
   296→    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
   297→        return None, [f"error reading findings: {exc}"]
   298→
   299→    if isinstance(findings_data, list):
   300→        findings_data = {"findings": findings_data}
   301→
   302→    if not isinstance(findings_data, dict):
   303→        return None, ["findings file must contain a JSON array or object"]
   304→
   305→    if "findings" not in findings_data:
   306→        return None, ["findings object must contain a 'findings' key"]
   307→    normalized_findings_data, shape_errors = _normalize_import_payload_shape(
   308→        findings_data
   309→    )
   310→    if shape_errors:
   311→        return None, shape_errors
   312→    assert normalized_findings_data is not None
   313→
   314→    override_enabled, override_attest = resolve_override_context(
   315→        manual_override=manual_override,
   316→        manual_attest=manual_attest,
   317→        assessment_override=assessment_override,
   318→        assessment_note=assessment_note,
   319→    )
   320→    if attested_external and override_enabled:
   321→        return None, [
   322→            "--attested-external cannot be combined with --manual-override"
   323→        ]
   324→    if attested_external and allow_partial:
   325→        return None, [
   326→            "--attested-external cannot be combined with --allow-partial; "
   327→            "attested score imports require fully valid findings payloads"
   328→        ]
   329→    if override_enabled and allow_partial:
   330→        return None, [
   331→            "--manual-override cannot be combined with --allow-partial; "
   332→            "manual score imports require fully valid findings payloads"
   333→        ]
   334→    findings_data, policy_errors = _apply_assessment_import_policy(
   335→        normalized_findings_data,
   336→        import_file=import_file,
   337→        attested_external=attested_external,
   338→        attested_attest=override_attest,
   339→        manual_override=override_enabled,
   340→        manual_attest=override_attest,
   341→        trusted_assessment_source=trusted_assessment_source,
   342→        trusted_assessment_label=trusted_assessment_label,
   343→    )
   344→    if policy_errors:
   345→        return None, policy_errors
   346→    assert findings_data is not None
   347→
   348→    missing_feedback, missing_low_score_findings = _validate_assessment_feedback(
   349→        findings_data
   350→    )
   351→    if missing_low_score_findings:
   352→        if override_enabled:
   353→            if not isinstance(override_attest, str) or not override_attest.strip():
   354→                return None, ["--manual-override requires --attest"]
   355→            return findings_data, []
   356→        return None, [
   357→            f"assessments below {LOW_SCORE_FINDING_THRESHOLD:.1f} must include at "
   358→            "least one finding for that same dimension with a concrete suggestion. "
   359→            f"Missing: {', '.join(missing_low_score_findings)}"
   360→        ]
   361→
   362→    if missing_feedback:
   363→        if override_enabled:
   364→            if not isinstance(override_attest, str) or not override_attest.strip():
   365→                return None, ["--manual-override requires --attest"]
   366→            return findings_data, []
   367→        return None, [
   368→            f"assessments below {ASSESSMENT_FEEDBACK_THRESHOLD:.1f} must include explicit feedback "
   369→            "(finding with same dimension and non-empty suggestion, or "
   370→            "dimension_notes evidence for that dimension). "
   371→            f"Missing: {', '.join(missing_feedback)}"
   372→        ]
   373→
   374→    schema_errors = _validate_holistic_findings_schema(
   375→        findings_data,
   376→        lang_name=lang_name,
   377→    )
   378→    if schema_errors and not allow_partial:
   379→        visible_errors = schema_errors[:10]
   380→        remaining = len(schema_errors) - len(visible_errors)
   381→        errors = [
   382→            "findings schema validation failed for holistic import. "
   383→            "Fix payload or rerun with --allow-partial to continue."
   384→        ]
   385→        errors.extend(visible_errors)
   386→        if remaining > 0:
   387→            errors.append(f"... {remaining} additional schema error(s) omitted")
   388→        return None, errors
   389→
   390→    return findings_data, []
   391→
   392→
   393→def load_import_findings_data(
   394→    import_file: str,
   395→    *,
   396→    colorize_fn=None,
   397→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   398→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   399→    trusted_assessment_source: bool = False,
   400→    trusted_assessment_label: str | None = None,
   401→    attested_external: bool = False,
   402→    manual_override: bool = False,
   403→    manual_attest: str | None = None,
   404→    assessment_override: bool = False,
   405→    assessment_note: str | None = None,
   406→) -> ReviewImportPayload:
   407→    """Load and normalize review import payload to object format.
   408→
   409→    Raises ``ImportPayloadLoadError`` when validation fails.
   410→    """
   411→    data, errors = _parse_and_validate_import(
   412→        import_file,
   413→        lang_name=lang_name,
   414→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   415→        trusted_assessment_source=trusted_assessment_source,
   416→        trusted_assessment_label=trusted_assessment_label,
   417→        attested_external=attested_external,
   418→        manual_override=manual_override,
   419→        manual_attest=manual_attest,
   420→        assessment_override=assessment_override,
   421→        assessment_note=assessment_note,
   422→    )
   423→    if errors:
   424→        raise ImportPayloadLoadError(errors)
   425→    assert data is not None  # guaranteed when errors is empty
   426→    return data
   427→
   428→
   429→def assessment_policy_from_payload(payload: ReviewImportPayload) -> AssessmentImportPolicy:
   430→    """Return parsed assessment policy metadata from a loaded import payload."""
   431→    policy = payload[_ASSESSMENT_POLICY_KEY]
   432→    if isinstance(policy, dict):
   433→        return policy
   434→    return AssessmentImportPolicyModel().to_dict()
   435→
   436→
   437→def assessment_policy_model_from_payload(
   438→    payload: ReviewImportPayload,
   439→) -> AssessmentImportPolicyModel:
   440→    """Return typed assessment policy metadata from a loaded import payload."""
   441→    return AssessmentImportPolicyModel.from_mapping(assessment_policy_from_payload(payload))
   442→
   443→
   444→def assessment_mode_label(policy: AssessmentImportPolicy) -> str:
   445→    """Return a user-facing label for the selected assessment import mode."""
   446→    mode = AssessmentImportPolicyModel.from_mapping(policy).mode.strip().lower()
   447→    return _ASSESSMENT_MODE_LABELS.get(mode, f"unknown ({mode or 'none'})")
   448→

   450→def print_assessment_policy_notice(
   451→    policy: AssessmentImportPolicy,
   452→    *,
   453→    import_file: str,
   454→    colorize_fn,
   455→) -> None:
   456→    """Render trust/override status for assessment-bearing imports."""
   457→    policy_model = AssessmentImportPolicyModel.from_mapping(policy)
   458→    if not policy_model.assessments_present:
   459→        return
   460→    mode = policy_model.mode.strip().lower()
   461→    reason = policy_model.reason.strip()
   462→
   463→    if mode == "trusted":

   465→        detail = f" · blind packet {packet_path}" if packet_path else ""
   466→        print(

   474→    if mode == "trusted_internal":
   475→        count = int(policy_model.assessment_count or 0)
   476→        reason_text = policy_model.reason.strip()
   477→        suffix = f" ({reason_text})" if reason_text else ""
   478→        print(

   485→
   486→    if mode == "manual_override":
   487→        count = int(policy_model.assessment_count or 0)
   488→        print(
   489→            colorize_fn(
   490→                f"  WARNING: applying {count} assessment update(s) via manual override from untrusted provenance.",
   491→                "yellow",
   492→            )
   493→        )
   494→        if reason:
   495→            print(colorize_fn(f"  Reason: {reason}", "dim"))
   496→        return
   497→
   498→    if mode == "attested_external":
   499→        count = int(policy_model.assessment_count or 0)
   500→        print(
   501→            colorize_fn(
   502→                f"  Assessment updates applied via attested external blind review: {count} dimension(s).",
   503→                "dim",
   504→            )
   505→        )
   506→        if reason:
   507→            print(colorize_fn(f"  Reason: {reason}", "dim"))
   508→        return
   509→
   510→    if mode == "findings_only":
   511→        count = int(policy_model.assessment_count or 0)
   512→        print(
   513→            colorize_fn(
   514→                "  WARNING: untrusted assessment source detected. "
   515→                f"Imported findings only; skipped {count} assessment score update(s).",
   516→                "yellow",
   517→            )
   518→        )
   519→        if reason:
   520→            print(colorize_fn(f"  Reason: {reason}", "dim"))
   521→        print(
   522→            colorize_fn(

   524→                "dim",
   525→            )
   526→        )
   527→        print(

   530→                "dim",
   531→            )
   532→        )
   533→        print(
```

```
    62→def _is_runner_missing(text: str) -> bool:
    63→    return (
    64→        "codex not found" in text
    65→        or ("no such file or directory" in text and "$ codex " in text)
    66→        or ("errno 2" in text and "codex" in text)
    67→    )

    70→def _is_runner_auth_failure(text: str) -> bool:
    71→    return any(phrase in text for phrase in _RUNNER_AUTH_PHRASES)
    72→
    73→
    74→def classify_runner_failure(log_text: str) -> str:
    75→    """Classify batch failure type from log contents."""
    76→    text = log_text.lower()
    77→    if "timeout after" in text:
    78→        return "timeout"
    79→    if any(phrase in text for phrase in _USAGE_LIMIT_PHRASES):
    80→        return "usage_limit"
    81→    if any(phrase in text for phrase in TRANSIENT_RUNNER_PHRASES):
    82→        return "stream_disconnect"
    83→    if _is_runner_missing(text):
    84→        return "runner_missing"
    85→    if _is_runner_auth_failure(text):
    86→        return "runner_auth"
```

```
     5→import logging
     6→from collections.abc import Callable
     7→from functools import lru_cache

     9→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    10→
    11→from desloppify import languages as lang_api
    12→from desloppify.core.text_api import PROJECT_ROOT
    13→
    14→if TYPE_CHECKING:
    15→    from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    16→
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→
    21→class LangResolutionError(SystemExit):
    22→    """Raised when language resolution fails with a user-facing message.
    23→
    24→    Inherits from SystemExit so that callers which don't catch it explicitly
    25→    will still terminate with a non-zero exit code, matching the previous
    26→    sys.exit(1) behaviour.  The CLI top-level catches it to print a clean
    27→    error without a traceback.
    28→    """
    29→
    30→    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
    31→        self.message = message
    32→        super().__init__(1)
    33→
    34→
    35→EXTRA_ROOT_MARKERS = (
    36→    "package.json",
    37→    "pyproject.toml",
    38→    "setup.py",
    39→    "setup.cfg",
    40→    "go.mod",
    41→    "Cargo.toml",
    42→)
    43→
    44→
    45→def _cache_once(fn: Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]]) -> Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]]:
    46→    """Cache a zero-arg function once while preserving cache_clear for tests."""
    47→    cached = lru_cache(maxsize=1)(fn)
    48→    return cached
    49→
    50→
    51→@_cache_once
    52→def _lang_config_markers() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    53→    """Collect project-root marker files from language plugins + fallback markers."""
    54→    markers = set(EXTRA_ROOT_MARKERS)
    55→
    56→    for lang_name in lang_api.available_langs():
    57→        try:
    58→            cfg = lang_api.get_lang(lang_name)
    59→        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
    60→            logger.debug(
    61→                "Skipping language marker collection for %s: %s", lang_name, exc
    62→            )
    63→            continue
    64→        for marker in getattr(cfg, "detect_markers", []) or []:
    65→            if not isinstance(marker, str):
    66→                continue
    67→            cleaned = marker.strip()
    68→            if cleaned:
    69→                markers.add(cleaned)
    70→    return tuple(sorted(markers))
    71→
    72→
    73→def resolve_detection_root(
    74→    args,
    75→    *,
    76→    project_root: Path = PROJECT_ROOT,
    77→    marker_provider: Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]] | None = None,
    78→) -> Path:
    79→    """Best root to auto-detect language from."""
    80→    marker_provider = marker_provider or _lang_config_markers
    81→    markers = marker_provider()
    82→
    83→    raw_path = getattr(args, "path", None)
    84→    if not raw_path:
    85→        return project_root
    86→
    87→    candidate = Path(raw_path)
    88→    if not candidate.is_absolute():
    89→        candidate = project_root / candidate
    90→    candidate = candidate.resolve()
    91→    search_root = candidate if candidate.is_dir() else candidate.parent
    92→
    93→    for root in (search_root, *search_root.parents):
    94→        if any((root / marker).exists() for marker in markers):
    95→            return root
    96→    return search_root
    97→
    98→
    99→def auto_detect_lang_name(args) -> str | None:
   100→    """Auto-detect language using the most relevant root for this command."""
   101→    root = resolve_detection_root(args)
   102→    detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(root)
   103→    if detected is None and root != PROJECT_ROOT:
   104→        detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(PROJECT_ROOT)
   105→    return detected
   106→
   107→
   108→def resolve_lang(args) -> LangConfig | None:
   109→    """Resolve language config from args, with auto-detection fallback."""
   110→    lang_name = getattr(args, "lang", None)
   111→    if lang_name is None:
   112→        lang_name = auto_detect_lang_name(args)
   113→    if lang_name is None:
   114→        return None
   115→    try:
   116→        return lang_api.get_lang(lang_name)
   117→    except ValueError as exc:
   118→        langs = lang_api.available_langs()
   119→        langs_str = ", ".join(langs) if langs else "registered language plugins"
   120→        raise LangResolutionError(
   121→            f"{exc}\n  Hint: use --lang to select manually (available: {langs_str})"
   122→        ) from exc
   123→
   124→
   125→def resolve_lang_settings(config: dict, lang: LangConfig) -> dict[str, object]:
   126→    """Resolve persisted per-language settings from config.languages.<lang>."""
   127→    if not isinstance(config, dict):
   128→        return lang.normalize_settings({})
   129→    languages = config.get("languages", {})
   130→    if not isinstance(languages, dict):
   131→        return lang.normalize_settings({})
   132→    raw = languages.get(lang.name, {})
   133→    return lang.normalize_settings(raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else {})
   134→
```

## Error Handling Patterns in Desloppify - Complete Analysis

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, I've identified the following error handling patterns and conflicts that contribute to the "error-contracts" cluster issues:

### 1. **WHERE SYS.EXIT IS USED IN NON-ENTRYPOINT FILES**

The codebase has **numerous instances of `sys.exit()` in helper/non-entrypoint modules**:

**Review module (30+ instances):**
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/batch.py`: Lines 107, 112, 294, 299, 304, 312, 315, 321, 364, 382
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/import_cmd.py`: Lines 277, 298, 361, 504, 523
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/entrypoint.py`: Lines 40, 79, 90, 99
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/external.py`: Multiple instances
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/batches.py`: Lines 31, 63
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/batches_scope.py`: Lines 25, 57
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/runner_packets.py`: Lines 132, 136
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/runner_helpers.py`: Line 1169
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/runner_failures.py`: Line 325

**Other modules:**
- `/desloppify/app/commands/dev_cmd.py`: Lines 24, 30, 148
- `/desloppify/app/commands/next.py`: Line 142

**Problem**: These are called from within helper functions that are invoked by command handlers, breaking the separation of concerns. Helpers should raise exceptions, not terminate the process.

### 2. **EXCEPTION CLASSES IN THE CODEBASE**

Several custom exception classes already exist, following an inconsistent pattern:

**SystemExit-based exception:**
- `LangResolutionError(SystemExit)` in `/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/lang.py` (lines 21-32)
  - Inherits from `SystemExit` to auto-exit if not caught
  - Has a `.message` attribute for clean printing in CLI entrypoint
  - Caught in `cli.py` line 154-156

**ValueError-based exceptions:**
- `ImportFlagValidationError(ValueError)` in `/desloppify/app/commands/review/import_cmd.py` (line 44)
- `ImportPayloadLoadError(ValueError)` in `/desloppify/app/commands/review/import_helpers.py` (line 50)
- `ScanStateContractError(ValueError)` in `/desloppify/app/commands/scan/scan_workflow.py` (line 72)
- `LangRuntimeOptionsError(ValueError)` in `/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/runtime_options.py` (line 10)
- `ReviewContextSchemaError(ValueError)` in various modules

**The pattern:**
- Exceptions are caught individually at call sites
- Handlers exit immediately with `sys.exit(1)` or raise `SystemExit(N)` after catching
- No unified error handling pipeline

### 3. **CONFLICTING EXIT CODES ACROSS MODULES**

Multiple modules use different exit codes inconsistently:

```
sys.exit(1)  - Generic error (most common)
sys.exit(2)  - Schema/contract errors
raise SystemExit(1)  - Alternative pattern (dev_cmd.py, next.py)
raise SystemExit(130)  - SIGINT signal (batches.py:745)
```

Examples of inconsistency:
- `scan.py` lines 124, 127: `raise SystemExit(2) from exc` for runtime options
- `batches.py` line 31: `sys.exit(2)` for validation
- `import_cmd.py` lines 277, 298: `sys.exit(1)` for validation
- `next.py` line 142: `raise SystemExit(1)`

### 4. **PLAN LOAD ERROR HANDLING - "BEST-EFFORT" PATTERNS**

The codebase uses a catch-all tuple `PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS` defined in `/desloppify/core/exception_sets.py`:

```python
PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS = (
    ImportError,
    AttributeError,
    OSError,
    ValueError,
    TypeError,
    KeyError,
)
```

**Silent/logged catching pattern (15+ locations):**
- `scan/scan_preflight.py` lines 54-57: Silently returns on exception
- `import_cmd.py` lines 236-242: Prints to stdout with "dim" coloring, continues execution
- `next.py` lines 156-160: Silently assigns `breakdown = None`
- `helpers/queue_progress.py` lines 304, 338: Silently returns/suppresses
- `show/cmd.py` lines 142-145: Sets `plan_active = None`
- `status_cmd.py` lines 190, 210: Mixed logging behavior

**Problem**: Errors are suppressed instead of propagated, making it impossible for callers to know if the plan actually loaded.

### 5. **RESOLVE COMMAND SPECIAL CASE (lines 116)**

In `/desloppify/app/commands/resolve/cmd.py` lines 94-117:

```python
try:
    if has_living_plan():
        plan = load_plan()
        # ... operations
        save_plan(plan)
except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
    print(colorize("  Warning: could not update living plan.", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
```

**Problem**: Plan operations fail silently, printing only a warning. Guard/cluster behaviors are disabled without informing the user of potential data loss.

### 6. **REVIEW COMMAND ENTRY POINT PATTERN** 

In `/desloppify/app/commands/review/entrypoint.py`:

```python
def _require_lang_or_exit(lang) -> None:
    if lang:
        return
    print(colorize("  Error: could not detect language. Use --lang.", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

def _validate_mode_selection_or_exit(args, *, mode_flags, import_file) -> None:
    if sum(...) > 1:
        print(colorize("Error: choose one review mode...", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    # ... more validation with sys.exit(2)
```

**Pattern**: Functions end with `_or_exit` suffix and call `sys.exit()` directly. This makes them impossible to test or use in contexts where exceptions are expected.

### 7. **DRY-RUN OUTPUT PATHS INCONSISTENT HANDLING**

In `/desloppify/app/commands/review/batch.py` lines 100-118:

```python
packet_override = getattr(args, "packet", None)
if packet_override:
    packet_path = Path(packet_override)
    if not packet_path.exists():
        print_error(f"packet not found: {packet_override}")
        sys.exit(1)
    try:
        packet = json.loads(packet_path.read_text())
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        print_error(f"reading packet: {exc}")
        sys.exit(1)
```

**Problem**: File read failures call `sys.exit()` immediately. These should be caught by entrypoint handlers.

### 8. **CLI ENTRYPOINT EXCEPTION HANDLING** 

In `/desloppify/cli.py` lines 147-159:

```python
try:
    with runtime_scope():
        _resolve_default_path(args)
        _load_shared_runtime(args)
        handler = _resolve_handler(args.command)
        handler(args)
except LangResolutionError as exc:
    print(colorize(f"  {exc.message}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print("\nInterrupted.")
    sys.exit(1)
```

**Current handling:**
- Only `LangResolutionError` is caught explicitly (which is `SystemExit` subclass)
- Everything else propagates as uncaught exception
- No handler for command-level exceptions
- No graceful degradation for partial failures

### 9. **MISSING EXCEPTION CONTRACTS**

No consistent command-level exception types exist:
- No `CommandError` exception class
- No `CommandExit` exception class  
- No structured error context/detail storage
- No standardized error codes mapping

### 10. **BARE EXCEPT BLOCKS**

Minimal bare except blocks found, but pattern exists in:
- `/desloppify/app/commands/review/entrypoint.py` lines 22-30: `except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc: _ = exc` (swallows, uses underscore variable)

## KEY FINDINGS SUMMARY

| Issue | Location | Impact | Example |
|-------|----------|--------|---------|
| **sys.exit() in helpers** | 30+ review module functions | Process terminates unpredictably | `batch.py:107`, `import_cmd.py:277` |
| **Best-effort plan loads** | 15+ command modules | Silent failures, data inconsistency | `scan_preflight.py:56`, `import_cmd.py:236` |
| **Conflicting exit codes** | Multiple modules | Unclear failure reasons | `sys.exit(1)` vs `sys.exit(2)` |
| **_or_exit functions** | review/entrypoint.py | Untestable, non-composable | `_require_lang_or_exit()` |
| **Missing exception hierarchy** | Entire app/commands | No unified error flow | No `CommandError` type |
| **Resolve silent guard disable** | resolve/cmd.py:116 | Potential data loss | Warns but continues on plan load failure |
| **No error context** | All exception handling | Debugging difficult | No structured error details |
| **Inconsistent output paths** | review/batch.py:100-118 | Unpredictable failure modes | File read -> `sys.exit(1)` immediately |

## ARCHITECTURE FOR FIX

The fix should establish:

1. **Exception hierarchy:**
   - `CommandError(Exception)` - base for all command failures
   - `CommandExit(SystemExit)` - wraps exit codes with context
   - Language-specific subclasses

2. **Exit code mapping:**
   - 1 = User error / invalid input
   - 2 = System/contract error
   - 3 = Plan/state error
   - 130 = Interrupted

3. **CLI entrypoint catches:**
   - `CommandError` → print + exit(1)
   - `CommandExit` → print context + exit(code)
   - Uncaught → traceback + exit(1)

4. **Helper module patterns:**
   - Raise exceptions, never call `sys.exit()`
   - Use `_or_raise` naming, not `_or_exit`
   - Propagate full exception chain

5. **Plan load unification:**
   - Create `load_plan_safe()` that returns `Optional[dict]`
   - Distinguish "no plan" from "load error"
   - Log properly at decision points, not silence

```
    66→    *,
    67→    mode_flags: list[bool],
    68→    import_file: object,
    69→) -> None:
    70→    if sum(1 for enabled in mode_flags if enabled) > 1:
    71→        print(
    72→            colorize(
    73→                "  Error: choose one review mode per command "
    74→                "(--merge | --run-batches | --import-run | --external-start | --external-submit | --import | --validate-import).",
    75→                "red",
    76→            ),
    77→            file=sys.stderr,
    78→        )
    79→        sys.exit(1)
    80→
    81→    external_submit = bool(getattr(args, "external_submit", False))
    82→    if external_submit and not import_file:
    83→        print(
    84→            colorize(
    85→                "  Error: --external-submit requires --import FILE.",
    86→                "red",
    87→            ),
    88→            file=sys.stderr,
    89→        )
    90→        sys.exit(2)
    91→    if external_submit and not getattr(args, "session_id", None):
    92→        print(
    93→            colorize(
    94→                "  Error: --external-submit requires --session-id.",
    95→                "red",
    96→            ),
    97→            file=sys.stderr,
    98→        )
    99→        sys.exit(2)
   100→
   101→
   102→def _run_review_mode(
   103→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   104→    *,
   105→    runtime,
   106→    state,
   107→    lang,
   108→    state_file,
   109→    import_file,
   110→    validate_import_file,
   111→) -> None:
   112→    if bool(getattr(args, "merge", False)):
   113→        do_merge(args)
   114→        return
   115→    if bool(getattr(args, "run_batches", False)):
   116→        review_rerun_preflight(state, args, state_file=state_file)
   117→        _do_run_batches(
   118→            args,
   119→            state,
   120→            lang,
   121→            state_file,
   122→            config=runtime.config,
   123→        )
   124→        return
   125→    import_run_dir = getattr(args, "import_run_dir", None)
   126→    if import_run_dir:
   127→        do_import_run(
   128→            import_run_dir,
   129→            state,
   130→            lang,
   131→            state_file,
   132→            config=runtime.config,
   133→            allow_partial=bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False)),
   134→            scan_after_import=bool(getattr(args, "scan_after_import", False)),
   135→            scan_path=str(getattr(args, "path", ".") or "."),
   136→        )
   137→        return
   138→    if bool(getattr(args, "external_start", False)):
   139→        review_rerun_preflight(state, args, state_file=state_file)
   140→        do_external_start(
   141→            args,
   142→            state,
   143→            lang,
   144→            config=runtime.config,
   145→        )
   146→        return
   147→    if bool(getattr(args, "external_submit", False)):
   148→        do_external_submit(
   149→            import_file=str(import_file),
   150→            session_id=str(getattr(args, "session_id")),
   151→            state=state,
   152→            lang=lang,
   153→            state_file=state_file,
   154→            config=runtime.config,
   155→            allow_partial=bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False)),
   156→            scan_after_import=bool(getattr(args, "scan_after_import", False)),
   157→            scan_path=str(getattr(args, "path", ".") or "."),
   158→            dry_run=bool(getattr(args, "dry_run", False)),
   159→        )
   160→        return
   161→    if validate_import_file:
   162→        do_validate_import(
   163→            validate_import_file,
   164→            lang,
   165→            allow_partial=bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False)),
   166→            manual_override=bool(getattr(args, "manual_override", False)),
   167→            attested_external=bool(getattr(args, "attested_external", False)),
   168→            manual_attest=getattr(args, "attest", None),
   169→        )
   170→        return
   171→
   172→    if import_file:
   173→        do_import(
   174→            import_file,
   175→            state,
   176→            lang,
   177→            state_file,
   178→            config=runtime.config,
   179→            allow_partial=bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False)),
   180→            manual_override=bool(getattr(args, "manual_override", False)),
   181→            attested_external=bool(getattr(args, "attested_external", False)),
   182→            manual_attest=getattr(args, "attest", None),
   183→        )
   184→        return
   185→    review_rerun_preflight(state, args, state_file=state_file)
   186→    do_prepare(args, state, lang, state_file, config=runtime.config)
   187→
   188→
   189→def cmd_review(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   190→    """Prepare or import subjective code review findings."""
   191→    _enable_live_review_output()
   192→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   193→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   194→    state = runtime.state
   195→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   196→    _require_lang_or_exit(lang)
   197→
   198→    mode_flags, import_file, validate_import_file = _mode_flags(args)
   199→    _validate_mode_selection_or_exit(
   200→        args,
   201→        mode_flags=mode_flags,
   202→        import_file=import_file,
   203→    )
   204→    _run_review_mode(
   205→        args,
   206→        runtime=runtime,
   207→        state=state,
   208→        lang=lang,
   209→        state_file=state_file,
   210→        import_file=import_file,
   211→        validate_import_file=validate_import_file,
   212→    )
```

```
   287→def _validate_run_dir(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, Path, str]:
   288→    """Validate run directory, load summary, and return (summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path).
   289→
   290→    Exits with error message on any validation failure.
   291→    """
   292→    if not run_dir.is_dir():
   293→        print(colorize(f"  Error: run directory not found: {run_dir}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   294→        sys.exit(1)
   295→
   296→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   297→    if not summary_path.exists():
   298→        print(colorize(f"  Error: no run_summary.json in {run_dir}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   299→        sys.exit(1)
   300→    try:
   301→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   302→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   303→        print(colorize(f"  Error reading run summary: {exc}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   304→        sys.exit(1)
   305→
   306→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   307→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   308→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   309→
   310→    if not successful:
   311→        print(colorize("  Error: no successful batches in run summary.", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   312→        sys.exit(1)
   313→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   314→        print(colorize(f"  Error: blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   315→        sys.exit(1)
   316→
   317→    try:
   318→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   319→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   320→        print(colorize(f"  Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   321→        sys.exit(1)
   322→
   323→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   324→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path

   327→def do_import_run(
   328→    run_dir_path: str,

   330→    lang,
   331→    state_file: str,

   334→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   335→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   336→    scan_path: str = ".",
   337→) -> None:
   338→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   339→
   340→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   341→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   342→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   343→    """
   344→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   345→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   346→
   347→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   348→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   349→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   350→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   351→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   352→
   353→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   354→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   355→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in successful]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   356→    output_files = {
   357→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   358→        for idx in selected_indexes
   359→    }
   360→
   361→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   362→    if missing:
   363→        print(colorize(f"  Error: missing result files for batches: {missing}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   364→        sys.exit(1)
   365→
   366→    batch_results, failures = runner_helpers_mod.collect_batch_results(
   367→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   368→        failures=[],
   369→        output_files=output_files,
   370→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   371→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: batch_core_mod.extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   372→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: batch_core_mod.normalize_batch_result(
   373→            payload,
   374→            dims,
   375→            max_batch_findings=max_batch_findings_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   376→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   377→        ),
   378→    )
   379→
   380→    if not batch_results:
   381→        print(colorize("  Error: no valid batch results could be parsed.", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   382→        sys.exit(1)
   383→
   384→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   385→    if failures:
   386→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   387→
   388→    # -- merge --
   389→    merged = _merge_batch_results(batch_results)
   390→
   391→    # -- build provenance --
   392→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   393→    merged["provenance"] = runner_helpers_mod.build_batch_import_provenance(
   394→        runner=runner,
   395→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   396→        run_stamp=stamp,
   397→        batch_indexes=successful_indexes,
   398→    )
   399→
   400→    # -- write merged output --
   401→    merged_path = run_dir / "holistic_findings_merged.json"
   402→    safe_write_text(merged_path, json.dumps(merged, indent=2) + "\n")
   403→    print(colorize(f"  Merged output: {merged_path}", "bold"))
   404→
   405→    # -- import with trusted source --
   406→    _do_import(
   407→        str(merged_path),
   408→        state,
   409→        lang,
   410→        state_file,
   411→        config=config,
   412→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   413→        trusted_assessment_source=True,
   414→        trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   415→    )
   416→
   417→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   418→    if scan_after_import:
   419→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   420→        if lang_name:
   421→            runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   422→                lang_name=lang_name,
   423→                scan_path=scan_path,

   427→                    python_executable=sys.executable,
   428→                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   429→                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   430→                    colorize_fn=colorize,
   431→                ),
   432→            )
```

```
   102→def _collect_reviewed_files_from_batches(
   103→    *,
   104→    batches: list[dict[str, object]],
   105→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   106→) -> list[str]:
   107→    """Collect normalized file paths reviewed in the selected batch set."""
   108→    reviewed: list[str] = []
   109→    seen: set[str] = set()
   110→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   111→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(batches):
   112→            continue
   113→        batch = batches[idx]
   114→        files = batch.get("files_to_read", [])
   115→        if not isinstance(files, list):
   116→            continue
   117→        for raw in files:
   118→            if not isinstance(raw, str):
   119→                continue
   120→            path = raw.strip().strip(",'\"")
   121→            if not path or path in {".", ".."}:
   122→                continue
   123→            if path.endswith("/"):
   124→                continue
   125→            if path in seen:
   126→                continue
   127→            seen.add(path)
   128→            reviewed.append(path)
   129→    return reviewed
   130→

   132→def _normalize_dimension_list(raw: object) -> list[str]:
   133→    """Normalize dimension collections to a stable, de-duplicated list."""
   134→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
   135→        return []
   136→    out: list[str] = []
   137→    seen: set[str] = set()
   138→    for item in raw:
   139→        if not isinstance(item, str):
   140→            continue
   141→        dim = item.strip()
   142→        if not dim or dim in seen:
   143→            continue
   144→        seen.add(dim)
   145→        out.append(dim)
   146→    return out

   290→    *,
   291→    batch_index: int,
   292→    prompt_path: Path,
   293→    output_path: Path,
   294→    log_path: Path,
   295→    project_root: Path,

   299→    try:

   316→    selected_indexes: list[int],

   320→    project_root: Path,
   321→    run_codex_batch_fn,
   322→) -> dict[int, object]:
   323→    """Build index→callable task map for execute_batches."""
   324→    tasks: dict[int, object] = {}

   409→def do_run_batches(
   410→    args,
   411→    state,
   412→    lang,
   413→    state_file,
   414→    *,
   415→    config: dict | None,
   416→    run_stamp_fn,
   417→    load_or_prepare_packet_fn,
   418→    selected_batch_indexes_fn,
   419→    prepare_run_artifacts_fn,
   420→    run_codex_batch_fn,
   421→    execute_batches_fn,
   422→    collect_batch_results_fn,
   423→    print_failures_fn,
   424→    print_failures_and_exit_fn,
   425→    merge_batch_results_fn,
   426→    build_import_provenance_fn,
   427→    do_import_fn,
   428→    run_followup_scan_fn,
   429→    safe_write_text_fn,
   430→    colorize_fn,
   431→    project_root: Path,
   432→    subagent_runs_dir: Path,
   433→) -> None:
   434→    """Run holistic investigation batches with a local subagent runner."""
   435→    config = config or {}
   436→    runner = getattr(args, "runner", "codex")
   437→    _validate_runner(runner, colorize_fn=colorize_fn)
   438→    allow_partial = bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False))
   439→    policy = resolve_batch_run_policy(args)
   440→    run_parallel = policy.run_parallel
   441→    max_parallel_batches = policy.max_parallel_batches
   442→    heartbeat_seconds = policy.heartbeat_seconds
   443→    batch_timeout_seconds = policy.batch_timeout_seconds
   444→    batch_max_retries = policy.batch_max_retries
```

```
    15→def validate_runner(runner: str, *, colorize_fn) -> None:

    60→def print_review_quality(quality: object, *, colorize_fn) -> None:
    61→    """Render merged review quality summary when present."""
    62→    if not isinstance(quality, dict):
    63→        return
    64→    coverage = quality.get("dimension_coverage")
    65→    density = quality.get("evidence_density")
    66→    high_missing_issue_note = quality.get(
    67→        REVIEW_QUALITY_HIGH_SCORE_MISSING_ISSUES_KEY
    68→    )
    69→    finding_pressure = quality.get("finding_pressure")
    70→    dims_with_findings = quality.get("dimensions_with_findings")
    71→    if not isinstance(coverage, int | float) or not isinstance(density, int | float):
    72→        return
    73→
    74→    pressure_segment = ""
    75→    if isinstance(finding_pressure, int | float) and isinstance(dims_with_findings, int):
    76→        pressure_segment = (
    77→            f", finding-pressure {float(finding_pressure):.2f} "
    78→            f"across {dims_with_findings} dims"
    79→        )
    80→    print(
    81→        colorize_fn(
    82→            "  Review quality: "
    83→            f"dimension coverage {float(coverage):.2f}, "
    84→            f"evidence density {float(density):.2f}, "
    85→            f"high-score-missing-issue-note {int(high_missing_issue_note or 0)}"
    86→            f"{pressure_segment}",
    87→            "dim",
    88→        )
    89→    )

    91→
    92→def collect_reviewed_files_from_batches(
    93→    *,
    94→    batches: list[dict[str, object]],
    95→    selected_indexes: list[int],
    96→) -> list[str]:
    97→    """Collect normalized file paths reviewed in the selected batch set."""
    98→    reviewed: list[str] = []
    99→    seen: set[str] = set()
   100→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   101→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(batches):
   102→            continue
   103→        batch = batches[idx]
   104→        files = batch.get("files_to_read", [])
   105→        if not isinstance(files, list):
   106→            continue
   107→        for raw in files:
   108→            if not isinstance(raw, str):
   109→                continue
   110→            path = raw.strip().strip(",'\"")
   111→            if not path or path in {".", ".."}:
   112→                continue
   113→            if path.endswith("/"):
   114→                continue
   115→            if path in seen:
   116→                continue
   117→            seen.add(path)
   118→            reviewed.append(path)
   119→    return reviewed
   120→
   121→
   122→def normalize_dimension_list(raw: object) -> list[str]:
   123→    """Normalize dimension collections to a stable, de-duplicated list."""
   124→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
   125→        return []
   126→    out: list[str] = []
   127→    seen: set[str] = set()
   128→    for item in raw:
   129→        if not isinstance(item, str):
   130→            continue
   131→        dim = item.strip()
   132→        if not dim or dim in seen:
   133→            continue
   134→        seen.add(dim)
   135→        out.append(dim)
   136→    return out
   137→
   138→
   139→def scored_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name: str) -> list[str]:
   140→    """Return default scored subjective dimensions for one language."""
   141→    try:
   142→        default_dims, _, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   143→    except (ValueError, RuntimeError):
   144→        return []
   145→    return normalize_dimension_list(default_dims)
   146→
   147→
   148→def missing_scored_dimensions(
   149→    *,
   150→    selected_dims: list[str],
   151→    scored_dims: list[str],
   152→) -> list[str]:
   153→    selected = set(selected_dims)
   154→    return [dim for dim in scored_dims if dim not in selected]
   155→
   156→
   157→def missing_dimensions_command(*, missing_dims: list[str], scan_path: str) -> str:
   158→    """Return rerun command for missing subjective dimensions."""
   159→    base = "desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import"
   160→    if scan_path and scan_path != ".":
   161→        base += f" --path {shlex.quote(scan_path)}"
   162→    if missing_dims:
   163→        base += f" --dimensions {','.join(missing_dims)}"
   164→    return base
   165→
   166→
   167→def print_preflight_dimension_scope_notice(
   168→    *,
   169→    selected_dims: list[str],
   170→    scored_dims: list[str],
   171→    explicit_selection: bool,
   172→    scan_path: str,
   173→    colorize_fn,
   174→) -> None:
   175→    """Print trigger-time notice when run scope is a scored-dimension subset."""
   176→    if not scored_dims:
   177→        return
   178→    missing_dims = missing_scored_dimensions(
   179→        selected_dims=selected_dims,
   180→        scored_dims=scored_dims,
   181→    )
   182→    if not missing_dims:
   183→        return
   184→
   185→    covered_count = len([dim for dim in selected_dims if dim in set(scored_dims)])
   186→    scope_reason = (
   187→        "explicit --dimensions selection"
   188→        if explicit_selection
   189→        else "language default review dimension set"
   190→    )
   191→    tone = "yellow" if explicit_selection else "red"
   192→    print(
   193→        colorize_fn(
   194→            "  WARNING: this run targets "
   195→            f"{covered_count}/{len(scored_dims)} scored subjective dimensions "
   196→            f"({scope_reason}).",
   197→            tone,
   198→        )
   199→    )
   200→    preview = ", ".join(missing_dims[:5])
   201→    if len(missing_dims) > 5:
   202→        preview = f"{preview}, +{len(missing_dims) - 5} more"
   203→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Missing from this run: {preview}", "yellow"))
   204→    print(
   205→        colorize_fn(
   206→            "  Rerun missing dimensions: "
   207→            f"`{missing_dimensions_command(missing_dims=missing_dims, scan_path=scan_path)}`",
   208→            "dim",
   209→        )
   210→    )
   211→
   212→
   213→def print_import_dimension_coverage_notice(
   214→    *,
   215→    assessed_dims: list[str],
   216→    scored_dims: list[str],
   217→    scan_path: str,
   218→    colorize_fn,
   219→) -> list[str]:
   220→    """Print result-time notice when merged import covers only a subset."""
   221→    if not scored_dims:
   222→        return []
   223→    missing_dims = missing_scored_dimensions(
   224→        selected_dims=assessed_dims,
   225→        scored_dims=scored_dims,
   226→    )
   227→    if not missing_dims:
   228→        return []
   229→
   230→    covered_count = len([dim for dim in assessed_dims if dim in set(scored_dims)])
   231→    print(
   232→        colorize_fn(
   233→            "  Coverage gap: imported assessments for "
   234→            f"{covered_count}/{len(scored_dims)} scored subjective dimensions.",
   235→            "yellow",
   236→        )
   237→    )
   238→    preview = ", ".join(missing_dims[:5])
   239→    if len(missing_dims) > 5:
   240→        preview = f"{preview}, +{len(missing_dims) - 5} more"
   241→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Still missing: {preview}", "yellow"))
   242→    print(
   243→        colorize_fn(
   244→            "  Run to cover missing dimensions: "
   245→            f"`{missing_dimensions_command(missing_dims=missing_dims, scan_path=scan_path)}`",
   246→            "dim",
   247→        )
   248→    )
   249→    return missing_dims
   250→
   251→
   252→def enforce_trusted_import_coverage_gate(
   253→    *,
   254→    missing_dims: list[str],
   255→    selected_dims: list[str],
   256→    allow_partial: bool,
   257→    scan_path: str,
   258→    colorize_fn,
   259→) -> None:
   260→    """Block trusted assessment import when selected assessment dimensions are missing."""
   261→    if not selected_dims or not missing_dims:
   262→        return
   263→    if allow_partial:
   264→        print(
   265→            colorize_fn(
   266→                "  Coverage override: importing with missing scored dimensions "
   267→                f"because {TRUSTED_IMPORT_COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_FLAG} is enabled.",
   268→                "yellow",
   269→            )
   270→        )
   271→        return
   272→
   273→    preview = ", ".join(missing_dims[:5])
   274→    if len(missing_dims) > 5:
   275→        preview = f"{preview}, +{len(missing_dims) - 5} more"
   276→    print(
   277→        colorize_fn(
   278→            "  Error: trusted assessment import blocked due to incomplete selected-dimension coverage.",
   279→            "red",
   280→        ),
   281→        file=sys.stderr,
   282→    )
   283→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Missing dimensions: {preview}", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
   284→    print(
   285→        colorize_fn(
   286→            "  Retry with full coverage or explicitly bypass with "
   287→            f"{TRUSTED_IMPORT_COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_FLAG}.",
   288→            "yellow",
   289→        ),
   290→        file=sys.stderr,
   291→    )
   292→    print(
   293→        colorize_fn(
   294→            "  Suggested rerun: "
   295→            f"`{missing_dimensions_command(missing_dims=missing_dims, scan_path=scan_path)}`",
   296→            "dim",
   297→        ),
   298→        file=sys.stderr,
   299→    )
   300→    raise SystemExit(1)
   301→
```

```
     2→

     5→
     6→class CommandError(Exception):
     7→    """Raised by command helpers to signal a user-facing CLI error.
     8→
     9→    The CLI entrypoint catches this and prints ``message`` to stderr
    10→    before exiting with ``exit_code``.  Helpers should raise this instead
    11→    of calling ``sys.exit()`` directly so that the error path is testable
    12→    and composable.
    13→    """
    14→
    15→    def __init__(self, message: str, *, exit_code: int = 1) -> None:
    16→        self.message = message
    17→        self.exit_code = exit_code
    18→        super().__init__(message)
    19→
```

```
   375→def _canonical_external_payload(
   376→    raw_payload: dict[str, Any],
   377→    *,
   378→    session: dict[str, Any],
   379→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   380→    """Return import payload with canonical provenance and required session token."""
   381→    session_meta = raw_payload.get("session")
   382→    if not isinstance(session_meta, dict):
   383→        print(
   384→            colorize(
   385→                "  Error: external reviewer payload must include top-level `session` object.",
   386→                "red",
   387→            ),
   388→            file=sys.stderr,
   389→        )
   390→        print(
   391→            colorize(
   392→                "  Expected: {\"session\":{\"id\":\"...\",\"token\":\"...\"},\"assessments\":{...},\"findings\":[...]}",
   393→                "dim",
   394→            ),
   395→            file=sys.stderr,
   396→        )
   397→        sys.exit(1)
   398→
   399→    payload_id = str(session_meta.get("id", "")).strip()
   400→    payload_token = str(session_meta.get("token", "")).strip()
   401→    expected_id = str(session.get("session_id", "")).strip()
   402→    expected_token = str(session.get("token", "")).strip()
   403→    if payload_id != expected_id or payload_token != expected_token:
   404→        print(
   405→            colorize(
   406→                "  Error: session id/token mismatch in external reviewer payload.",
   407→                "red",
   408→            ),
   409→            file=sys.stderr,
   410→        )
   411→        print(
   412→            colorize("  Regenerate output using the session template/instructions.", "yellow"),
   413→            file=sys.stderr,
   414→        )
   415→        sys.exit(1)
   416→
   417→    payload = dict(raw_payload)
   418→    payload.pop("session", None)
   419→    payload.pop("provenance", None)
   420→    payload["provenance"] = {
   421→        "kind": "blind_review_batch_import",
   422→        "blind": True,
   423→        "runner": str(session.get("runner", "claude")),
   424→        "run_stamp": str(session.get("session_id", "")),
   425→        "created_at": _iso_seconds(_utc_now()),
   426→        "packet_path": str(session.get("blind_packet_path", "")),
   427→        "packet_sha256": str(session.get("packet_sha256", "")),
   428→        "external_session_id": expected_id,
   429→    }
   430→    return payload
   431→

   433→def _ensure_session_open_or_exit(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   434→    status = str(session.get("status", "open")).strip().lower()
   435→    if status == "open":
   436→        return
   437→    print(
   438→        colorize(
   439→            f"  Error: session is not open (status={status or 'unknown'}). Start a new session with --external-start.",
   440→            "red",
   441→        ),
   442→        file=sys.stderr,
   443→    )
   444→    sys.exit(1)
   445→
   446→
   447→def _ensure_session_not_expired_or_exit(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   448→    expires_at = _parse_iso(session.get("expires_at"))
   449→    if expires_at is None:
   450→        print(
   451→            colorize(
   452→                "  Error: session metadata is missing/invalid expires_at.",
   453→                "red",
   454→            ),
   455→            file=sys.stderr,
   456→        )
   457→        sys.exit(1)
   458→    now = _utc_now()
   459→    if now <= expires_at:
   460→        return
   461→    print(
   462→        colorize(
   463→            f"  Error: session expired at {session.get('expires_at')}. Start a new session with --external-start.",
   464→            "red",
   465→        ),
   466→        file=sys.stderr,
   467→    )
   468→    sys.exit(1)

   470→
   471→def do_external_submit(
   472→    *,
   473→    import_file: str,
   474→    session_id: str,
   475→    state: dict,
   476→    lang,
   477→    state_file,
   478→    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   479→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   480→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   481→    scan_path: str = ".",
   482→    dry_run: bool = False,
   483→) -> None:
   484→    """Submit external reviewer output via session, adding canonical provenance."""
   485→    config = config or {}
   486→    session_path, session = _session_payload_or_exit(session_id)
   487→    _ensure_session_open_or_exit(session)
   488→    _ensure_session_not_expired_or_exit(session)
   489→
   490→    if str(session.get("runner", "")).strip().lower() not in _EXTERNAL_SUPPORTED_RUNNERS:
   491→        print(
   492→            colorize(
   493→                "  Error: only Claude external sessions currently support durable score submit.",
   494→                "red",
   495→            ),
   496→            file=sys.stderr,
   497→        )
   498→        sys.exit(1)
   499→
   500→    findings_path = Path(import_file)
   501→    raw_payload = _load_json_object(findings_path, label="external findings")
   502→    canonical_payload = _canonical_external_payload(raw_payload, session=session)
   503→
   504→    stamp = runner_helpers_mod.run_stamp()
   505→    session_dir = session_path.parent
   506→    canonical_path = session_dir / f"canonical_import_{stamp}.json"
   507→    safe_write_text(canonical_path, json.dumps(canonical_payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   508→
   509→    if dry_run:
   510→        do_validate_import(
   511→            str(canonical_path),
   512→            lang,
   513→            allow_partial=allow_partial,
   514→            attested_external=True,
   515→            manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   516→        )
   517→        return
   518→
   519→    do_import(
   520→        str(canonical_path),
   521→        state,
   522→        lang,
   523→        state_file,
   524→        config=config,
   525→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   526→        attested_external=True,
   527→        manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   528→    )
   529→
   530→    submitted_at = _iso_seconds(_utc_now())
   531→    session["status"] = "submitted"
   532→    session["submitted_at"] = submitted_at
   533→    session["submitted_input_file"] = str(findings_path)
   534→    session["submitted_canonical_file"] = str(canonical_path)
   535→    safe_write_text(session_path, json.dumps(session, indent=2) + "\n")
   536→
   537→    if scan_after_import:
   538→        code = runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   539→            lang_name=lang.name,
   540→            scan_path=scan_path,
   541→            deps=runner_helpers_mod.FollowupScanDeps(
   542→                project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   543→                timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   544→                python_executable=sys.executable,
   545→                subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   546→                timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   547→                colorize_fn=colorize,
   548→            ),
   549→        )
   550→        if code != 0:
   551→            raise SystemExit(code)
   552→
   553→
   554→__all__ = ["do_external_start", "do_external_submit", "EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT"]
   555→
```

```
   285→def _validate_run_dir(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, Path, str]:
   286→    """Validate run directory, load summary, and return (summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path).
   287→
   288→    Exits with error message on any validation failure.
   289→    """
   290→    if not run_dir.is_dir():
   291→        raise CommandError(f"run directory not found: {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   292→
   293→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   294→    if not summary_path.exists():
   295→        raise CommandError(f"no run_summary.json in {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   296→    try:
   297→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   298→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   299→        raise CommandError(f"Error reading run summary: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   300→
   301→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   302→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   303→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   304→
   305→    if not successful:
   306→        raise CommandError("no successful batches in run summary.", exit_code=1)
   307→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   308→        raise CommandError(f"blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", exit_code=1)

   310→    try:
   311→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   312→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   313→        raise CommandError(f"Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   314→
   315→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   316→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path
   317→
   318→
   319→def do_import_run(
   320→    run_dir_path: str,
   321→    state: dict,
   322→    lang,
   323→    state_file: str,
   324→    *,
   325→    config: dict | None = None,
   326→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   327→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   328→    scan_path: str = ".",
   329→) -> None:
   330→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   331→
   332→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   333→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   334→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   335→    """
   336→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   337→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   338→
   339→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   340→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   341→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   342→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   343→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   344→
   345→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   346→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   347→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in successful]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   348→    output_files = {
   349→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   350→        for idx in selected_indexes
   351→    }
   352→
   353→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   354→    if missing:
   355→        raise CommandError(f"missing result files for batches: {missing}", exit_code=1)
   356→
   357→    batch_results, failures = runner_helpers_mod.collect_batch_results(
   358→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   359→        failures=[],
   360→        output_files=output_files,
   361→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   362→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: batch_core_mod.extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   363→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: batch_core_mod.normalize_batch_result(
   364→            payload,
   365→            dims,
   366→            max_batch_findings=max_batch_findings_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   367→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   368→        ),
   369→    )
   370→
   371→    if not batch_results:
   372→        raise CommandError("no valid batch results could be parsed.", exit_code=1)
   373→
   374→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   375→    if failures:
   376→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   377→
   378→    # -- merge --
   379→    merged = _merge_batch_results(batch_results)
   380→
   381→    # -- build provenance --
   382→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   383→    merged["provenance"] = runner_helpers_mod.build_batch_import_provenance(
   384→        runner=runner,
   385→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   386→        run_stamp=stamp,
   387→        batch_indexes=successful_indexes,
   388→    )
   389→
   390→    # -- write merged output --
   391→    merged_path = run_dir / "holistic_findings_merged.json"
   392→    safe_write_text(merged_path, json.dumps(merged, indent=2) + "\n")
   393→    print(colorize(f"  Merged output: {merged_path}", "bold"))
   394→
   395→    # -- import with trusted source --
   396→    _do_import(
   397→        str(merged_path),
   398→        state,
   399→        lang,
   400→        state_file,
   401→        config=config,
   402→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   403→        trusted_assessment_source=True,
   404→        trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   405→    )
   406→
   407→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   408→    if scan_after_import:
   409→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   410→        if lang_name:
   411→            runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   412→                lang_name=lang_name,
   413→                scan_path=scan_path,
   414→                deps=runner_helpers_mod.FollowupScanDeps(
   415→                    project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   416→                    timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   417→                    python_executable=sys.executable,
   418→                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   419→                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   420→                    colorize_fn=colorize,
   421→                ),
   422→            )
   423→
```
