   116→
   117→def _progress_contract(
   118→    progress_fn,
   119→    *,
   120→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] | None = None,
   121→) -> str:
   122→    """Resolve callback contract once: ``event`` or ``legacy``."""
   123→    if not callable(progress_fn):
   124→        return "none"
   125→    fn_id = id(progress_fn)
   126→    cache = contract_cache if contract_cache is not None else {}
   127→    cached = cache.get(fn_id)
   128→    if cached:
   129→        return cached
   130→    try:
   131→        signature = inspect.signature(progress_fn)
   132→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   133→        contract = "event"
   134→    else:
   135→        required_positional = 0
   136→        for param in signature.parameters.values():
   137→            if param.kind not in (
   138→                inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
   139→                inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
   140→            ):
   141→                continue
   142→            if param.default is inspect.Signature.empty:
   143→                required_positional += 1
   144→        # Legacy callbacks require at least (batch_index, event).
   145→        contract = "legacy" if required_positional >= 2 else "event"
   146→    cache[fn_id] = contract
   147→    return contract
   148→
   149→
   150→def _emit_progress(
   151→    progress_fn,
   152→    batch_index: int,
   153→    event: str,
   154→    code: int | None = None,
   155→    *,
   156→    details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   157→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] | None = None,
   158→) -> Exception | None:
   159→    """Forward a progress event and return callback exceptions to caller."""
   160→    contract = _progress_contract(progress_fn, contract_cache=contract_cache)
   161→    if contract == "none":
   162→        return None
   163→    payload = dict(details or {})
   164→    progress_event = BatchProgressEvent(
   165→        batch_index=batch_index,
   166→        event=event,
   167→        code=code,
   168→        details=payload,
   169→    )
   170→    try:
   171→        if contract == "legacy":
   172→            progress_fn(batch_index, event, code, **payload)
   173→        else:
   174→            progress_fn(progress_event)
   175→        return None
   176→    except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   177→        return RuntimeError(
   178→            f"progress callback failed for event={event} batch={batch_index}: {exc}"
   179→        )
   180→
   181→
   182→def _record_execution_error(
   183→    *,
   184→    error_log_fn,
   185→    failures: set[int],
   186→    idx: int,
   187→    exc: Exception,
   188→) -> None:
   189→    """Record an execution/progress error through shared failure plumbing."""
   190→    if callable(error_log_fn):
   191→        try:
   192→            error_log_fn(idx, exc)
   193→        except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as err:
   194→            log_best_effort_failure(
   195→                logger,
   196→                "record batch execution error via callback",
   197→                err,
   198→            )
   199→    failures.add(idx)
   200→
   201→
   202→def execute_batches(
   203→    *,
   204→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
   205→    options: BatchExecutionOptions | None = None,
   206→    progress_fn=None,
   207→    error_log_fn=None,
   208→    **legacy_options: object,
   209→) -> list[int]:
   210→    """Run indexed tasks and return failed index list.
   211→
   212→    Each value in *tasks* is a zero-arg callable returning an int exit code.
   213→    All domain knowledge (files, prompts, etc.) is pre-bound by the caller.
   214→    """
   215→    resolved_options = _coerce_batch_execution_options(options, **legacy_options)
   216→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] = {}
   217→    indexes = sorted(tasks)
   218→    if resolved_options.run_parallel:
   219→        return _execute_parallel(
   220→            tasks=tasks,
   221→            indexes=indexes,
   222→            progress_fn=progress_fn,
   223→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   224→            max_parallel_workers=resolved_options.max_parallel_workers,
   225→            heartbeat_seconds=resolved_options.heartbeat_seconds,
   226→            clock_fn=resolved_options.clock_fn,
   227→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   228→        )
   229→    return _execute_serial(
   230→        tasks=tasks,
   231→        indexes=indexes,
   232→        progress_fn=progress_fn,
   233→        error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   234→        clock_fn=resolved_options.clock_fn,
   235→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
   236→    )
   237→
   238→
   239→def _execute_serial(
   240→    *,
   241→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
   242→    indexes: list[int],
   243→    progress_fn,
   244→    error_log_fn,
   245→    clock_fn,
   246→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   247→) -> list[int]:
   248→    """Run tasks one at a time — no threads, no closures."""
   249→    failures: set[int] = set()
   250→    for idx in indexes:
   251→        t0 = float(clock_fn())
   252→        start_error = _emit_progress(
   253→            progress_fn,
   254→            idx,
   255→            "start",
   256→            None,
   257→            details={"max_workers": 1},
   258→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   259→        )
   260→        if start_error is not None:
   261→            _record_execution_error(
   262→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   263→                failures=failures,
   264→                idx=idx,
   265→                exc=start_error,
   266→            )
   267→        try:
   268→            code = tasks[idx]()
   269→        except _RUNNER_TASK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   270→            _record_execution_error(
   271→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   272→                failures=failures,
   273→                idx=idx,
   274→                exc=exc,
   275→            )
   276→            code = 1
   277→        if code != 0:
   278→            failures.add(idx)
   279→        done_error = _emit_progress(
   280→            progress_fn,
   281→            idx,
   282→            "done",
   283→            code,
   284→            details={"elapsed_seconds": int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - t0))},
   285→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   286→        )
   287→        if done_error is not None:
   288→            _record_execution_error(
   289→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   290→                failures=failures,
   291→                idx=idx,
   292→                exc=done_error,
   293→            )
   294→    return sorted(failures)
   295→
   296→
   297→def _execute_parallel(
   298→    *,
   299→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
   300→    indexes: list[int],
   301→    progress_fn,
   302→    error_log_fn,
   303→    max_parallel_workers,
   304→    heartbeat_seconds,
   305→    clock_fn,
   306→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   307→) -> list[int]:
   308→    """Run tasks in a thread pool with optional heartbeat monitoring."""
   309→    max_workers, heartbeat = _resolve_parallel_runtime(
   310→        indexes=indexes,
   311→        max_parallel_workers=max_parallel_workers,
   312→        heartbeat_seconds=heartbeat_seconds,
   313→    )
   314→    failures: set[int] = set()
   315→    progress_failures: set[int] = set()
   316→    started_at: dict[int, float] = {}
   317→    lock = threading.Lock()
   318→
   319→    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
   320→        futures = _queue_parallel_tasks(
   321→            executor=executor,
   322→            indexes=indexes,
   323→            tasks=tasks,
   324→            progress_fn=progress_fn,
   325→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   326→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   327→            max_workers=max_workers,
   328→            failures=failures,
   329→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   330→            started_at=started_at,
   331→            lock=lock,
   332→            clock_fn=clock_fn,
   333→        )
   334→        pending = set(futures.keys())
   335→        _drain_parallel_completions(
   336→            pending=pending,
   337→            futures=futures,
   338→            heartbeat=heartbeat,
   339→            indexes=indexes,
   340→            progress_fn=progress_fn,
   341→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   342→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   343→            failures=failures,
   344→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   345→            started_at=started_at,
   346→            lock=lock,
   347→            clock_fn=clock_fn,
   348→        )
   349→    return sorted(failures)
   350→
   351→
   352→def _resolve_parallel_runtime(
   353→    *,
   354→    indexes: list[int],
   355→    max_parallel_workers,
   356→    heartbeat_seconds,
   357→) -> tuple[int, float | None]:
   358→    requested = (
   359→        int(max_parallel_workers)
   360→        if isinstance(max_parallel_workers, int) and max_parallel_workers > 0
   361→        else 8
   362→    )
   363→    max_workers = max(1, min(len(indexes), requested))
   364→    heartbeat = (
   365→        float(heartbeat_seconds)
   366→        if isinstance(heartbeat_seconds, int | float) and heartbeat_seconds > 0
   367→        else None
   368→    )
   369→    return max_workers, heartbeat
   370→
   371→
   372→def _record_progress_error(
   373→    *,
   374→    idx: int,
   375→    err: Exception,
   376→    progress_failures: set[int],
   377→    lock: threading.Lock,
   378→    error_log_fn,
   379→) -> None:
   380→    with lock:
   381→        progress_failures.add(idx)
   382→    if not callable(error_log_fn):
   383→        return
   384→    try:
   385→        error_log_fn(idx, err)
   386→    except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
   387→        log_best_effort_failure(
   388→            logger,
   389→            "record batch progress failure via callback",
   390→            exc,
   391→        )
   392→
   393→
   394→def _run_parallel_task(
   395→    *,
   396→    idx: int,
   397→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
   398→    progress_fn,
   399→    error_log_fn,
   400→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   401→    max_workers: int,
   402→    progress_failures: set[int],
   403→    started_at: dict[int, float],
   404→    lock: threading.Lock,
   405→    clock_fn,
   406→) -> int:
   407→    with lock:
   408→        started_at[idx] = float(clock_fn())
   409→    progress_error = _emit_progress(
   410→        progress_fn,
   411→        idx,
   412→        "start",
   413→        None,
   414→        details={"max_workers": max_workers},
   415→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
   416→    )
   417→    if progress_error is not None:
   418→        _record_progress_error(
   419→            idx=idx,
   420→            err=progress_error,
   421→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   422→            lock=lock,
   423→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   424→        )
   425→    return tasks[idx]()
   426→
   427→
   428→def _queue_parallel_tasks(
   429→    *,
   430→    executor: ThreadPoolExecutor,
   431→    indexes: list[int],
   432→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
   433→    progress_fn,
   434→    error_log_fn,
   435→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   436→    max_workers: int,
   437→    failures: set[int],
   438→    progress_failures: set[int],
   439→    started_at: dict[int, float],
   440→    lock: threading.Lock,
   441→    clock_fn,
   442→) -> dict:
   443→    futures: dict = {}
   444→    for idx in indexes:
   445→        queue_error = _emit_progress(
   446→            progress_fn,
   447→            idx,
   448→            "queued",
   449→            None,
   450→            details={"max_workers": max_workers},
   451→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   452→        )
   453→        if queue_error is not None:
   454→            _record_progress_error(
   455→                idx=idx,
   456→                err=queue_error,
   457→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   458→                lock=lock,
   459→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   460→            )
   461→            failures.add(idx)
   462→        futures[
   463→            executor.submit(
   464→                _run_parallel_task,
   465→                idx=idx,
   466→                tasks=tasks,
   467→                progress_fn=progress_fn,
   468→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   469→                contract_cache=contract_cache,
   470→                max_workers=max_workers,
   471→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   472→                started_at=started_at,
   473→                lock=lock,
   474→                clock_fn=clock_fn,
   475→            )
   476→        ] = idx
   477→    return futures
   478→
   479→
   480→def _complete_parallel_future(
   481→    *,
   482→    future,
   483→    futures: dict,
   484→    progress_fn,
   485→    error_log_fn,
   486→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   487→    failures: set[int],
   488→    progress_failures: set[int],
   489→    started_at: dict[int, float],
   490→    lock: threading.Lock,
   491→    clock_fn,
   492→) -> None:
   493→    idx = futures[future]
   494→    with lock:
   495→        t0 = started_at.get(idx, float(clock_fn()))
   496→    elapsed = int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - t0))
   497→    try:
   498→        code = future.result()
   499→    except _RUNNER_TASK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   500→        _record_execution_error(
   501→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   502→            failures=failures,
   503→            idx=idx,
   504→            exc=exc,
   505→        )
   506→        done_error = _emit_progress(
   507→            progress_fn,
   508→            idx,
   509→            "done",
   510→            1,
   511→            details={"elapsed_seconds": elapsed},
   512→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   513→        )
   514→        if done_error is not None:
   515→            _record_progress_error(
   516→                idx=idx,
   517→                err=done_error,
   518→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   519→                lock=lock,
   520→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   521→            )
   522→        return
   523→
   524→    done_error = _emit_progress(
   525→        progress_fn,
   526→        idx,
   527→        "done",
   528→        code,
   529→        details={"elapsed_seconds": elapsed},
   530→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
   531→    )
   532→    if done_error is not None:
   533→        _record_progress_error(
   534→            idx=idx,
   535→            err=done_error,
   536→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   537→            lock=lock,
   538→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   539→        )
   540→    with lock:
   541→        had_progress_failure = idx in progress_failures
   542→    if code != 0 or had_progress_failure:
   543→        failures.add(idx)
   544→
   545→
   546→def _drain_parallel_completions(
   547→    *,
   548→    pending: set,
   549→    futures: dict,
   550→    heartbeat: float | None,
   551→    indexes: list[int],
   552→    progress_fn,
   553→    error_log_fn,
   554→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   555→    failures: set[int],
   556→    progress_failures: set[int],
   557→    started_at: dict[int, float],
   558→    lock: threading.Lock,
   559→    clock_fn,
   560→) -> None:
   561→    if heartbeat is None:
   562→        for future in as_completed(pending):
   563→            _complete_parallel_future(
   564→                future=future,
   565→                futures=futures,
   566→                progress_fn=progress_fn,
   567→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   568→                contract_cache=contract_cache,
   569→                failures=failures,
   570→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   571→                started_at=started_at,
   572→                lock=lock,
   573→                clock_fn=clock_fn,
   574→            )
   575→        return
   576→
   577→    while pending:
   578→        try:
   579→            future = next(as_completed(pending, timeout=heartbeat))
   580→        except FuturesTimeoutError:
   581→            _heartbeat(
   582→                pending,
   583→                futures,
   584→                started_at,
   585→                lock,
   586→                indexes,
   587→                progress_fn,
   588→                clock_fn,
   589→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   590→                contract_cache=contract_cache,
   591→            )
   592→            continue
   593→        pending.discard(future)
   594→        _complete_parallel_future(
   595→            future=future,
   596→            futures=futures,
   597→            progress_fn=progress_fn,
   598→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   599→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   600→            failures=failures,
   601→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   602→            started_at=started_at,
   603→            lock=lock,
   604→            clock_fn=clock_fn,
   605→        )
   606→
   607→
   608→def _heartbeat(
   609→    pending,
   610→    futures,
   611→    started_at,
   612→    lock,
   613→    indexes,
   614→    progress_fn,
   615→    clock_fn,
   616→    *,
   617→    error_log_fn=None,
   618→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] | None = None,
   619→):
   620→    """Build and emit a heartbeat with active/queued batch status."""
   621→    with lock:
   622→        active = sorted(futures[f] for f in pending if futures[f] in started_at)
   623→    active_set = set(active)
   624→    queued = sorted(futures[f] for f in pending if futures[f] not in active_set)
   625→    elapsed = {
   626→        idx: int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - started_at.get(idx, clock_fn())))
   627→        for idx in active
   628→    }
   629→    heartbeat_error = _emit_progress(
   630→        progress_fn,
   631→        -1,
   632→        "heartbeat",
   633→        None,
   634→        details={
   635→            "active_batches": active,
   636→            "queued_batches": queued,
   637→            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   638→            "active_count": len(active),
   639→            "queued_count": len(queued),
   640→            "total_count": len(indexes),
   641→        },
   642→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
   643→    )
   644→    if heartbeat_error is not None and callable(error_log_fn):
   645→        try:
   646→            error_log_fn(-1, heartbeat_error)
   647→        except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   648→            log_best_effort_failure(
   649→                logger,
   650→                "record batch heartbeat failure via callback",
   651→                exc,
   652→            )
   653→
   654→
   655→__all__ = [
   656→    "BatchExecutionOptions",
   657→    "BatchProgressEvent",
   658→    "execute_batches",
   659→]
   660→

    41→    for issue in matches:
    42→        by_file[issue["file"]].append(issue)
    43→    return sorted(by_file.items(), key=lambda item: -len(item[1]))
    44→
    45→
    46→def _print_single_issue(issue: dict, *, show_code: bool) -> None:
    47→    """Render a single issue to terminal."""
    48→    normalized_status = canonical_issue_status(issue.get("status"))
    49→    status_icon = {
    50→        "open": "○",
    51→        "fixed": "✓",
    52→        "wontfix": "—",
    53→        "false_positive": "✗",
    54→        "auto_resolved": "◌",
    55→    }.get(normalized_status, "?")
    56→    zone = issue.get("zone", "production")
    57→    zone_tag = colorize(f" [{zone}]", "dim") if zone != "production" else ""
    58→    print(
    59→        f"    {status_icon} T{issue['tier']} [{issue['confidence']}] {issue['summary']}{zone_tag}"
    60→    )
    61→
    62→    detail_parts = format_detail(issue.get("detail", {}))
    63→    if detail_parts:
    64→        print(colorize(f"      {' · '.join(detail_parts)}", "dim"))
    65→    if show_code:
    66→        detail = issue.get("detail", {})
    67→        target_line = (
    68→            detail.get("line") or (detail.get("lines", [None]) or [None])[0]
    69→        )
    70→        if target_line and issue["file"] not in (".", ""):
    71→            snippet = read_code_snippet(issue["file"], target_line)
    72→            if snippet:
    73→                print(snippet)
    74→    if issue.get("reopen_count", 0) >= 2:
    75→        print(
    76→            colorize(
    77→                f"      ⟳ reopened {issue['reopen_count']} times — fix properly or wontfix",
    78→                "red",
    79→            )
    80→        )
    81→    if issue.get("note"):
    82→        print(colorize(f"      note: {issue['note']}", "dim"))
    83→    print(colorize(f"      {issue['id']}", "dim"))
    84→
    85→
    86→def render_issues(
    87→    matches: list[dict],
    88→    *,
    89→    pattern: str,
    90→    status_filter: str,
    91→    show_code: bool,
    92→    top: int,
    93→    hidden_by_detector: dict[str, int],
    94→    hidden_total: int,
    95→    noise_budget: int,
    96→    global_noise_budget: int,
    97→    budget_warning: str | None,
    98→) -> None:
    99→    """Render grouped issues and rollup summary to terminal."""
   100→    sorted_files = group_matches_by_file(matches)
   101→    print(
   102→        colorize(
   103→            f"\n  {len(matches)} {status_filter} issues matching '{pattern}'\n",
   104→            "bold",
   105→        )
   106→    )
   107→    if budget_warning:
   108→        print(colorize(f"  {budget_warning}\n", "yellow"))
   109→    if hidden_total:
   110→        global_label = (
   111→            f", {global_noise_budget} global" if global_noise_budget > 0 else ""
   112→        )
   113→        hidden_parts = ", ".join(
   114→            f"{det}: +{count}" for det, count in hidden_by_detector.items()
   115→        )
   116→        print(
   117→            colorize(
   118→                (
   119→                    "  Noise budget: "
   120→                    f"{noise_budget}/detector{global_label} "
   121→                    f"({hidden_total} hidden: {hidden_parts})\n"
   122→                ),
   123→                "dim",
   124→            )
   125→        )
   126→
   127→    shown_files = sorted_files[:top]
   128→    remaining_files = sorted_files[top:]
   129→    remaining_issues = sum(len(files) for _, files in remaining_files)
   130→
   131→    for filepath, issues in shown_files:
   132→        issues.sort(
   133→            key=lambda issue: (
   134→                issue["tier"],
   135→                CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(issue["confidence"], 9),
   136→            )
   137→        )
   138→        display_path = "Codebase-wide" if filepath == "." else filepath
   139→        print(
   140→            colorize(f"  {display_path}", "cyan")
   141→            + colorize(f"  ({len(issues)} issues)", "dim")
   142→        )
   143→
   144→        for issue in issues:
   145→            _print_single_issue(issue, show_code=show_code)
   146→        print()
   147→
   148→    if remaining_issues:
   149→        print(
   150→            colorize(
   151→                (
   152→                    f"  ... and {len(remaining_files)} more files "
   153→                    f"({remaining_issues} issues). "
   154→                    f"Use --top {top + 20} to see more.\n"
   155→                ),
   156→                "dim",
   157→            )
   158→        )
   159→
   160→    by_detector: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   161→    by_tier: dict[int, int] = defaultdict(int)
   162→    for issue in matches:
   163→        by_detector[issue["detector"]] += 1
   164→        by_tier[issue["tier"]] += 1
   165→
   166→    print(colorize("  Summary:", "bold"))
   167→    print(
   168→        colorize(
   169→            (
   170→                "    By tier:     "
   171→                + ", ".join(
   172→                    f"T{tier}:{count}" for tier, count in sorted(by_tier.items())
   173→                )
   174→            ),
   175→            "dim",
   176→        )
   177→    )
   178→    print(
   179→        colorize(
   180→            (
   181→                "    By detector: "
   182→                + ", ".join(
   183→                    f"{detector}:{count}"
   184→                    for detector, count in sorted(
   185→                        by_detector.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1]
   186→                    )
   187→                )
   188→            ),
   189→            "dim",
   190→        )
   191→    )
   192→    if hidden_total:
   193→        print(
   194→            colorize(
   195→                (
   196→                    "    Hidden:      "
   197→                    + ", ".join(
   198→                        f"{detector}:+{count}"
   199→                        for detector, count in hidden_by_detector.items()
   200→                    )
   201→                ),
   202→                "dim",
   203→            )
   204→        )
   205→    print()
   206→
   207→
   208→def show_agent_plan(
   209→    narrative: dict, matches: list[dict], *, plan: dict | None = None
   210→) -> None:
   211→    """Render a compact plan from current issues and narrative actions.
   212→
   213→    When a living *plan* is active, renders plan focus/progress instead.
   214→    """
   215→    if plan and (plan.get("queue_order") or plan.get("clusters")):
   216→        render_plan_with_living_plan(
   217→            [],
   218→            plan=plan,
   219→            header="  AGENT PLAN (use `desloppify next` to see your next task):",
   220→        )
   221→        return
   222→
   223→    actions = narrative.get("actions", [])
   224→    if not actions and not matches:
   225→        return
   226→
   227→    print(
   228→        colorize(
   229→            "  AGENT PLAN (use `desloppify next --count 20` to inspect more items):",
   230→            "yellow",
   231→        )
   232→    )
   233→    if actions:
   234→        top = actions[0]
   235→        print(
   236→            colorize(
   237→                f"  Agent focus: `{top['command']}` — {top['description']}",
   238→                "cyan",
   239→            )
   240→        )
   241→    elif matches:
   242→        first = matches[0]
   243→        print(
   244→            colorize(
   245→                "  Agent focus: `desloppify next --count 20` — "
   246→                f"inspect and resolve `{first.get('id', '')}`",
   247→                "cyan",
   248→            )
   249→        )
   250→
   251→    if print_ranked_actions(actions):
   252→        print()
   253→
   254→
   255→def show_subjective_followup(
   256→    state: dict, target_strict_score: float, *, objective_backlog: int = 0,
   257→) -> None:
   258→    """Show subjective follow-up guidance for the current state."""
   259→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {}) or {}
   260→    if not dim_scores:
   261→        return
   262→
   263→    subjective = reporting_dimensions_mod.scorecard_subjective_entries(
   264→        state,
   265→        dim_scores=dim_scores,
   266→    )
   267→    if not subjective:
   268→        return
   269→
   270→    followup = reporting_dimensions_mod.build_subjective_followup(
   271→        state,
   272→        subjective,
   273→        threshold=target_strict_score,
   274→        max_quality_items=3,
   275→        max_integrity_items=5,
   276→    )
   277→    if print_subjective_followup(followup, objective_backlog=objective_backlog):
   278→        print()
   279→
   280→
   281→__all__ = [
   282→    "group_matches_by_file",
   283→    "render_issues",
   284→    "show_agent_plan",
   285→    "show_subjective_followup",
   286→    "write_show_output_file",
   287→]

1→"""Queue-order enforcement helpers for resolve command flows."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→
     7→from desloppify.core.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS
     8→from desloppify.core.output_api import colorize
     9→from desloppify.engine.plan import has_living_plan, load_plan
    10→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.plan_order import collapse_clusters
    11→from desloppify.engine.work_queue import QueueBuildOptions, build_work_queue, queue_context
    12→
    13→_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    14→
    15→
    16→def _check_queue_order_guard(
    17→    state: dict,
    18→    patterns: list[str],
    19→    status: str,
    20→) -> bool:
    21→    """Warn and block if resolving items not at the front of the plan queue."""
    22→    if status != "fixed":
    23→        return False
    24→    try:
    25→        if not has_living_plan():
    26→            return False
    27→        plan = load_plan()
    28→        queue_order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    29→        if not queue_order:
    30→            return False
    31→
    32→        ctx = queue_context(state, plan=plan)
    33→        result = build_work_queue(
    34→            state,
    35→            options=QueueBuildOptions(
    36→                count=None,
    37→                include_subjective=True,
    38→                context=ctx,
    39→            ),
    40→        )
    41→        items = result["items"]
    42→        if not plan.get("active_cluster"):
    43→            items = collapse_clusters(items, plan)
    44→        if not items:
    45→            return False
    46→
    47→        front_item = items[0]
    48→        front_id = front_item["id"]
    49→
    50→        front_ids: set[str] = set()
    51→        if front_item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    52→            for member in front_item.get("members", []):
    53→                front_ids.add(member["id"])
    54→            front_ids.add(front_id)
    55→        else:
    56→            front_ids.add(front_id)
    57→
    58→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    59→        resolved_ids: set[str] = set()
    60→        for pattern in patterns:
    61→            if pattern in clusters:
    62→                resolved_ids.update(clusters[pattern].get("issue_ids", []))
    63→                resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    64→            else:
    65→                resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    66→
    67→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
    68→        resolved_ids = {
    69→            issue_id
    70→            for issue_id in resolved_ids
    71→            if issue_id in clusters
    72→            or (issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open")
    73→        }
    74→        if not resolved_ids:
    75→            return False
    76→
    77→        out_of_order = resolved_ids - front_ids
    78→        for cluster_id in list(out_of_order):
    79→            if cluster_id in clusters:
    80→                alive_members = {
    81→                    issue_id
    82→                    for issue_id in clusters[cluster_id].get("issue_ids", [])
    83→                    if issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open"
    84→                }
    85→                if alive_members and alive_members <= front_ids:
    86→                    out_of_order.discard(cluster_id)
    87→        if not out_of_order:
    88→            return False
    89→
    90→        print(colorize("\n  Queue order violation: these items are not next in the plan queue:\n", "yellow"))
    91→        for issue_id in sorted(out_of_order):
    92→            print(f"    {issue_id}")
    93→        print(colorize(f"\n  The current next item is: {front_id}", "dim"))
    94→        print(colorize("  Items must be resolved in plan order. If you need to reprioritize:", "dim"))
    95→        print(colorize("    desloppify plan reorder <pattern> top            # move to front", "dim"))
    96→        print(colorize("    desloppify plan skip <pattern> --reason '...'    # skip for now", "dim"))
    97→        print(colorize("    desloppify next                                  # see what's next\n", "dim"))
    98→        return True
    99→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   100→        _logger.debug("queue order guard skipped", exc_info=True)
   101→        return False
   102→
   103→
   104→__all__ = ["_check_queue_order_guard"]
   105→

    52→def cmd_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    53→    """Resolve issue(s) matching one or more patterns."""
    54→    attestation = getattr(args, "attest", None)
    55→    _validate_resolve_inputs(args, attestation)
    56→
    57→    if args.status == "fixed":
    58→        note = getattr(args, "note", None)
    59→        if not validate_note_length(note):
    60→            show_note_length_requirement(note)
    61→            return
    62→
    63→    state_file = state_path(args)
    64→    state = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
    65→
    66→    if _check_queue_order_guard(state, args.patterns, args.status):
    67→        return
    68→
    69→    if args.status == "fixed":
    70→        require_triage_current_or_exit(
    71→            state=state,
    72→            bypass=bool(getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)),
    73→            attest=getattr(args, "attest", "") or "",
    74→        )
    75→
    76→    _enforce_batch_wontfix_confirmation(
    77→        state,
    78→        args,
    79→        attestation=attestation,
    80→        resolve_all_patterns_fn=_resolve_all_patterns,
    81→    )
    82→    prev = _previous_score_snapshot(state)
    83→    prev_subjective_scores = {
    84→        str(dim): (coerce_assessment_score(payload) or 0.0)
    85→        for dim, payload in (state.get("subjective_assessments") or {}).items()
    86→        if isinstance(dim, str)
    87→    }
    88→
    89→    all_resolved = _resolve_all_patterns(state, args, attestation=attestation)
    90→    if not all_resolved:
    91→        status_label = "resolved" if args.status == "open" else "open"
    92→        print(colorize(f"No {status_label} issues matching: {' '.join(args.patterns)}", "yellow"))
    93→        return
    94→
    95→    _save_state_or_exit(state, state_file)
    96→
    97→    plan = None
    98→    try:
    99→        if has_living_plan():
   100→            plan = load_plan()
   101→            purged = purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)
   102→            append_log_entry(
   103→                plan,
   104→                "resolve",
   105→                issue_ids=all_resolved,
   106→                actor="user",
   107→                note=getattr(args, "note", None),
   108→                detail={"status": args.status, "attestation": attestation},
   109→            )
   110→            # Commit tracking: add to uncommitted on fix, remove on reopen
   111→            if args.status == "fixed":
   112→                add_uncommitted_issues(plan, all_resolved)
   113→            elif args.status == "open":
   114→                purge_uncommitted_ids(plan, all_resolved)
   115→            if purged:
   116→                save_plan(plan)
   117→                print(colorize(f"  Plan updated: {purged} item(s) removed from queue.", "dim"))
   118→            else:
   119→                save_plan(plan)
   120→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   121→        _logger.debug("plan update failed after resolve", exc_info=True)
   122→        print(colorize("  Warning: could not update living plan.", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
   123→
   124→    _print_resolve_summary(status=args.status, all_resolved=all_resolved)
   125→    _print_wontfix_batch_warning(
   126→        state,
   127→        status=args.status,
   128→        resolved_count=len(all_resolved),
   129→    )
   130→    show_score_with_plan_context(state, prev)
   131→    render_commit_guidance(state, plan, all_resolved, args.status)
   132→    _print_subjective_reset_hint(

   135→        all_resolved=all_resolved,
   136→        prev_subjective_scores=prev_subjective_scores,
   137→    )
   138→
   139→    lang = resolve_lang(args)

   141→    narrative = narrative_mod.compute_narrative(

   145→    if narrative.get("milestone"):

   147→

    40→def _render_dimension_legend(
    41→    scorecard_subjective: list[dict],
    42→    state: dict | None = None,
    43→    *,
    44→    objective_backlog: int = 0,
    45→) -> None:
    46→    """Print the legend footer and, when actionable, the stale rerun command."""
    47→    print(
    48→        colorize("  Health = open penalized | Strict = open + wontfix penalized", "dim")
    49→    )
    50→    print(
    51→        colorize(
    52→            "  Action: fix=auto-fixer | move=reorganize | refactor=manual rewrite | manual=review & fix",
    53→            "dim",
    54→        )
    55→    )
    56→    stale_keys = [
    57→        str(e.get("dimension_key"))
    58→        for e in scorecard_subjective
    59→        if e.get("stale") and e.get("dimension_key")
    60→    ]
    61→    if stale_keys:
    62→        print(
    63→            colorize("  [stale] = assessment outdated", "yellow")
    64→        )
    65→        if objective_backlog <= 0:
    66→            n = len(stale_keys)
    67→            dims_arg = ",".join(stale_keys)
    68→            print(
    69→                colorize(
    70→                    f"  {n} stale dimension{'s' if n != 1 else ''}"
    71→                    f": `desloppify review --prepare --dimensions {dims_arg} --force-review-rerun`",
    72→                    "yellow",
    73→                )
    74→            )

    96→    _render_subjective_dimensions(

   106→def show_focus_suggestion(
   107→    dim_scores: dict, state: dict, *, plan: dict | None = None
   108→) -> None:
   109→    """Show the lowest-scoring dimension as the focus area."""
   110→    # When plan has an active focus cluster, show that instead
   111→    if plan and plan.get("active_cluster"):
   112→        cluster_name = plan["active_cluster"]
   113→        cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name, {})
   114→        remaining = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   115→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   116→        desc_str = f" — {desc}" if desc else ""
   117→        print(
   118→            colorize(
   119→                f"  Focus: {cluster_name} ({remaining} items remaining){desc_str}",
   120→                "cyan",
   121→            )
   122→        )
   123→        print()
   124→        return
   125→
   126→    scorecard_subjective = _scorecard_subjective_entries(state, dim_scores)
   127→    lowest_name = _find_lowest_dimension(dim_scores, scorecard_subjective)
   128→    if not lowest_name:
   129→        return
   130→
   131→    # Determine kind, score, and issue count from the resolved name
   132→    lowest_kind = None
   133→    lowest_score = 101.0
   134→    lowest_issues = 0
   135→    for dim in DIMENSIONS:
   136→        if dim.name == lowest_name:
   137→            ds = dim_scores.get(dim.name)
   138→            if ds:
   139→                lowest_score = float(ds.get("strict", ds["score"]))
   140→                lowest_kind = "mechanical"
   141→                lowest_issues = int(ds.get("failing", 0))
   142→            break
   143→    else:
   144→        for entry in scorecard_subjective:
   145→            if entry.get("name") == lowest_name:
   146→                lowest_score = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))
   147→                lowest_kind = "subjective"
   148→                lowest_issues = 0
   149→                break
   150→
   151→    if lowest_name and lowest_score < 100:
   152→        if lowest_kind == "subjective":
   153→            print(
   154→                colorize(
   155→                    f"  Focus: {lowest_name} ({lowest_score:.1f}%) — re-review to improve",
   156→                    "cyan",
   157→                )
   158→            )
   159→            print()
   160→            return
   161→
   162→        potentials = merge_potentials(state.get("potentials", {}))
   163→        target_dim = next((d for d in DIMENSIONS if d.name == lowest_name), None)
   164→        if target_dim:
   165→            impact = 0.0
   166→            for det in target_dim.detectors:
   167→                impact = compute_score_impact(
   168→                    {
   169→                        k: {
   170→                            "score": v["score"],
   171→                            "tier": v.get("tier", 3),
   172→                            "detectors": v.get("detectors", {}),
   173→                        }
   174→                        for k, v in dim_scores.items()
   175→                        if "score" in v
   176→                    },
   177→                    potentials,
   178→                    det,
   179→                    lowest_issues,
   180→                )
   181→                if impact > 0:
   182→                    break
   183→
   184→            impact_str = f" for +{impact:.1f} pts" if impact > 0 else ""
   185→            print(
   186→                colorize(
   187→                    f"  Focus: {lowest_name} ({lowest_score:.1f}%) — "
   188→                    f"fix {lowest_issues} items{impact_str}",
   189→                    "cyan",
   190→                )
   191→            )
   192→            print()
   193→
   194→

    97→                "stale": stale,
    98→                "dimension_key": dim_key,
    99→                "not_scanned": not_scanned,
   100→                "carried_forward": carried_forward,
   101→                "cli_keys": cli_keys,
   102→            }
   103→        )
   104→    return entries
   105→
   106→
   107→def show_scorecard_subjective_measures(state: dict) -> None:
   108→    """Show canonical scorecard dimensions only (mechanical + subjective)."""
   109→    entries = scorecard_dimension_entries(state)
   110→    if not entries:
   111→        return
   112→
   113→    print(colorize("  Scorecard dimensions (matches scorecard.png):", "dim"))
   114→    for entry in entries:
   115→        if entry.get("not_scanned"):
   116→            print(
   117→                "  "
   118→                + f"{entry['name']:<18} "
   119→                + colorize("─── skipped ───────────────────  (run without --skip-slow)", "yellow")
   120→            )
   121→            continue
   122→        bar = _dimension_bar(entry["score"])
   123→        suffix = ""
   124→        if entry.get("carried_forward"):
   125→            suffix = colorize("  ⟲ prior scan", "dim")
   126→        elif entry.get("placeholder"):
   127→            suffix = colorize("  [unassessed]", "yellow")
   128→        elif entry.get("stale"):
   129→            suffix = colorize("  [stale — re-review]", "yellow")
   130→        print(
   131→            "  "
   132→            + f"{entry['name']:<18} {bar} {entry['score']:5.1f}%  "
   133→            + colorize(f"(strict {entry['strict']:5.1f}%)", "dim")
   134→            + suffix
   135→        )
   136→    stale_keys = [e["dimension_key"] for e in entries if e.get("stale")]
   137→    has_open = any(
   138→        f.get("status") == "open" and not f.get("suppressed")
   139→        for f in (state.get("issues") or {}).values()
   140→    )
   141→    if stale_keys and not has_open:
   142→        n = len(stale_keys)
   143→        dims_arg = ",".join(stale_keys)
   144→        print(
   145→            colorize(
   146→                f"  {n} stale subjective dimension{'s' if n != 1 else ''}"
   147→                f" — run `desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import --dimensions {dims_arg}` to re-review",
   148→                "yellow",
   149→            )
   150→        )
   151→    print()
   152→
   153→
   154→def show_score_model_breakdown(state: dict, *, dim_scores: dict | None = None) -> None:
   155→    """Show score recipe and weighted drags so users can see what drives the north star."""
   156→    return presentation_mod.show_score_model_breakdown(
   157→        state,
   158→        scoring_mod=scoring_mod,
   159→        colorize_fn=colorize,

   166→    return presentation_mod.show_dimension_deltas(
   167→        prev,
   168→        current,

   170→        colorize_fn=colorize,

   177→        dim_scores,
   178→        scoring_mod=scoring_mod,
   179→        colorize_fn=colorize,

     6→

     8→def _abs(filepath: str) -> str:
     9→    """Resolve filepath to absolute using resolve_path."""
    10→    return resolve_path(filepath)
    11→
    12→
    13→def _read_file_contents(files: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    14→    file_contents: dict[str, str] = {}
    15→    for filepath in files:

    17→        if content is not None:
    18→            file_contents[filepath] = content
    19→    return file_contents

    21→def _cmd_commit_log_status(plan: dict) -> None:
    22→    """Show full commit-log status: uncommitted, committed, git context."""
    23→    from desloppify.core.git_context import detect_git_context
    24→
    25→    git = detect_git_context()
    26→    summary = commit_tracking_summary(plan)
    27→
    28→    print(colorize("  Commit Tracking Status", "bold"))
    29→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 40, "dim"))
    30→
    31→    if git.available:
    32→        print(f"  Branch:  {git.branch or '(detached)'}")
    33→        print(f"  HEAD:    {git.head_sha or '?'}")
    34→        if git.has_uncommitted:
    35→            print(colorize("  Working tree has uncommitted changes", "yellow"))
    36→    else:
    37→        print(colorize("  Git: not available", "dim"))
    38→
    39→    from desloppify.core.config import load_config
    40→
    41→    config = load_config()
    42→    pr = config.get("commit_pr", 0)
    43→    if pr:
    44→        print(f"  PR:      #{pr}")
    45→
    46→    uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)
    47→    print(f"\n  Uncommitted:  {summary['uncommitted']} issue(s)")
    48→    for fid in uncommitted[:10]:
    49→        print(f"    {fid}")
    50→    if len(uncommitted) > 10:
    51→        print(f"    ... and {len(uncommitted) - 10} more")
    52→
    53→    commit_log = plan.get("commit_log", [])
    54→    committed_count = sum(len(r.get("issue_ids", [])) for r in commit_log)
    55→    print(f"  Committed:    {committed_count} issue(s) in {len(commit_log)} commit(s)")
    56→
    57→    if not uncommitted and not commit_log:
    58→        print(colorize("\n  No commit tracking data yet.", "dim"))
    59→        print(colorize("  Resolve issues with `desloppify resolve` or `desloppify plan resolve` to start.", "dim"))

    62→def _cmd_commit_log_record(args: argparse.Namespace, plan: dict) -> None:
    63→    """Record a commit: capture HEAD, move uncommitted → committed, update PR."""
    64→    from desloppify.core.git_context import detect_git_context, update_pr_body
    65→
    66→    sha = getattr(args, "sha", None)
    67→    branch = getattr(args, "branch", None)
    68→    note = getattr(args, "note", None)
    69→    only_patterns: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "only", None)
    70→
    71→    # Auto-detect from git if not overridden
    72→    if not sha or not branch:
    73→        git = detect_git_context()
    74→        if git.available:
    75→            sha = sha or git.head_sha
    76→            branch = branch or git.branch
    77→        elif not sha:
    78→            print(colorize("  Cannot detect HEAD. Use --sha to specify.", "red"))
    79→            return

    81→    # Determine which issues to record
    82→    uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)

   188→def cmd_commit_log_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   189→    """Route commit-log subcommands."""
   190→    from desloppify.core.config import load_config
   191→
   192→    config = load_config()
   193→    if not config.get("commit_tracking_enabled", True):

     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import logging

     8→from desloppify import state as state_mod
     9→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.query import write_query_best_effort as _write_query_best_effort
    10→from desloppify.core.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS
    11→from desloppify.core.output_contract import OutputResult
    12→from desloppify.engine.plan import has_living_plan, load_plan
    13→
    14→from .selection import ResolveQueryContext

    16→_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    18→
    19→def _try_expand_cluster(pattern: str) -> list[str] | None:
    20→    """If pattern matches a cluster name, return its issue IDs."""
    21→    try:
    22→        if not has_living_plan():
    23→            return None
    24→        plan = load_plan()
    25→        cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(pattern)
    26→        if cluster and cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    27→            return list(cluster["issue_ids"])
    28→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    29→        _logger.debug("cluster expansion skipped for %r", pattern, exc_info=True)
    30→    return None
    31→
    32→
    33→def _resolve_all_patterns(
    34→    state: dict,
    35→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    36→    *,
    37→    attestation: str | None,
    38→) -> list[str]:
    39→    all_resolved: list[str] = []
    40→    for pattern in args.patterns:
    41→        # Check if pattern is a cluster name — expand to member IDs
    42→        cluster_ids = _try_expand_cluster(pattern)
    43→        if cluster_ids:
    44→            for fid in cluster_ids:
    45→                resolved = state_mod.resolve_issues(
    46→                    state,
    47→                    fid,
    48→                    args.status,
    49→                    args.note,
    50→                    attestation=attestation,
    51→                )
    52→                all_resolved.extend(resolved)
    53→            continue
    54→
    55→        resolved = state_mod.resolve_issues(
    56→            state,
    57→            pattern,
    58→            args.status,
    59→            args.note,
    60→            attestation=attestation,
    61→        )
    62→        all_resolved.extend(resolved)
    63→    return all_resolved
    64→
    65→
    66→def write_query(payload: dict) -> OutputResult:
    67→    """Backward-compatible resolve query writer seam."""
    68→    return _write_query_best_effort(
    69→        payload,
    70→        context="resolve query payload update",
    71→    )
    72→
    73→
    74→def _write_resolve_query_entry(context: ResolveQueryContext) -> None:
    75→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(context.state)
    76→    write_query(
    77→        {
    78→            "command": "resolve",
    79→            "patterns": context.patterns,
    80→            "status": context.status,
    81→            "resolved": context.resolved,
    82→            "count": len(context.resolved),
    83→            "next_command": context.next_command,

    92→            "attestation": context.attestation,
    93→            "narrative": context.narrative,
    94→        }
    95→    )

    55→def _merge_batch_results(batch_results: list[object]) -> dict[str, object]:
    56→    """Deterministically merge assessments/issues across batch outputs."""
    57→    normalized_results: list[dict] = []
    58→    for result in batch_results:
    59→        if hasattr(result, "to_dict") and callable(result.to_dict):
    60→            payload = result.to_dict()
    61→            if isinstance(payload, dict):
    62→                normalized_results.append(payload)
    63→                continue
    64→        if isinstance(result, dict):
    65→            normalized_results.append(result)
    66→    return batch_core_mod.merge_batch_results(
    67→        normalized_results,

    69→        abstraction_component_names=ABSTRACTION_COMPONENT_NAMES,

   264→
   265→def _validate_run_dir(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, Path, str]:
   266→    """Validate run directory, load summary, and return (summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path).
   267→
   268→    Raises CommandError on any validation failure.
   269→    """
   270→    if not run_dir.is_dir():
   271→        raise CommandError(f"run directory not found: {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   272→
   273→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   274→    if not summary_path.exists():
   275→        raise CommandError(f"no run_summary.json in {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   276→    try:
   277→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   278→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   279→        raise CommandError(f"Error reading run summary: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   280→
   281→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   282→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   283→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   284→
   285→    if not successful:
   286→        raise CommandError("no successful batches in run summary.", exit_code=1)
   287→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   288→        raise CommandError(f"blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", exit_code=1)
   289→
   290→    try:
   291→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   292→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   293→        raise CommandError(f"Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   294→
   295→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   296→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path
   297→
   298→
   299→def do_import_run(
   300→    run_dir_path: str,
   301→    state: dict,
   302→    lang,
   303→    state_file: str,
   304→    *,
   305→    config: dict | None = None,
   306→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   307→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   308→    scan_path: str = ".",
   309→) -> None:
   310→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   311→
   312→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   313→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   314→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   315→    """
   316→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   317→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   318→
   319→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   320→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   321→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   322→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   323→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   324→
   325→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   326→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   327→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in successful]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   328→    output_files = {
   329→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   330→        for idx in selected_indexes
   331→    }
   332→
   333→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   334→    if missing:
   335→        raise CommandError(f"missing result files for batches: {missing}", exit_code=1)
   336→
   337→    batch_results, failures = runner_helpers_mod.collect_batch_results(
   338→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   339→        failures=[],
   340→        output_files=output_files,
   341→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   342→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: batch_core_mod.extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   343→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: batch_core_mod.normalize_batch_result(
   344→            payload,
   345→            dims,
   346→            max_batch_issues=max_batch_issues_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   347→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   348→        ),
   349→    )
   350→
   351→    if not batch_results:
   352→        raise CommandError("no valid batch results could be parsed.", exit_code=1)
   353→
   354→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   355→    if failures:
   356→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   357→
   358→    # -- merge --
   359→    merged = _merge_batch_results(batch_results)
   360→
   361→    # -- build provenance --
   362→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   363→    merged["provenance"] = runner_helpers_mod.build_batch_import_provenance(
   364→        runner=runner,
   365→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   366→        run_stamp=stamp,
   367→        batch_indexes=successful_indexes,
   368→    )
   369→
   370→    # -- write merged output --
   371→    merged_path = run_dir / "holistic_issues_merged.json"
   372→    safe_write_text(merged_path, json.dumps(merged, indent=2) + "\n")
   373→    print(colorize(f"  Merged output: {merged_path}", "bold"))
   374→
   375→    # -- import with trusted source --
   376→    _do_import(
   377→        str(merged_path),
   378→        state,
   379→        lang,
   380→        state_file,
   381→        config=config,
   382→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   383→        trusted_assessment_source=True,
   384→        trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   385→    )
   386→
   387→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   388→    if scan_after_import:
   389→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   390→        if lang_name:
   391→            runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   392→                lang_name=lang_name,
   393→                scan_path=scan_path,
   394→                deps=runner_helpers_mod.FollowupScanDeps(
   395→                    project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   396→                    timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   397→                    python_executable=sys.executable,
   398→                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   399→                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   400→                    colorize_fn=colorize,
   401→                ),
   402→            )
   403→

1→"""Stage-gate and coverage helpers for triage command handlers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.core.output import colorize
     6→from desloppify.engine.plan import TRIAGE_ID
     7→
     8→
     9→def _require_triage_pending(plan: dict, *, action: str) -> bool:
    10→    """Require ``triage::pending`` to be present in queue for an action."""
    11→    if TRIAGE_ID in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    12→        return True
    13→    print(colorize(f"  triage::pending is not in the queue — nothing to {action}.", "yellow"))
    14→    return False
    15→
    16→
    17→def _validate_stage_report(
    18→    report: str | None,
    19→    *,
    20→    stage: str,
    21→    min_chars: int,
    22→    missing_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    23→    short_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    24→) -> str | None:
    25→    """Validate staged report presence/length and print consistent guidance."""
    26→    if not report:
    27→        print(colorize(f"  --report is required for --stage {stage}.", "red"))
    28→        for line in missing_guidance or []:
    29→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    30→        return None
    31→    cleaned = report.strip()
    32→    if len(cleaned) < min_chars:
    33→        print(
    34→            colorize(
    35→                f"  Report too short: {len(cleaned)} chars (minimum {min_chars}).",
    36→                "red",
    37→            )
    38→        )
    39→        for line in short_guidance or []:
    40→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    41→        return None
    42→    return cleaned
    43→
    44→
    45→def _triage_coverage(plan: dict) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    46→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for triage progress."""
    47→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    48→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
    49→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    50→        all_cluster_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    51→    queue_ids = [issue_id for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", []) if issue_id != TRIAGE_ID]
    52→    organized = sum(1 for issue_id in queue_ids if issue_id in all_cluster_ids)
    53→    return organized, len(queue_ids), clusters
    54→
    55→
    56→def _unenriched_clusters(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    57→    """Return clusters with issues that are missing required enrichment."""
    58→    gaps: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    59→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
    60→        if not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    61→            continue
    62→        if cluster.get("auto"):
    63→            continue
    64→        missing: list[str] = []
    65→        if not cluster.get("description"):
    66→            missing.append("description")
    67→        if not cluster.get("action_steps"):
    68→            missing.append("action_steps")
    69→        if missing:
    70→            gaps.append((name, missing))
    71→    return gaps
    72→
    73→
    74→def _manual_clusters_with_issues(plan: dict) -> list[str]:
    75→    """Return names of non-auto clusters that have issues."""
    76→    return [
    77→        name
    78→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
    79→        if cluster.get("issue_ids") and not cluster.get("auto")
    80→    ]
    81→

1→"""State-path and scan-gating helpers for command modules."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.lang import auto_detect_lang_name
     8→from desloppify.core.text_api import PROJECT_ROOT
     9→from desloppify.core.output_api import colorize
    10→
    11→
    12→def _sole_existing_lang_state_file() -> Path | None:
    13→    """Return the only existing language-specific state file, if unambiguous."""
    14→    state_dir = PROJECT_ROOT / ".desloppify"
    15→    if not state_dir.exists():
    16→        return None
    17→    candidates = sorted(path for path in state_dir.glob("state-*.json") if path.is_file())
    18→    if len(candidates) == 1:
    19→        return candidates[0]
    20→    return None
    21→
    22→
    23→def _allow_lang_state_fallback(args) -> bool:
    24→    """Whether command can safely fallback to the sole existing lang state file."""
    25→    # Scan should always honor detected/explicit language mapping to avoid cross-lang merges.
    26→    return getattr(args, "command", None) != "scan"
    27→
    28→
    29→def state_path(args) -> Path | None:
    30→    """Get state file path from args, or None for default."""
    31→    path_arg = getattr(args, "state", None)
    32→    if path_arg:
    33→        return Path(path_arg)
    34→    lang_name = getattr(args, "lang", None)
    35→    if not lang_name:
    36→        lang_name = auto_detect_lang_name(args)
    37→    if lang_name:
    38→        resolved = PROJECT_ROOT / ".desloppify" / f"state-{lang_name}.json"
    39→        if resolved.exists() or not _allow_lang_state_fallback(args):
    40→            return resolved
    41→        fallback = _sole_existing_lang_state_file()
    42→        if fallback is not None:
    43→            return fallback
    44→        return resolved
    45→
    46→    if _allow_lang_state_fallback(args):
    47→        fallback = _sole_existing_lang_state_file()
    48→        if fallback is not None:
    49→            return fallback
    50→    return None
    51→
    52→
    53→def require_completed_scan(state: dict) -> bool:
    54→    """Return True when the state contains at least one completed scan."""
    55→    has_completed_scan = bool(state.get("last_scan"))
    56→    if not has_completed_scan:
    57→        print(colorize("No scans yet. Run: desloppify scan", "yellow"))
    58→    return has_completed_scan
    59→

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging
     7→import shutil
     8→import sys
     9→from pathlib import Path
    10→from typing import cast
    11→
    12→__all__ = [

    16→
    17→from desloppify.core.text_api import is_numeric

    19→    CURRENT_VERSION,
    20→    STATE_FILE,
    21→    StateModel,
    22→    empty_state,
    23→    ensure_state_defaults,
    24→    json_default,
    25→    validate_state_invariants,
    26→)

    28→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import safe_write_text
    29→
    30→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    31→
    32→
    33→def _load_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
    34→    data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    35→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    36→        raise ValueError("state file root must be a JSON object")
    37→    return data
    38→
    39→
    40→def _normalize_loaded_state(data: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    41→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    42→        raise ValueError("state file root must be a JSON object")
    43→    ensure_state_defaults(data)
    44→    normalized = cast(StateModel, data)
    45→    validate_state_invariants(normalized)
    46→    return normalized
    47→
    48→
    49→def load_state(path: Path | None = None) -> StateModel:
    50→    """Load state from disk, or return empty state on missing/corruption."""
    51→    state_path = path or STATE_FILE
    52→    if not state_path.exists():
    53→        return empty_state()
    54→
    55→    try:
    56→        data = _load_json(state_path)
    57→    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError, ValueError) as ex:
    58→        backup = state_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
    59→        if backup.exists():
    60→            try:
    61→                backup_data = _load_json(backup)
    62→                print(
    63→                    f"  ⚠ State file corrupted ({ex}), loaded from backup.",
    64→                    file=sys.stderr,
    65→                )
    66→                return _normalize_loaded_state(backup_data)
    67→            except (
    68→                json.JSONDecodeError,
    69→                UnicodeDecodeError,
    70→                OSError,
    71→                ValueError,
    72→                TypeError,
    73→                AttributeError,
    74→            ) as backup_ex:
    75→                logger.debug("Backup state load failed from %s: %s", backup, backup_ex)
    76→
    77→        print(f"  ⚠ State file corrupted ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    78→        rename_failed = False
    79→        try:
    80→            state_path.rename(state_path.with_suffix(".json.corrupted"))
    81→        except OSError as rename_ex:
    82→            rename_failed = True
    83→            logger.debug(
    84→                "Failed to rename corrupted state file %s: %s", state_path, rename_ex
    85→            )
    86→        if rename_failed:
    87→            logger.debug(
    88→                "Corrupted state file retained at original path: %s", state_path
    89→            )
    90→        return empty_state()
    91→
    92→    version = data.get("version", 1)
    93→    if version > CURRENT_VERSION:
    94→        print(
    95→            "  ⚠ State file version "
    96→            f"{version} is newer than supported ({CURRENT_VERSION}). "
    97→            "Some features may not work correctly.",
    98→            file=sys.stderr,
    99→        )
   100→
   101→    try:
   102→        return _normalize_loaded_state(data)
   103→    except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as normalize_ex:
   104→        print(
   105→            f"  ⚠ State invariants invalid ({normalize_ex}). Starting fresh.",
   106→            file=sys.stderr,
   107→        )
   108→        return empty_state()
   109→
   110→
   111→def _coerce_integrity_target(value: object) -> float | None:
   112→    if not is_numeric(value):
   113→        return None
   114→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value)))
   115→
   116→
   117→def _resolve_integrity_target(
   118→    state: StateModel,
   119→    explicit_target: float | None,
   120→) -> float | None:
   121→    target = _coerce_integrity_target(explicit_target)
   122→    if target is not None:
   123→        return target
   124→
   125→    integrity = state.get("subjective_integrity")
   126→    if not isinstance(integrity, dict):
   127→        return None
   128→    return _coerce_integrity_target(integrity.get("target_score"))
   129→
   130→
   131→def save_state(
   132→    state: StateModel,
   133→    path: Path | None = None,
   134→    *,
   135→    subjective_integrity_target: float | None = None,
   136→) -> None:
   137→    """Recompute stats/score and save to disk atomically."""
   138→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   139→    _recompute_stats(
   140→        state,
   141→        scan_path=state.get("scan_path"),
   142→        subjective_integrity_target=_resolve_integrity_target(
   143→            state,
   144→            subjective_integrity_target,
   145→        ),
   146→    )
   147→    validate_state_invariants(state)
   148→
   149→    state_path = path or STATE_FILE
   150→    state_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   151→
   152→    content = json.dumps(state, indent=2, default=json_default) + "\n"
   153→
   154→    if state_path.exists():
   155→        backup = state_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
   156→        try:
   157→            shutil.copy2(str(state_path), str(backup))
   158→        except OSError as backup_ex:
   159→            logger.debug(
   160→                "Failed to create state backup %s: %s",
   161→                state_path.with_suffix(".json.bak"),
   162→                backup_ex,
   163→            )
   164→
   165→    try:
   166→        safe_write_text(state_path, content)
   167→    except OSError as ex:
   168→        print(f"  Warning: Could not save state: {ex}", file=sys.stderr)
   169→        raise
   170→

1→"""Registry for optional language hook modules consumed by detectors."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import importlib
     6→import logging
     7→import sys
     8→from collections import defaultdict
     9→
    10→_LANG_HOOKS: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = defaultdict(dict)
    11→_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    12→
    13→
    14→def register_lang_hooks(
    15→    lang_name: str,
    16→    *,
    17→    test_coverage: object | None = None,
    18→) -> None:
    19→    """Register optional detector hook modules for a language."""
    20→    hooks = _LANG_HOOKS[lang_name]
    21→    if test_coverage is not None:
    22→        hooks["test_coverage"] = test_coverage
    23→
    24→
    25→def get_lang_hook(lang_name: str | None, hook_name: str) -> object | None:
    26→    """Get a previously-registered language hook module."""
    27→    if not lang_name:
    28→        return None
    29→
    30→    hook = _LANG_HOOKS.get(lang_name, {}).get(hook_name)
    31→    if hook is not None:
    32→        return hook
    33→
    34→    module_name = f"desloppify.languages.{lang_name}"
    35→    module = sys.modules.get(module_name)
    36→
    37→    # Lazy-load only the requested language package.
    38→    if module is None:
    39→        try:
    40→            importlib.import_module(module_name)
    41→        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError, OSError) as exc:
    42→            _LOGGER.debug(
    43→                "Unable to import language hook package %s: %s", lang_name, exc
    44→            )
    45→            return None
    46→    elif lang_name not in _LANG_HOOKS:
    47→        try:
    48→            importlib.reload(module)
    49→        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError, OSError) as exc:
    50→            _LOGGER.debug(
    51→                "Unable to reload language hook package %s: %s", lang_name, exc
    52→            )
    53→            return None

    12→def add_uncommitted_issues(plan: dict[str, Any], issue_ids: list[str]) -> int:
    13→    """Add issue IDs to the uncommitted list (deduplicates).  Returns count added."""
    14→    uncommitted: list[str] = plan.setdefault("uncommitted_issues", [])
    15→    existing = set(uncommitted)
    16→    added = 0
    17→    for fid in issue_ids:
    18→        if fid not in existing:
    19→            uncommitted.append(fid)
    20→            existing.add(fid)
    21→            added += 1
    22→    return added
    23→
    24→
    25→def purge_uncommitted_ids(plan: dict[str, Any], issue_ids: list[str]) -> int:
    26→    """Remove issue IDs from the uncommitted list.  Returns count removed."""
    27→    to_remove = set(issue_ids)
    28→    uncommitted: list[str] = plan.get("uncommitted_issues", [])
    29→    original = len(uncommitted)
    30→    plan["uncommitted_issues"] = [fid for fid in uncommitted if fid not in to_remove]
    31→    return original - len(plan["uncommitted_issues"])

    40→    plan: dict[str, Any],
    41→    sha: str,

    43→    issue_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    44→    note: str | None = None,
    45→    cluster_name: str | None = None,
    46→) -> CommitRecord:
    47→    """Move uncommitted issues into a new CommitRecord.
    48→
    49→    If *issue_ids* is None, all uncommitted issues are recorded.
    50→    """
    51→    uncommitted = plan.get("uncommitted_issues", [])
    52→    if issue_ids is None:
    53→        ids_to_record = list(uncommitted)
    54→    else:
    55→        ids_to_record = list(issue_ids)
    56→
    57→    record: CommitRecord = {
    58→        "sha": sha,
    59→        "branch": branch,
    60→        "issue_ids": ids_to_record,
    61→        "recorded_at": utc_now(),
    62→        "note": note,
    63→        "cluster_name": cluster_name,
    64→    }
    65→
    66→    commit_log: list[CommitRecord] = plan.setdefault("commit_log", [])
    67→    commit_log.append(record)
    68→
    69→    # Remove recorded IDs from uncommitted
    70→    recorded_set = set(ids_to_record)
    71→    plan["uncommitted_issues"] = [fid for fid in uncommitted if fid not in recorded_set]
    72→
    73→    return record

   100→    summary = issue.get("summary", "")

   106→def _score_delta_line(plan: dict[str, Any], state: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
   107→    """Build a score delta summary line from plan_start_scores to current."""
   108→    start = plan.get("plan_start_scores", {})
   109→    current_dim = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   110→    if not start or not current_dim:
   111→        return ""
   112→
   113→    start_strict = start.get("strict")
   114→    if start_strict is None:
   115→        return ""
   116→
   117→    # Compute current strict from dimension_scores
   118→    try:
   119→        from desloppify.engine._scoring.results.core import compute_aggregate_scores
   120→        scores = compute_aggregate_scores(current_dim)
   121→        current_strict = scores.get("strict", 0)
   122→    except (ImportError, TypeError, ValueError, KeyError):
   123→        return ""
   124→
   125→    delta = current_strict - start_strict
   126→    sign = "+" if delta >= 0 else ""
   127→    return f"Score: {start_strict:.1f} → {current_strict:.1f} strict ({sign}{delta:.1f})"
   128→
   129→
   130→def generate_pr_body(plan: dict[str, Any], state: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
   131→    """Generate the PR description markdown from commit_log."""
   132→    lines: list[str] = ["## Code Health Improvements", ""]
   133→
   134→    commit_log: list[dict] = plan.get("commit_log", [])
   135→    if commit_log:
   136→        lines.append("### Commits")
   137→        lines.append("")
   138→        total_issues = 0
   139→        for record in commit_log:
   140→            sha = record.get("sha", "?")[:7]
   141→            note = record.get("note") or ""
   142→            issue_ids = record.get("issue_ids", [])
   143→            total_issues += len(issue_ids)
   144→
   145→            header = f"**{sha}**"
   146→            if note:
   147→                header += f" — {note}"
   148→            lines.append(header)
   149→
   150→            for fid in issue_ids:
   151→                summary = _issue_summary(state, fid)
   152→                if summary and summary != fid:
   153→                    lines.append(f"- `{fid}` — {summary}")
   154→                else:
   155→                    lines.append(f"- `{fid}`")
   156→            lines.append("")
   157→
   158→        lines.append("### Summary")
   159→        commit_count = len(commit_log)
   160→        lines.append(
   161→            f"{total_issues} issue{'s' if total_issues != 1 else ''} "
   162→            f"resolved across {commit_count} commit{'s' if commit_count != 1 else ''}"
   163→        )
   164→        score_line = _score_delta_line(plan, state)
   165→        if score_line:
   166→            lines.append(score_line)
   167→    else:
   168→        lines.append("*No commits recorded yet.*")
   169→
   170→    return "\n".join(lines)
   171→
   172→
   173→def suggest_commit_message(
   174→    plan: dict[str, Any],
   175→    template: str,
   176→) -> str:
   177→    """Generate a suggested commit message from uncommitted issues."""
   178→    uncommitted = plan.get("uncommitted_issues", [])
   179→    if not uncommitted:
   180→        return ""
   181→
   182→    # Extract common detector/category
   183→    detectors: set[str] = set()
   184→    dirs: set[str] = set()
   185→    for fid in uncommitted:
   186→        parts = fid.split("::")
   187→        if parts:
   188→            detectors.add(parts[0])
   189→        if len(parts) >= 2:
   190→            file_part = parts[1]
   191→            slash_idx = file_part.rfind("/")
   192→            if slash_idx > 0:
   193→                dirs.add(file_part[:slash_idx + 1])
   194→
   195→    summary_parts: list[str] = []
   196→    if len(detectors) == 1:
   197→        summary_parts.append(f"{next(iter(detectors))}")
   198→    else:
   199→        summary_parts.append(f"{len(detectors)} detector{'s' if len(detectors) != 1 else ''}")
   200→    if len(dirs) == 1:
   201→        summary_parts.append(f"in {next(iter(dirs))}")
   202→
   203→    summary = " ".join(summary_parts)
   204→
   205→    return template.format(
   206→        status="autofix",
   207→        count=len(uncommitted),
   208→        summary=summary,
   209→    )
   210→
   211→
   212→def filter_issue_ids_by_pattern(issue_ids: list[str], patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   213→    """Filter issue IDs by glob patterns (used for --only)."""
   214→    result: list[str] = []
   215→    for fid in issue_ids:
   216→        for pattern in patterns:
   217→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(fid, pattern):
   218→                result.append(fid)
   219→                break
   220→    return result
   221→
   222→
