   338→_CLUSTER_INDIVIDUAL_THRESHOLD = 10
   339→
   340→
   341→def _check_cluster_guard(patterns: list[str], plan: dict, state: dict) -> bool:
   342→    """Return True if blocked by cluster guard, False if OK to proceed."""
   343→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   344→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   345→    for pattern in patterns:
   346→        if pattern in clusters:
   347→            cluster = clusters[pattern]
   348→            # Filter to alive issues only — stale IDs should not count
   349→            ids = [
   350→                fid for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   351→                if fid in issues and issues[fid].get("status") == "open"
   352→            ]
   353→            if len(ids) == 0:
   354→                print(colorize(
   355→                    f"\n  Cluster '{pattern}' is empty — add items before marking it done.\n",
   356→                    "yellow",
   357→                ))
   358→                print(colorize(
   359→                    f"  Use: desloppify plan cluster add {pattern} <issue-id>",
   360→                    "dim",
   361→                ))
   362→                return True  # blocked
   363→            if len(ids) <= _CLUSTER_INDIVIDUAL_THRESHOLD:
   364→                _print_cluster_guard(pattern, ids, state)
   365→                return True  # blocked
   366→    return False  # OK
   367→
   368→
   369→def _print_cluster_guard(cluster_name: str, issue_ids: list[str], state: dict) -> None:
   370→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   371→    print(colorize(
   372→        f"\n  Cluster '{cluster_name}' has {len(issue_ids)} item(s) — mark them done individually first:\n",
   373→        "yellow",
   374→    ))
   375→    for fid in issue_ids:
   376→        f = issues.get(fid, {})
   377→        summary = f.get("summary", "(no summary)")[:80]
   378→        detector = f.get("detector", "?")
   379→        print(f"    {fid}  [{detector}]  {summary}")
   380→    print(colorize(
   381→        f"\n  Use: desloppify resolve <id> --status fixed --note '...' --attest '...'",
   382→        "dim",
   383→    ))
   384→    print(colorize(
   385→        f"  Or mark each resolved: desloppify plan resolve <id> --note '...' --confirm\n",
   386→        "dim",
   387→    ))
   388→
   389→
   390→def _is_synthetic_id(fid: str) -> bool:
   391→    """Return True if the ID is a synthetic workflow/triage item, not a real issue."""
   392→    return fid.startswith("triage::") or fid.startswith("workflow::") or fid.startswith("subjective::")
   393→
   394→
   395→def _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
   396→    """Separate synthetic IDs from real issue patterns.
   397→
   398→    Returns (synthetic_ids, remaining_patterns).
   399→    """
   400→    synthetic = [p for p in patterns if _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   401→    remaining = [p for p in patterns if not _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   402→    return synthetic, remaining
   403→
   404→
   405→def _blocked_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   406→    """Return ``{stage_id: [blocked_by_ids]}`` for triage stages that can't run yet.
   407→
   408→    Uses the dependency graph and confirmed-stage metadata directly —
   409→    no state needed, no queue item construction.
   410→    """
   411→    from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage_playbook import TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES
   412→    from desloppify.engine.plan import TRIAGE_IDS, TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS
   413→
   414→    order_set = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   415→    present = order_set & TRIAGE_IDS
   416→    if not present:
   417→        return {}
   418→
   419→    confirmed = set(plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   420→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit")
   421→
   422→    blocked: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   423→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names):
   424→        if sid not in present or name in confirmed:
   425→            continue
   426→        deps = TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.get(name, set())
   427→        unmet = sorted(
   428→            f"triage::{dep}" for dep in deps
   429→            if f"triage::{dep}" in present and dep not in confirmed
   430→        )
   431→        if unmet:
   432→            blocked[sid] = unmet
   433→    return blocked
   434→
   435→
   436→def cmd_plan_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   437→    """Mark issues as fixed — delegates to cmd_resolve for rich UX."""
   438→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   439→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   440→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   441→
   442→    # --confirm: auto-generate attestation from --note
   443→    if getattr(args, "confirm", False):
   444→        if not note:
   445→            print(colorize("  --confirm requires --note to describe what you did.", "red"))
   446→            return
   447→        attestation = f"I have actually {note} and I am not gaming the score."
   448→        args.attest = attestation
   449→
   450→    # Handle synthetic IDs (triage::*, workflow::*, subjective::*) directly
   451→    synthetic_ids, real_patterns = _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns)
   452→    if synthetic_ids:
   453→        plan = load_plan()
   454→        # Validate triage dependency chain
   455→        blocked_map = _blocked_triage_stages(plan)
   456→        for sid in synthetic_ids:
   457→            if sid in blocked_map:
   458→                deps = ", ".join(b.replace("triage::", "") for b in blocked_map[sid])
   459→                print(colorize(f"  Cannot resolve {sid} — blocked by: {deps}", "red"))
   460→                print(colorize("  Complete those stages first, or use --force-resolve to override.", "dim"))
   461→                if not getattr(args, "force_resolve", False):
   462→                    return
   463→        purge_ids(plan, synthetic_ids)
   464→        append_log_entry(
   465→            plan, "done", issue_ids=synthetic_ids, actor="user", note=note,
   466→        )
   467→        save_plan(plan)
   468→        for sid in synthetic_ids:
   469→            print(colorize(f"  Resolved: {sid}", "green"))
   470→        if not real_patterns:
   471→            return
   472→        # Continue with remaining real patterns
   473→        patterns = real_patterns
   474→        args.patterns = patterns
   475→
   476→    # Validate note length
   477→    if not validate_note_length(note):
   478→        show_note_length_requirement(note)
   479→        return
   480→
   481→    # Pre-validate attestation before delegating (avoids stale hint in resolve)
   482→    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
   483→        show_attestation_requirement("Plan resolve", attestation, ATTEST_EXAMPLE)
   484→        return
   485→
   486→    # Cluster completion guard: block bulk-completing small clusters
   487→    try:
   488→        runtime = command_runtime(args)
   489→        state = runtime.state
   490→        plan = load_plan()
   491→        if _check_cluster_guard(patterns, plan, state):
   492→            return
   493→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   494→        plan = None
   495→
   496→    # Log the done action (best-effort)
   497→    try:
   498→        if plan is None:
   499→            plan = load_plan()
   500→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   501→        cluster_name = None
   502→        for p in patterns:
   503→            if p in clusters:
   504→                cluster_name = p
   505→                break
   506→        append_log_entry(
   507→            plan,
   508→            "done",
   509→            issue_ids=patterns,
   510→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   511→            actor="user",
   512→            note=note,
   513→        )
   514→        save_plan(plan)
   515→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   516→        print(colorize(f"  Note: unable to append plan resolve log entry ({exc}).", "dim"))
   517→
   518→    # Deferred import: cmd_resolve has a heavy import chain that isn't needed
   519→    # for synthetic-ID handling above.
   520→    from desloppify.app.commands.resolve.cmd import cmd_resolve
   521→
   522→    # Build a Namespace that cmd_resolve expects
   523→    resolve_args = argparse.Namespace(
   524→        status="fixed",
   525→        patterns=patterns,
   526→        note=note,
   527→        attest=attestation,
   528→        confirm_batch_wontfix=False,
   529→        force_resolve=bool(getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)),
   530→        state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   531→        lang=getattr(args, "lang", None),
   532→        path=getattr(args, "path", None),
   533→        exclude=getattr(args, "exclude", None),
   534→    )
   535→
   536→    cmd_resolve(resolve_args)
   537→

   539→def cmd_plan_focus(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   540→    """Set or clear the active cluster focus."""
   541→    clear_flag = getattr(args, "clear", False)
   542→    cluster_name: str | None = getattr(args, "cluster_name", None)
   543→
   544→    plan = load_plan()
   545→    if clear_flag:
   546→        prev = plan.get("active_cluster")
   547→        clear_focus(plan)
   548→        append_log_entry(

1→"""Scan preflight guard: warn and gate scan when queue has unfinished items."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→
     7→_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
     8→
     9→from desloppify import state as state_mod
    10→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.queue_progress import plan_aware_queue_breakdown
    11→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.state import state_path
    12→from desloppify.core.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS, CommandError
    13→from desloppify.core.output_api import colorize
    14→from desloppify.engine.plan import load_plan, save_plan
    15→
    16→
    17→def scan_queue_preflight(args) -> None:
    18→    """Warn and gate scan when queue has unfinished items."""
    19→    # CI profile always passes
    20→    if getattr(args, "profile", None) == "ci":
    21→        return
    22→
    23→    # --force-rescan with valid attestation bypasses
    24→    if getattr(args, "force_rescan", False):
    25→        attest = getattr(args, "attest", None) or ""
    26→        if "i understand" not in attest.lower():
    27→            raise CommandError(
    28→                '--force-rescan requires --attest "I understand this is not '
    29→                "the intended workflow and I am intentionally skipping queue "
    30→                'completion"'
    31→            )
    32→        print(
    33→            colorize(
    34→                "  --force-rescan: bypassing queue completion check. "
    35→                "Plan-start score will be reset.",
    36→                "yellow",
    37→            )
    38→        )
    39→        # Clear plan_start_scores
    40→        try:
    41→            plan = load_plan()
    42→            if plan.get("plan_start_scores"):
    43→                plan["plan_start_scores"] = {}
    44→                save_plan(plan)
    45→        except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
    46→            logging.debug("Plan score cleanup skipped: %s", exc)
    47→        return
    48→
    49→    # No plan = no gate (first scan, or user never uses plan)
    50→    try:
    51→        plan = load_plan()
    52→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    53→        _logger.debug("scan preflight plan load skipped", exc_info=True)
    54→        return
    55→    if not plan.get("plan_start_scores"):
    56→        return  # No active cycle
    57→
    58→    # Count plan-aware remaining items, excluding workflow actions (e.g.
    59→    # "run scan") which would otherwise create a circular gate.
    60→    try:
    61→        state = state_mod.load_state(state_path(args))
    62→        breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan)
    63→        remaining = breakdown.actionable
    64→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    65→        _logger.debug("scan preflight queue breakdown skipped", exc_info=True)
    66→        return
    67→    if remaining <= 0:
    68→        return  # Queue clear, scan allowed
    69→
    70→    # GATE
    71→    raise CommandError(
    72→        f"{remaining} item{'s' if remaining != 1 else ''}"
    73→        " remaining in your queue.\n"
    74→        "  The intended workflow is to complete the queue before scanning.\n"
    75→        "  Work through items with `desloppify next`, then scan when clear.\n\n"
    76→        "  To force a rescan (resets your plan-start score):\n"
    77→        '    desloppify scan --force-rescan --attest "I understand this is not '
    78→        "the intended workflow and I am intentionally skipping queue "
    79→        'completion"'
    80→    )
    81→
    82→
    83→__all__ = ["scan_queue_preflight"]
    84→

    14→def resolve_project_name(project_root: Path) -> str:
    15→    """Resolve owner/repo display name from GitHub CLI, git remote, or folder."""
    16→    try:
    17→        name = subprocess.check_output(
    18→            ["gh", "repo", "view", "--json", "nameWithOwner", "-q", ".nameWithOwner"],
    19→            cwd=str(project_root),
    20→            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    21→            text=True,
    22→            timeout=5,
    23→        ).strip()
    24→        if "/" in name:
    25→            return name
    26→    except (
    27→        subprocess.CalledProcessError,
    28→        FileNotFoundError,
    29→        subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
    30→    ) as exc:
    31→        logger.debug("gh repo view failed, falling back to git remote: %s", exc)
    32→
    33→    try:
    34→        url = subprocess.check_output(
    35→            ["git", "config", "--get", "remote.origin.url"],
    36→            cwd=str(project_root),
    37→            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    38→            text=True,
    39→            timeout=5,
    40→        ).strip()
    41→        if url.startswith("git@") and ":" in url:
    42→            path = url.split(":")[-1]
    43→        else:
    44→            path = "/".join(url.split("/")[-2:])
    45→        return path.removesuffix(".git")
    46→    except (
    47→        subprocess.CalledProcessError,
    48→        FileNotFoundError,
    49→        IndexError,
    50→        subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
    51→    ) as exc:
    52→        logger.debug("git remote lookup failed, falling back to folder name: %s", exc)
    53→        return project_root.name
    54→
    55→
    56→def resolve_package_version(
    57→    project_root: Path,
    58→    *,
    59→    version_getter: Callable[[str], str],
    60→    package_not_found_error: type[Exception],
    61→) -> str:
    62→    """Resolve package version from installed metadata or local pyproject."""
    63→    try:
    64→        return version_getter("desloppify")
    65→    except package_not_found_error as exc:
    66→        logger.debug("Package metadata lookup failed, trying pyproject.toml: %s", exc)
    67→
    68→    pyproject_path = project_root / "pyproject.toml"
    69→    try:
    70→        text = pyproject_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    71→        match = re.search(r'^\s*version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"\s*$', text, re.MULTILINE)
    72→        if match:
    73→            return match.group(1)
    74→    except OSError as exc:
    75→        logger.debug("Failed to read pyproject.toml for version: %s", exc)
    76→
    77→    return "unknown"
    78→

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging
     7→import shutil
     8→import sys
     9→from pathlib import Path

    11→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import safe_write_text
    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import (
    13→    PLAN_VERSION,
    14→    PlanModel,
    15→    empty_plan,
    16→    ensure_plan_defaults,
    17→    validate_plan,
    18→)
    19→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import STATE_DIR, json_default
    20→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import utc_now
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    24→PLAN_FILE = STATE_DIR / "plan.json"
    25→
    26→
    27→def load_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> PlanModel:
    28→    """Load plan from disk, or return empty plan on missing/corruption."""
    29→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
    30→    if not plan_path.exists():
    31→        return empty_plan()
    32→
    33→    try:
    34→        data = json.loads(plan_path.read_text())
    35→    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as ex:
    36→        # Try backup before giving up
    37→        backup = plan_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
    38→        if backup.exists():
    39→            try:
    40→                data = json.loads(backup.read_text())
    41→                logger.warning("Plan file corrupted (%s), loaded from backup.", ex)
    42→                print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}), loaded from backup.", file=sys.stderr)
    43→                # Fall through to validation below
    44→            except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as backup_ex:
    45→                logger.warning("Plan file and backup both corrupted: %s / %s", ex, backup_ex)
    46→                print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    47→                return empty_plan()
    48→        else:
    49→            logger.warning("Plan file corrupted (%s). Starting fresh.", ex)
    50→            print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    51→            return empty_plan()
    52→
    53→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    54→        logger.warning("Plan file root is not a JSON object. Starting fresh.")
    55→        print("  Warning: Plan file root must be a JSON object. Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    56→        return empty_plan()
    57→
    58→    version = data.get("version", 1)
    59→    if version > PLAN_VERSION:
    60→        logger.warning("Plan file version %d > supported %d.", version, PLAN_VERSION)
    61→        print(
    62→            f"  Warning: Plan file version {version} is newer than supported "
    63→            f"({PLAN_VERSION}). Some features may not work correctly.",
    64→            file=sys.stderr,
    65→        )
    66→
    67→    ensure_plan_defaults(data)
    68→    try:
    69→        validate_plan(data)
    70→    except ValueError as ex:
    71→        logger.warning("Plan invariants invalid (%s). Starting fresh.", ex)
    72→        print(f"  Warning: Plan invariants invalid ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    73→        return empty_plan()
    74→
    75→    return data  # type: ignore[return-value]
    76→
    77→
    78→def save_plan(plan: PlanModel | dict, path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    79→    """Validate and save plan to disk atomically."""
    80→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    81→    plan["updated"] = utc_now()
    82→    validate_plan(plan)
    83→
    84→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
    85→    plan_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    86→
    87→    content = json.dumps(plan, indent=2, default=json_default) + "\n"
    88→
    89→    if plan_path.exists():
    90→        backup = plan_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
    91→        try:
    92→            shutil.copy2(str(plan_path), str(backup))
    93→        except OSError as backup_ex:
    94→            logger.debug("Failed to create plan backup: %s", backup_ex)
    95→
    96→    try:
    97→        safe_write_text(plan_path, content)
    98→    except OSError as ex:
    99→        print(f"  Warning: Could not save plan: {ex}", file=sys.stderr)
   100→        raise
   101→
   102→
   103→def plan_path_for_state(state_path: Path) -> Path:
   104→    """Derive plan.json path from a state file path."""
   105→    return state_path.parent / "plan.json"
   106→
   107→
   108→def has_living_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> bool:
   109→    """Return True if a plan.json exists and has user intent."""
   110→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
   111→    if not plan_path.exists():
   112→        return False
   113→    plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   114→    return bool(
   115→        plan.get("queue_order")
   116→        or plan.get("overrides")
   117→        or plan.get("clusters")
   118→    )
   119→
   120→

   123→    "has_living_plan",
   124→    "load_plan",
   125→    "plan_path_for_state",
   126→    "save_plan",
   127→]

    25→def architecture_context(lang, file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
    26→    arch: dict = {}
    27→    if not lang.dep_graph:
    28→        return arch
    29→
    30→    importer_counts = {}
    31→    for filepath, entry in lang.dep_graph.items():
    32→        entry_importer_count = importer_count(entry)
    33→        if entry_importer_count > 0:
    34→            importer_counts[rel(filepath)] = entry_importer_count
    35→    top_imported = sorted(importer_counts.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])[:10]
    36→    arch["god_modules"] = [
    37→        {"file": filepath, "importers": count, "excerpt": file_excerpt(filepath) or ""}
    38→        for filepath, count in top_imported
    39→        if count >= 5
    40→    ]
    41→    arch["top_imported"] = dict(top_imported)
    42→    return arch
    43→
    44→
    45→def coupling_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
    46→    coupling: dict = {}
    47→    module_level_io = []
    48→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    49→        for idx, raw_line in enumerate(content.splitlines()[:50]):
    50→            stripped = raw_line.strip()
    51→            if stripped.startswith(
    52→                ("def ", "class ", "async def ", "if ", "#", "@", "import ", "from ")
    53→            ):
    54→                continue
    55→            if re.search(
    56→                r"\b(?:open|connect|requests?\.|urllib|subprocess|os\.system)\b",

    62→                        "line": idx + 1,
    63→                        "code": stripped[:100],
    64→                    }
    65→                )
    66→    if module_level_io:
    67→        coupling["module_level_io"] = module_level_io[:20]
    68→    return coupling

    70→
    71→def naming_conventions_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
    72→    dir_styles: dict[str, Counter] = {}
    73→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    74→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
    75→        if len(parts) < 2:
    76→            continue
    77→        dir_name = parts[-2] + "/"
    78→        counter = dir_styles.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
    79→        for name in _FUNC_NAME_RE.findall(content):
    80→            if "_" in name and name.islower():
    81→                counter["snake_case"] += 1
    82→            elif name[0].islower() and any(ch.isupper() for ch in name):
    83→                counter["camelCase"] += 1
    84→            elif name[0].isupper():
    85→                counter["PascalCase"] += 1
    86→    return {
    87→        name: dict(counter.most_common(3))
    88→        for name, counter in dir_styles.items()
    89→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 3
    90→    }
    91→
    92→
    93→def sibling_behavior_context(
    94→    file_contents: dict[str, str],
    95→    *,
    96→    base_path: Path | str | None = None,
    97→) -> dict:
    98→    root = Path(base_path).resolve() if base_path is not None else None
    99→    boilerplate_names = frozenset({"__init__.py", "conftest.py", "setup.py", "__main__.py"})
   100→
   101→    def _bucket_for(filepath: str) -> str | None:
   102→        if Path(filepath).name in boilerplate_names:
   103→            return None
   104→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   105→        if root is not None:
   106→            try:
   107→                parts = target.relative_to(root).parts
   108→                if len(parts) >= 2:
   109→                    return "/".join(parts[:-1]) + "/"
   110→                return None
   111→            except ValueError:
   112→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using fallback bucket", filepath, root)
   113→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
   114→        if len(parts) < 2:
   115→            return None
   116→        return f"{parts[-2]}/"
   117→
   118→    def _display_path(filepath: str) -> str:
   119→        target = Path(filepath).resolve()
   120→        if root is not None:
   121→            try:
   122→                return target.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   123→            except ValueError:
   124→                logger.debug("Path %s not relative to root %s, using rel() fallback", filepath, root)
   125→        return rel(filepath)
   126→
   127→    dir_imports: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {}
   128→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   129→        dir_name = _bucket_for(filepath)
   130→        if dir_name is None:
   131→            continue
   132→        file_rel = _display_path(filepath)
   133→        dir_imports.setdefault(dir_name, {})[file_rel] = _extract_imported_names(content)
   134→
   135→    sibling_behavior: dict = {}
   136→    for dir_name, file_names_map in dir_imports.items():
   137→        total = len(file_names_map)
   138→        if total < 3:
   139→            continue
   140→        name_counts: Counter = Counter()
   141→        for names in file_names_map.values():
   142→            for name in names:
   143→                name_counts[name] += 1
   144→        threshold = total * 0.6
   145→        shared = {name: count for name, count in name_counts.items() if count >= threshold}
   146→        if not shared:
   147→            continue
   148→        outliers = []
   149→        for file_rel, names in file_names_map.items():
   150→            missing = [name for name in shared if name not in names]
   151→            if missing:
   152→                outliers.append({"file": file_rel, "missing": sorted(missing)})
   153→        if not outliers:
   154→            continue
   155→        sibling_behavior[dir_name] = {
   156→            "shared_patterns": {
   157→                name: {"count": count, "total": total}
   158→                for name, count in sorted(shared.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
   159→            },
   160→            "outliers": sorted(outliers, key=lambda item: len(item["missing"]), reverse=True),
   161→        }
   162→    return sibling_behavior
   163→
   164→
   165→def error_strategy_context(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   166→    dir_errors: dict[str, Counter] = {}
   167→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
   168→        parts = Path(filepath).parts
   169→        if len(parts) < 2:
   170→            continue
   171→        dir_name = parts[-2] + "/"
   172→        counter = dir_errors.setdefault(dir_name, Counter())
   173→        for pattern_name, pattern in _ERROR_PATTERNS.items():
   174→            matches = pattern.findall(content)
   175→            if matches:
   176→                counter[pattern_name] += len(matches)
   177→    return {
   178→        name: dict(counter.most_common(5))
   179→        for name, counter in dir_errors.items()
   180→        if sum(counter.values()) >= 2
   181→    }

   183→
   184→def in_allowed_files(filepath: object, allowed_files: set[str] | None) -> bool:
   185→    if allowed_files is None:
   186→        return True
   187→    return isinstance(filepath, str) and filepath in allowed_files

   190→def dependencies_context(
   191→    state: dict,
   192→    *,
   193→    allowed_files: set[str] | None = None,
   194→) -> dict:
   195→    cycle_issues = []
   196→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   197→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
   198→        issues = {}
   199→    for issue in issues.values():
   200→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   201→            continue
   202→        if issue.get("detector") != "cycles" or issue.get("status") != "open":
   203→            continue
   204→        if not in_allowed_files(issue.get("file", ""), allowed_files):
   205→            continue
   206→        cycle_issues.append(issue)
   207→    if not cycle_issues:
   208→        return {}
   209→    return {
   210→        "existing_cycles": len(cycle_issues),
   211→        "cycle_summaries": [issue["summary"][:120] for issue in cycle_issues[:10]],
   212→    }
   213→
   214→
   215→def testing_context(
   216→    lang,
   217→    state: dict,
   218→    file_contents: dict[str, str],
   219→    *,
   220→    allowed_files: set[str] | None = None,
   221→) -> dict:
   222→    testing: dict = {"total_files": len(file_contents)}
   223→    if not lang.dep_graph:
   224→        return testing
   225→
   226→    tc_issues = {
   227→        issue["file"]
   228→        for issue in state.get("issues", {}).values()
   229→        if issue.get("detector") == "test_coverage"
   230→        and issue.get("status") == "open"
   231→        and in_allowed_files(issue.get("file", ""), allowed_files)
   232→    }
   233→    if not tc_issues:
   234→        return testing
   235→
   236→    critical_untested = []
   237→    for filepath in tc_issues:
   238→        entry = lang.dep_graph.get(resolve_path(filepath), {})
   239→        entry_importer_count = importer_count(entry)
   240→        if entry_importer_count >= 3:
   241→            critical_untested.append(
   242→                {"file": filepath, "importers": entry_importer_count}
   243→            )
   244→    testing["critical_untested"] = sorted(
   245→        critical_untested,
   246→        key=lambda item: -item["importers"],
   247→    )[:10]
   248→    return testing
   249→
   250→
   251→def api_surface_context(lang, file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict:
   252→    api_surface_fn = getattr(lang, "review_api_surface_fn", None)
   253→    if not callable(api_surface_fn):
   254→        return {}
   255→    computed = api_surface_fn(file_contents)
   256→    return computed if isinstance(computed, dict) else {}

   224→def prepare_review(
   225→    path: Path,
   226→    lang: object,
   227→    state: dict,
   228→    options: ReviewPrepareOptions | None = None,
   229→) -> dict[str, object]:
   230→    """Prepare review data for agent consumption. Returns structured dict.
   231→
   232→    If *files* is provided, skip file_finder (avoids redundant filesystem walks
   233→    when the caller already has the file list, e.g. from _setup_lang).
   234→    """
   235→    resolved_options = options or ReviewPrepareOptions()
   236→    resolved_options.max_files = _normalize_max_files(resolved_options.max_files)
   237→    all_files = (
   238→        resolved_options.files
   239→        if resolved_options.files is not None
   240→        else (lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else [])
   241→    )
   242→
   243→    # Enable file cache for entire prepare operation — context building,
   244→    # file selection, and content extraction all read the same files.
   245→    already_cached = is_file_cache_enabled()
   246→    if not already_cached:
   247→        enable_file_cache()
   248→    try:
   249→        context = build_review_context(path, lang, state, files=all_files)
   250→        selected = select_files_for_review(
   251→            lang,
   252→            path,
   253→            state,
   254→            options=ReviewSelectionOptions(
   255→                max_files=resolved_options.max_files,
   256→                max_age_days=resolved_options.max_age_days,
   257→                force_refresh=resolved_options.force_refresh,
   258→                files=all_files,
   259→            ),
   260→        )
   261→        file_requests = _build_file_requests(selected, lang, state)
   262→    finally:
   263→        if not already_cached:
   264→            disable_file_cache()
   265→
   266→    default_dims, dimension_prompts, system_prompt = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang.name)
   267→    dims = resolve_dimensions(
   268→        cli_dimensions=resolved_options.dimensions,
   269→        config_dimensions=resolved_options.config_dimensions,
   270→        default_dimensions=default_dims,
   271→    )
   272→    lang_guide = get_lang_guidance(lang.name)
   273→    valid_dims = set(dimension_prompts)
   274→    invalid_requested = [
   275→        dim for dim in (resolved_options.dimensions or []) if dim not in valid_dims
   276→    ]
   277→    invalid_config = [
   278→        dim
   279→        for dim in (resolved_options.config_dimensions or [])
   280→        if dim not in valid_dims
   281→    ]
   282→
   283→    return {
   284→        "command": "review",
   285→        "language": lang.name,
   286→        "dimensions": dims,
   287→        "dimension_prompts": {
   288→            d: dimension_prompts[d] for d in dims if d in dimension_prompts
   289→        },
   290→        "lang_guidance": lang_guide,
   291→        "context": serialize_context(context),
   292→        "system_prompt": system_prompt,
   293→        "files": file_requests,
   294→        "total_candidates": len(file_requests),
   295→        "cache_status": {
   296→            "fresh": count_fresh(state, resolved_options.max_age_days),
   297→            "stale": count_stale(state, resolved_options.max_age_days),
   298→            "new": len(file_requests),
   299→        },
   300→        "invalid_dimensions": {
   301→            "requested": invalid_requested,
   302→            "config": invalid_config,
   303→        },
   304→    }

   307→def _build_file_requests(files: list[str], lang, state: dict) -> list[dict]:
   308→    """Build per-file review request dicts."""
   309→    file_requests = []
   310→    for filepath in files:
   311→        content = read_file_text(abs_path(filepath))
   312→        if content is None:
   313→            continue
   314→
   315→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   316→        zone = "production"
   317→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
   318→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath).value
   319→
   320→        neighbors: dict
   321→        if lang.dep_graph:
   322→            entry = dep_graph_lookup(lang.dep_graph, filepath)
   323→            imports_raw = entry.get("imports", set())
   324→            importers_raw = entry.get("importers", set())
   325→            importer_count_value = importer_count(entry)
   326→            neighbors = {
   327→                "imports": _rel_list(imports_raw),

   489→    payload["investigation_batches"] = batches
   490→    return payload

1→"""Tree-sitter based import extraction and dep graph builder."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging

     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    10→
    11→from ._cache import _PARSE_CACHE
    12→from ._extractors import _get_parser, _make_query, _run_query, _unwrap_node
    13→

    15→    from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import TreeSitterLangSpec

    20→def ts_build_dep_graph(
    21→    path: Path,
    22→    spec: TreeSitterLangSpec,
    23→    file_list: list[str],
    24→) -> dict[str, dict]:
    25→    """Build a dependency graph by parsing imports with tree-sitter.
    26→
    27→    Returns the same shape as Python/TS dep graphs:
    28→    {file: {"imports": set[str], "importers": set[str], "import_count": int, "importer_count": int}}
    29→    """
    30→    if not spec.import_query or not spec.resolve_import:
    31→        return {}
    32→
    33→    parser, language = _get_parser(spec.grammar)
    34→    query = _make_query(language, spec.import_query)
    35→
    36→    scan_path = str(path.resolve())
    37→    file_set = set(file_list)
    38→    graph: dict[str, dict] = {}
    39→
    40→    # Initialize all files in the graph.
    41→    for f in file_list:
    42→        graph[f] = {"imports": set(), "importers": set()}
    43→
    44→    for filepath in file_list:
    45→        cached = _PARSE_CACHE.get_or_parse(filepath, parser, spec.grammar)
    46→        if cached is None:
    47→            continue
    48→        _source, tree = cached
    49→        matches = _run_query(query, tree.root_node)
    50→
    51→        for _pattern_idx, captures in matches:
    52→            path_node = _unwrap_node(captures.get("path"))
    53→            if not path_node:
    54→                continue
    55→
    56→            raw_text = path_node.text
    57→            import_text = (
    58→                raw_text.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    59→                if isinstance(raw_text, bytes)
    60→                else str(raw_text)
    61→            )
    62→
    63→            # Strip surrounding quotes if present.
    64→            import_text = import_text.strip("\"'`")
    65→
    66→            resolved = spec.resolve_import(import_text, filepath, scan_path)
    67→            if resolved is None:
    68→                continue
    69→
    70→            # Normalize to absolute path.
    71→            if not os.path.isabs(resolved):
    72→                resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(scan_path, resolved))
    73→
    74→            # Only track edges within the scanned file set.
    75→            if resolved not in file_set:
    76→                continue
    77→
    78→            graph[filepath]["imports"].add(resolved)
    79→            if resolved in graph:
    80→                graph[resolved]["importers"].add(filepath)
    81→
    82→    # Finalize: add counts.
    83→    for data in graph.values():
    84→        data["import_count"] = len(data["imports"])
    85→        data["importer_count"] = len(data["importers"])
    86→
    87→    return graph
    88→
    89→
    90→def make_ts_dep_builder(spec: TreeSitterLangSpec, file_finder):
    91→    """Create a dep graph builder bound to a TreeSitterLangSpec + file finder.
    92→
    93→    Returns a callable with signature (path: Path) -> dict,
    94→    matching the contract expected by LangConfig.build_dep_graph.
    95→    """
    96→
    97→    def build(path: Path) -> dict:
    98→        file_list = file_finder(path)
    99→        return ts_build_dep_graph(path, spec, file_list)
   100→
   101→    return build

   107→def resolve_go_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   108→    """Resolve Go imports to local files.
   109→
   110→    Go imports are module paths like "myproject/pkg/foo". We need the go.mod
   111→    module path to determine if an import is local, then map it to a file.
   112→    """
   113→    # Skip standard library and common external packages.
   114→    if not import_text or "/" not in import_text:
   115→        return None  # stdlib (e.g. "fmt", "os")
   116→
   117→    # Read go.mod to get module path.
   118→    go_mod = os.path.join(scan_path, "go.mod")
   119→    module_path = _read_go_module_path(go_mod)
   120→    if not module_path:
   121→        return None
   122→
   123→    if not import_text.startswith(module_path):
   124→        return None  # external package
   125→
   126→    # Map module-relative import to filesystem path.
   127→    rel_path = import_text[len(module_path) :].lstrip("/")
   128→    candidate_dir = os.path.join(scan_path, rel_path)
   129→
   130→    # Go imports point to packages (directories), not files.
   131→    # Return the directory — the coupling detector works with directories.
   132→    if os.path.isdir(candidate_dir):
   133→        # Find the first .go file in the package dir.
   134→        for f in sorted(os.listdir(candidate_dir)):
   135→            if f.endswith(".go") and not f.endswith("_test.go"):
   136→                return os.path.join(candidate_dir, f)
   137→    return None
   138→
   139→
   140→_GO_MODULE_CACHE: dict[str, str] = {}
   141→
   142→
   143→def _read_go_module_path(go_mod_path: str) -> str:
   144→    """Read module path from go.mod, caching the result."""
   145→    if go_mod_path in _GO_MODULE_CACHE:
   146→        return _GO_MODULE_CACHE[go_mod_path]
   147→
   148→    module_path = ""
   149→    try:
   150→        with open(go_mod_path) as f:
   151→            for line in f:
   152→                line = line.strip()
   153→                if line.startswith("module "):
   154→                    module_path = line.split(None, 1)[1].strip()
   155→                    break
   156→    except OSError as exc:
   157→        logger.debug("Failed to read go.mod at %s: %s", go_mod_path, exc)
   158→    _GO_MODULE_CACHE[go_mod_path] = module_path
   159→    return module_path

   162→def resolve_rust_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   163→    """Resolve Rust `use` declarations to local files.
   164→
   165→    Handles `crate::module::item` → src/module.rs or src/module/mod.rs.
   166→    """
   167→    if not import_text.startswith("crate::"):
   168→        return None  # external crate or std
   169→
   170→    parts = import_text[len("crate::") :].split("::")
   171→    if not parts:
   172→        return None
   173→
   174→    src_dir = os.path.join(scan_path, "src")
   175→    if not os.path.isdir(src_dir):
   176→        src_dir = scan_path
   177→
   178→    # Try file path: src/a/b.rs
   179→    path_parts = parts[:-1] if len(parts) > 1 else parts
   180→    candidate = os.path.join(src_dir, *path_parts) + ".rs"
   181→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   182→        return candidate
   183→
   184→    # Try directory path: src/a/b/mod.rs
   185→    candidate = os.path.join(src_dir, *path_parts, "mod.rs")
   186→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   187→        return candidate
   188→
   189→    # Try with all parts as path.
   190→    candidate = os.path.join(src_dir, *parts) + ".rs"
   191→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   192→        return candidate
   193→
   194→    return None

   292→def resolve_php_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   293→    """Resolve PHP use statements via PSR-4-like mapping.
   294→
   295→    Maps `App\\Models\\User` → src/Models/User.php or app/Models/User.php.
   296→    """
   297→    # Parse composer.json for autoload mapping if available.
   298→    parts = import_text.replace("\\", "/").split("/")
   299→    if len(parts) < 2:

   301→
   302→    # Try common PSR-4 roots.

   305→        for src_root in ["src", "app", "lib", "."]:

   359→def resolve_swift_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   360→    """Best-effort local Swift import resolution.
   361→
   362→    Swift imports are usually module-level and often external. Resolve only when
   363→    the import path clearly matches a local ``.swift`` file.
   364→    """
   365→    text = import_text.strip()
   366→    if not text:
   367→        return None
   368→
   369→    module_path = text.replace(".", os.sep)
   370→    leaf = module_path.split(os.sep)[-1]
   371→    source_dir = os.path.dirname(source_file)
   372→
   373→    candidates = [
   374→        os.path.join(source_dir, module_path + ".swift"),
   375→        os.path.join(scan_path, module_path + ".swift"),
   376→        os.path.join(scan_path, "Sources", module_path + ".swift"),
   377→        os.path.join(scan_path, "Sources", module_path, f"{leaf}.swift"),
   378→        os.path.join(scan_path, module_path, f"{leaf}.swift"),
   379→    ]
   380→    seen: set[str] = set()
   381→    for candidate in candidates:
   382→        if candidate in seen:
   383→            continue
   384→        seen.add(candidate)
   385→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   386→            return candidate
   387→    return None

   544→def resolve_zig_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   545→    """Resolve Zig `@import("utils.zig")` to local files.
   546→
   547→    Skips `"std"` and `"builtin"`. Resolves relative to source file.
   548→    """
   549→    if not import_text:
   550→        return None
   551→
   552→    # Strip quotes.
   553→    text = import_text.strip('"')
   554→
   555→    # Skip standard library.
   556→    if text in ("std", "builtin"):
   557→        return None
   558→
   559→    # Resolve relative to source file directory.
   560→    base = os.path.dirname(source_file)
   561→    candidate = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, text))
   562→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   563→        return candidate
   564→
   565→    # Try adding .zig extension.
   566→    if not candidate.endswith(".zig"):

   580→def resolve_haskell_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   581→    """Resolve Haskell `import MyApp.Module` to local files.
   582→
   583→    Converts dots to slashes, searches in `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`.
   584→    Skips known stdlib prefixes.
   585→    """
   586→    if not import_text:
   587→        return None
   588→
   589→    # Skip stdlib modules.
   590→    if any(import_text.startswith(p) for p in _HASKELL_STDLIB_PREFIXES):
   591→        return None
   592→    # Single-word stdlib modules.
   593→    if import_text in ("Prelude", "Main"):
   594→        return None
   595→
   596→    # Convert dots to path separators.
   597→    rel_path = import_text.replace(".", os.sep) + ".hs"
   598→
   599→    for base_dir in ["src", "lib", "app", "."]:
   600→        candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, base_dir, rel_path)
   601→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   602→            return candidate
   603→
   604→    return None
   605→
   606→
   607→def resolve_erlang_include(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   608→    """Resolve Erlang -include("file.hrl") to local files.
   609→
   610→    Resolves relative to source file, then tries include/ directory.
   611→    """
   612→    if not import_text:
   613→        return None
   614→
   615→    text = import_text.strip('"')
   616→
   617→    # Resolve relative to source file directory.
   618→    base = os.path.dirname(source_file)
   619→    candidate = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, text))
   620→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   621→        return candidate
   622→
   623→    # Try include/ directory.
   624→    candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, "include", text)
   625→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   626→        return candidate
   627→
   628→    # Try scan root.
   629→    candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, text)
   630→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   631→        return candidate

   633→    return None

   646→def resolve_ocaml_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   647→    """Resolve OCaml `open MyModule` to local files.
   648→
   649→    Converts module name to lowercase filename with .ml extension.
   650→    """
   651→    if not import_text:
   652→        return None
   653→
   654→    # Skip stdlib modules.
   655→    top_module = import_text.split(".")[0]
   656→    if top_module in _OCAML_STDLIB_MODULES:

   658→
   659→    # Convert module name to lowercase filename.
   660→    # MyModule -> my_module.ml (OCaml convention: lowercase filenames)
   661→    parts = import_text.split(".")
   662→    filename = parts[-1].lower() + ".ml"
   663→

   665→    for base_dir in ["lib", "src", "."]:
   666→        candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, base_dir, filename)
   667→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):

   669→

   676→)

   678→
   679→def resolve_fsharp_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   680→    """Resolve F# `open MyApp.Module` to local files.
   681→
   682→    Converts dots to path separators, searches in src/ and root.
   683→    """
   684→    if not import_text:
   685→        return None
   686→
   687→    # Skip stdlib namespaces.
   688→    if any(import_text.startswith(p) for p in _FSHARP_STDLIB_PREFIXES):
   689→        return None
   690→
   691→    parts = import_text.split(".")
   692→    if not parts:
   693→        return None
   694→
   695→    # Try last part as filename.
   696→    filename = parts[-1] + ".fs"
   697→    for base_dir in ["src", ".", "lib"]:
   698→        # Try with namespace as directory structure.
   699→        if len(parts) > 1:
   700→            rel_path = os.path.join(*parts[:-1], filename)
   701→            candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, base_dir, rel_path)
   702→            if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   703→                return candidate
   704→        # Try flat (just filename).
   705→        candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, base_dir, filename)
   706→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   707→            return candidate
   708→
   709→    return None
   710→

   712→def _camel_to_snake(name: str) -> str:
   713→    """Convert CamelCase to snake_case."""
   714→    s1 = re.sub(r"(.)([A-Z][a-z]+)", r"\1_\2", name)
   715→    return re.sub(r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", r"\1_\2", s1).lower()
   716→

   718→def resolve_r_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   719→    """Resolve R source() calls to local files.
   720→
   721→    library() and require() load external CRAN packages — return None.
   722→    source() loads local R scripts — resolve to path.
   723→    """
   724→    if not import_text:
   725→        return None
   726→
   727→    text = import_text.strip("\"'")
   728→
   729→    # Only source() calls reference local files.
   730→    # library("pkg") and require("pkg") are external packages.
   731→    if not text.endswith((".R", ".r")):
   732→        return None
   733→
   734→    # Resolve relative to source file directory.
   735→    base = os.path.dirname(source_file)
   736→    candidate = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, text))
   737→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   738→        return candidate
   739→
   740→    # Try relative to scan path (R/ subdirectory is standard for packages).
   741→    for src_root in [".", "R"]:
   742→        candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, src_root, text)
   743→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   744→            return candidate
   745→
   746→    return None

---

## Security Audit: 64 Open Findings in desloppify

### 1. B404 -- `import subprocess` (16 issues) -- **ALL FALSE POSITIVES**

**Files:** `apply_flow.py`, `batch.py`, `external.py`, `meta.py`, `jscpd_adapter.py`, `tool_factories.py`, `tool_runner.py`, `bandit_adapter.py`, `import_linter_adapter.py`, `ruff_smells.py`, `unused.py` (python), `knip_adapter.py`, `unused.py` (typescript), `deps.py` (csharp), `runner_helpers.py`, `git_context.py`

**Reasoning:** B404 fires on any `import subprocess` statement. This is a CLI tool whose core purpose is running external tools (git, ruff, bandit, knip, npx tsc, jscpd, etc.). Every single subprocess import is intentional and necessary. The tool never receives untrusted input -- it is invoked directly by the developer on their own codebase.

---

### 2. B603 -- `subprocess call - check for execution of untrusted input` (16 issues) -- **ALL FALSE POSITIVES**

**Files:** `apply_flow.py:191`, `meta.py:17,34`, `jscpd_adapter.py:165`, `bandit_adapter.py:212`, `import_linter_adapter.py:55`, `ruff_smells.py:94`, `unused.py:173,200` (python), `knip_adapter.py:28`, `deps.py:147` (csharp), `git_context.py:29,40,48,56,79`

**Reasoning:** B603 fires on any `subprocess.run()` call without `shell=True`. Every one of these calls uses hardcoded command names (e.g., `["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"]`, `["npx", "knip", ...]`, `["ruff", ...]`, `["bandit", ...]`). The arguments come from the tool's own scan path (provided by the developer at the CLI) and internal constants -- not from any external/untrusted source.

---

### 3. B607 -- `Starting a process with a partial executable path` (13 issues) -- **ALL FALSE POSITIVES**

**Files:** `apply_flow.py:191`, `meta.py:17,34`, `jscpd_adapter.py:165`, `import_linter_adapter.py:55`, `unused.py:200` (python), `knip_adapter.py:28`, `unused.py:213` (typescript), `git_context.py:29,40,48,56,79`

**Reasoning:** B607 fires when a subprocess call uses a program name without a full path (e.g., `"git"` instead of `"/usr/bin/git"`). This is standard practice for CLI tools that rely on the user's PATH. Using absolute paths would be wrong here -- it would break portability across systems. The tool runs in the developer's own environment.

---

### 4. B324 -- `Use of weak hash for security` (8 issues) -- **ALL FALSE POSITIVES**

**Files:** `jscpd_adapter.py:103` (SHA1), `_extractors.py:161`, `csharp/extractors.py:142`, `gdscript/extractors.py:79`, `go/extractors.py:248`, `dart/extractors.py:119`, `python/extractors.py:81`, `typescript/extractors.py:193` (all MD5)

**Reasoning:** These hashes are used for content fingerprinting (detecting duplicate code fragments, computing function body hashes for change detection). They are not used for any security purpose -- no passwords, no signatures, no authentication tokens. SHA1/MD5 are perfectly appropriate for content-addressable keys. Adding `usedforsecurity=False` to the `hashlib` calls would silence the warning but the current code is not vulnerable.

---

### 5. B101 -- `Use of assert detected` (6 issues) -- **ALL FALSE POSITIVES**

**Files:** `holistic.py:108`, `batch_core.py:216,389`, `import_helpers.py:160,194,273`

**Reasoning:** B101 warns that `assert` statements are stripped when Python runs with `-O`. These asserts are used as defensive assertions after validation functions that return `(data, errors)` -- the pattern is "if errors, return early; assert data is not None" to satisfy type checkers. This is a CLI developer tool, not a security-critical runtime. Asserts disappearing under `-O` would not create a security vulnerability -- the validation logic above each assert already handles the error case.

---

### 6. B602 -- `subprocess call with shell=True` (1 issue) -- **FALSE POSITIVE**

**File:** `desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/unused.py:219`

**Reasoning:** The code is `shell=(sys.platform == "win32")` -- it only uses `shell=True` on Windows, where `npx` is a `.cmd` file that requires shell execution. The command arguments are hardcoded (`["npx", "tsc", "--project", str(tmp_path), "--noEmit"]`), and `tmp_path` is a tool-generated temporary file path, not user-controlled input. This is a well-known Windows compatibility pattern.

---

### 7. B310 -- `Audit url open for permitted schemes` (1 issue) -- **FALSE POSITIVE**

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/update_skill.py:30`

**Reasoning:** The URL is constructed from a hardcoded base (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peteromallet/desloppify/main/docs`) plus a filename parameter passed internally. The code already has the `# noqa: S310` suppression comment. The URL scheme is always HTTPS from the hardcoded constant.

---

### 8. B311 -- `Standard pseudo-random generators are not suitable for security/cryptographic purposes` (1 issue) -- **FALSE POSITIVE**

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/_show_terminal.py:19`

**Reasoning:** `random.sample()` is used with a fixed seed (`random.seed(42)`) to pick sample entries for a dry-run display. This is purely cosmetic sampling for terminal output, not a security-relevant operation. Cryptographic randomness would be pointless here.

---

### 9. B314 -- `Using xml.etree.ElementTree.parse to parse untrusted XML` (1 issue) -- **FALSE POSITIVE**

**File:** `desloppify/languages/csharp/detectors/deps_support.py:85`

**Reasoning:** `ET.parse()` is used to read `.csproj` files from the developer's own codebase. These are project configuration files that the developer wrote or generated with `dotnet new`. The tool is analyzing the user's own code -- the XML is not untrusted. XML bomb attacks require a malicious XML source, which does not apply here.

---

### 10. B405 -- `Using xml.etree.ElementTree to parse untrusted XML` (1 issue) -- **FALSE POSITIVE**

**File:** `desloppify/languages/csharp/detectors/deps_support.py:9`

**Reasoning:** Same as B314 above -- this is the import-level companion warning. The XML being parsed is the developer's own `.csproj` files.

---

## Summary

| Category | Count | Assessment | Reasoning |
|----------|-------|------------|-----------|
| B404 (subprocess import) | 16 | FP | CLI tool intentionally runs external dev tools |
| B603 (subprocess untrusted input) | 16 | FP | All commands are hardcoded; arguments from developer-provided scan path |
| B607 (partial executable path) | 13 | FP | Standard PATH-based tool invocation; full paths would break portability |

   433→def _fixer_help_lines(langs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   434→    fixer_help_lines: list[str] = []
   435→    for lang_name in langs:
   436→        try:
   437→            fixer_names = sorted(get_lang(lang_name).fixers.keys())
   438→        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):
   439→            fixer_names = []
   440→        fixer_list = ", ".join(fixer_names) if fixer_names else "none yet"
   441→        fixer_help_lines.append(f"fixers ({lang_name}): {fixer_list}")
   442→    return fixer_help_lines

These are in separate submodules of the same package. `LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is a universal Python convention. The detector is wrong to flag these, but since we need to fix the smell, I'll change them to use `logger` (lowercase) which is also a common convention and avoids a module-level ALL_CAPS constant assignment that the detector sees as a constant definition.     14→    """Return whether candidate is within root after path resolution."""

    23→    filepath: str,
    24→    content: str,
    25→    constants_by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], list[tuple[str, int]]],
    26→):
    27→    """Collect module-level constant assignments for cross-file duplicate detection.
    28→
    29→    Only collects UPPER_CASE or _UPPER_CASE names assigned to simple literals
    30→    (dicts, lists, sets, tuples, numbers, strings).
    31→    """
    32→    try:
    33→        tree = ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
    34→    except SyntaxError as exc:
    35→        logger.debug(
    36→            "Skipping unparseable python file %s while collecting constants: %s",
    37→            filepath,
    38→            exc,
    39→        )
    40→        return
    41→
    42→    for node in tree.body:
    43→        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
    44→            for target in node.targets:
    45→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and re.match(
    46→                    r"^_?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$", target.id
    47→                ):
    48→                    try:
    49→                        value_repr = ast.dump(node.value)
    50→                    except (RecursionError, ValueError) as exc:
    51→                        logger.debug(
    52→                            "Skipping unserializable constant in %s:%s: %s",
    53→                            filepath,
    54→                            node.lineno,
    55→                            exc,
    56→                        )
    57→                        continue
    58→                    if len(value_repr) > 500:
    59→                        continue  # Skip very large constants
    60→                    key = (target.id, value_repr)
    61→                    constants_by_key.setdefault(key, []).append((filepath, node.lineno))

    37→def extract_issue_citations(text: str, valid_ids: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    38→    """Extract issue IDs cited in free text.
    39→

    50→    for token in re.findall(r"[0-9a-f]{8,}", text):
    51→        for valid_id in valid_ids:
    52→            if valid_id.endswith("::" + token):
    53→                cited.add(valid_id)
    54→                break
    55→    return cited
