   141→def augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   142→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   143→    *,
   144→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   145→    scan_path: Path,
   146→    project_root: Path,
   147→    decay_scans: int,
   148→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
   149→    """Append re-triage issues for stale or worsening wontfix debt."""
   150→    existing = state.get("issues", {})
   151→    if not isinstance(existing, dict):
   152→        return issues, 0
   153→
   154→    current_by_id = {
   155→        issue.get("id"): issue
   156→        for issue in issues
   157→        if issue.get("id")
   158→    }
   159→    augmented = list(issues)
   160→    monitored = 0
   161→
   162→    for issue_id, previous in existing.items():
   163→        if not isinstance(previous, dict):
   164→            continue
   165→        if previous.get("status") != "wontfix":
   166→            continue
   167→        if issue_id not in current_by_id:
   168→            continue
   169→        if not _in_scan_scope(
   170→            str(previous.get("file", "")),
   171→            scan_path,
   172→            project_root=project_root,
   173→        ):
   174→            continue
   175→
   176→        monitored += 1
   177→        scan_count = int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   178→        since_scan = scan_count - int(previous.get("wontfix_scan_count", scan_count) or 0)
   179→        since_scan = max(since_scan, 0)
   180→
   181→        reasons, drift = _wontfix_staleness_reasons(
   182→            previous,
   183→            current_by_id[issue_id],
   184→            since_scan=since_scan,
   185→            decay_scans=decay_scans,
   186→        )
   187→        if not reasons:

   189→
   190→        augmented.append(

   193→                previous,
   194→                reasons=reasons,
   195→                drift=drift,
   196→                since_scan=since_scan,
   197→            )
   198→        )

   200→    return augmented, monitored

Now that I've updated the original issues' `wontfix_scan_count`, on the NEXT scan these stale_wontfix wrappers will auto-resolve (because the original issue's `wontfix_scan_count` will be recent). But to clean them up NOW, I should mark them as auto_resolved in state so they don't show up.

Let me do that. The appropriate status for stale_wontfix wrappers that no longer apply is `auto_resolved`.

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
```json
{
  "command": "python3 << 'PYEOF'\nimport json, shutil, tempfile, os\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\n\nstate_path = Path(\".desloppify/state-python.json\")\nbackup = state_path.with_suffix(\".json.bak\")\nshutil.copy2(str(state_path), str(backup))\n\nstate = json.loads(state_path.read_text())\nissues = state.get(\"issues\", {})\nnow = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec=\"seconds\").replace(\"+00:00\", \"Z\")\n\nresolved = 0\nfor issue_id, issue in list(issues.items()):\n    if not issue_id.startswith(\"stale_wontfix::\"):\n        continue\n    if issue.get(\"status\") != \"open\":\n        continue\n    issue[\"status\"] = \"auto_resolved\"\n    issue[\"resolved_at\"] = now\n    issue[\"note\"] = \"Stale wontfix re-triaged: original wontfix refreshed after code review\"\n    resolved += 1\n    print(f\"AUTO_RESOLVED: {issue_id}\")\n\ncontent = json.dumps(state, indent=2) + \"\\n\"\nfd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(state_path.parent), suffix=\".tmp\")\nos.write(fd, content.encode())\nos.close(fd)\nos.replace(tmp, str(state_path))\n\nprint(f\"\\nAuto-resolved {resolved} stale_wontfix wrapper issues\")\nPYEOF",
  "description": "Auto-resolve stale_wontfix wrapper issues in state"
}

   215→def _start_live_writer(
   216→    state: _RunnerState, ctx: _AttemptContext, interval: float,
   217→) -> threading.Thread:
   218→    """Spawn a daemon thread that periodically writes live log snapshots."""
   219→    def _loop() -> None:
   220→        while not state.stop_event.wait(interval):
   221→            _write_live_snapshot(state, ctx)
   222→
   223→    thread = threading.Thread(target=_loop, daemon=True)
   224→    thread.start()
   225→    return thread
   226→
   227→
   228→def _check_stall(
   229→    output_file: Path,
   230→    prev_sig: tuple[int, int] | None,
   231→    prev_stable: float | None,
   232→    now: float,
   233→    last_activity: float,
   234→    threshold: int,
   235→) -> tuple[bool, tuple[int, int] | None, float | None]:
   236→    """Check for runner stall. Returns (stalled, new_sig, new_stable_since)."""
   237→    try:
   238→        stat = output_file.stat()
   239→        current_signature: tuple[int, int] | None = (int(stat.st_size), int(stat.st_mtime))
   240→    except OSError:
   241→        current_signature = None
   242→    if current_signature is None:
   243→        # If no output file ever appears, still recover from a silent hang once
   244→        # both output state and process streams have been idle long enough.
   245→        baseline = (
   246→            prev_stable if isinstance(prev_stable, int | float) else now
   247→        )
   248→        output_age = now - baseline
   249→        stream_idle = now - last_activity
   250→        if output_age >= threshold and stream_idle >= threshold:
   251→            return True, None, baseline
   252→        return False, None, baseline
   253→    if current_signature != prev_sig:
   254→        return False, current_signature, now
   255→    if prev_stable is None:
   256→        return False, prev_sig, prev_stable
   257→    output_age = now - prev_stable
   258→    stream_idle = now - last_activity
   259→    if output_age >= threshold and stream_idle >= threshold:
   260→        return True, prev_sig, prev_stable
   261→    return False, prev_sig, prev_stable
   262→
   263→
   264→def run_codex_batch(
   265→    *,
   266→    prompt: str,
   267→    repo_root: Path,
   268→    output_file: Path,
   269→    log_file: Path,
   270→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   271→) -> int:
   272→    """Execute one codex batch and return a stable CLI-style status code."""
   273→    cmd = codex_batch_command(prompt=prompt, repo_root=repo_root, output_file=output_file)
   274→    retries_raw = deps.max_retries if isinstance(deps.max_retries, int) else 0
   275→    max_retries = max(0, retries_raw)
   276→    max_attempts = max_retries + 1
   277→    backoff_raw = (
   278→        float(deps.retry_backoff_seconds)
   279→        if isinstance(deps.retry_backoff_seconds, int | float)
   280→        else 0.0
   281→    )
   282→    retry_backoff_seconds = max(0.0, backoff_raw)
   283→    live_log_interval = (
   284→        float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds)
   285→        if isinstance(deps.live_log_interval_seconds, int | float)
   286→        and float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds) > 0
   287→        else 5.0
   288→    )
   289→    stall_seconds = (
   290→        int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds)
   291→        if isinstance(deps.stall_after_output_seconds, int | float)
   292→        and int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds) > 0
   293→        else 0
   294→    )
   295→    log_sections: list[str] = []
   296→    use_popen = bool(deps.use_popen_runner) and callable(
   297→        getattr(deps, "subprocess_popen", None)
   298→    )
   299→
   300→    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts + 1):
   301→        header = f"ATTEMPT {attempt}/{max_attempts}\n$ {' '.join(cmd)}"
   302→        started_monotonic = time.monotonic()
   303→        state = _RunnerState(last_stream_activity=started_monotonic)
   304→        ctx = _AttemptContext(
   305→            header=header,
   306→            started_at_iso=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
   307→            started_monotonic=started_monotonic,
   308→            output_file=output_file,
   309→            log_file=log_file,
   310→            log_sections=log_sections,
   311→            safe_write_text_fn=deps.safe_write_text_fn,
   312→        )
   313→        _write_live_snapshot(state, ctx)
   314→
   315→        if use_popen:
   316→            result = _run_via_popen(cmd, deps, state, ctx, live_log_interval, stall_seconds)
   317→        else:
   318→            result = _run_via_subprocess(cmd, deps, state, ctx, live_log_interval)
   319→
   320→        if result.early_return is not None:
   321→            return result.early_return
   322→
   323→        if result.timed_out:
   324→            log_sections.append(
   325→                f"{header}\n\nTIMEOUT after {deps.timeout_seconds}s\n\n"
   326→                f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   327→            )
   328→            if _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   329→                log_sections.append(
   330→                    "Recovered timed-out batch from JSON output file; "
   331→                    "continuing as success."
   332→                )
   333→                deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   334→                return 0
   335→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   336→            return 124
   337→
   338→        if result.stalled:
   339→            log_sections.append(
   340→                f"{header}\n\nSTALL RECOVERY after {stall_seconds}s "
   341→                "of stable output and no stream activity.\n\n"
   342→                f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   343→            )
   344→            if _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   345→                log_sections.append(
   346→                    "Recovered stalled batch from JSON output file; "
   347→                    "continuing as success."
   348→                )
   349→                deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   350→                return 0
   351→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   352→            return 124
   353→
   354→        log_sections.append(
   355→            f"{header}\n\nSTDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   356→        )
   357→
   358→        if result.code == 0:
   359→            if not _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   360→                log_sections.append(
   361→                    "Runner exited 0 but output file is missing or invalid; "
   362→                    "treating as execution failure."
   363→                )
   364→                deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   365→                return 1
   366→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   367→            return 0
   368→
   369→        combined = f"{result.stdout_text}\n{result.stderr_text}".lower()
   370→        is_transient = any(needle in combined for needle in _TRANSIENT_RUNNER_PHRASES)
   371→        if not is_transient or attempt >= max_attempts:
   372→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   373→            return result.code
   374→
   375→        delay_seconds = retry_backoff_seconds * (2 ** (attempt - 1))
   376→        log_sections.append(
   377→            "Transient runner failure detected; "
   378→            f"retrying in {delay_seconds:.1f}s (attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_attempts})."
   379→        )
   380→        try:
   381→            if delay_seconds > 0:
   382→                deps.sleep_fn(delay_seconds)
   383→        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
   384→            log_sections.append(
   385→                f"Retry delay hook failed: {exc} — aborting remaining retries."
   386→            )
   387→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   388→            return 1
   389→
   390→    deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   391→    return 1
   392→
   393→
   394→def run_followup_scan(
   395→    *,
   396→    lang_name: str,
   397→    scan_path: str,
   398→    deps: FollowupScanDeps,
   399→) -> int:
   400→    """Run a follow-up scan and return a non-zero status when it fails."""
   401→    scan_cmd = [
   402→        deps.python_executable,
   403→        "-m",
   404→        "desloppify",
   405→        "--lang",
   406→        lang_name,
   407→        "scan",
   408→        "--path",
   409→        scan_path,
   410→    ]
   411→    print(deps.colorize_fn("\n  Running follow-up scan...", "bold"))
   412→    try:
   413→        result = deps.subprocess_run(
   414→            scan_cmd,
   415→            cwd=str(deps.project_root),
   416→            timeout=deps.timeout_seconds,
   417→        )
   418→    except deps.timeout_error:
   419→        print(
   420→            deps.colorize_fn(
   421→                f"  Follow-up scan timed out after {deps.timeout_seconds}s.",
   422→                "yellow",
   423→            ),
   424→            file=sys.stderr,
   425→        )
   426→        return 124
   427→    except OSError as exc:
   428→        print(
   429→            deps.colorize_fn(f"  Follow-up scan failed: {exc}", "red"),
   430→            file=sys.stderr,
   431→        )
   432→        return 1
   433→    return int(getattr(result, "returncode", 0) or 0)
   434→

   436→def _build_blind_packet(packet: dict) -> dict:
   437→    """Return a blind-review packet with score anchoring metadata removed."""
   438→    blind = deepcopy(packet)
   439→    for key in _BLIND_PACKET_DROP_KEYS:
   440→        blind.pop(key, None)
   441→
   442→    config = blind.get("config")
   443→    if isinstance(config, dict):
   444→        sanitized = _sanitize_blind_config(config)
   445→        if sanitized:
   446→            blind["config"] = sanitized
   447→        else:
   448→            blind.pop("config", None)
   449→    return blind
   450→
   451→
   452→def build_blind_packet(packet: dict) -> dict:
   453→    """Public wrapper for blind packet sanitization."""
   454→    return _build_blind_packet(packet)

   457→def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str | None:
   458→    """Compute sha256 hex digest for path contents (or None on read failure)."""
   459→    try:
   460→        data = path.read_bytes()
   461→    except OSError:
   462→        return None
   463→    return sha256(data).hexdigest()

   465→
   466→def _emit_progress(
   467→    progress_fn,
   468→    batch_index: int,
   469→    event: str,
   470→    code: int | None = None,
   471→    *,
   472→    details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   473→) -> Exception | None:
   474→    """Forward a progress event and return callback exceptions to caller."""
   475→    if not callable(progress_fn):
   476→        return None
   477→    payload = dict(details or {})
   478→    progress_event = BatchProgressEvent(
   479→        batch_index=batch_index,
   480→        event=event,
   481→        code=code,
   482→        details=payload,
   483→    )
   484→    try:
   485→        progress_fn(progress_event)
   486→        return None
   487→    except TypeError as exc:
   488→        if not _looks_like_progress_signature_mismatch(exc):
   489→            return RuntimeError(
   490→                f"progress callback failed for event={event} batch={batch_index}: {exc}"
   491→            )
   492→        try:
   493→            progress_fn(batch_index, event, code, **payload)
   494→            return None
   495→        except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as legacy_exc:
   496→            return RuntimeError(
   497→                f"progress callback failed for event={event} batch={batch_index}: {legacy_exc}"
   498→            )
   499→    except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   500→        return RuntimeError(
   501→            f"progress callback failed for event={event} batch={batch_index}: {exc}"
   502→        )
   503→
   504→
   505→def _record_execution_error(
   506→    *,
   507→    error_log_fn,
   508→    failures: set[int],
   509→    idx: int,
   510→    exc: Exception,
   511→) -> None:
   512→    """Record an execution/progress error through shared failure plumbing."""
   513→    if callable(error_log_fn):
   514→        try:
   515→            error_log_fn(idx, exc)
   516→        except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
   517→            _ = exc  # error-logging callback failed; don't crash the batch
   518→    failures.add(idx)
   519→
   520→
   521→def _record_parallel_progress_error(
   522→    *,
   523→    idx: int,
   524→    err: Exception,
   525→    progress_failures: set[int],
   526→    lock: threading.Lock,
   527→    error_log_fn,
   528→) -> None:
   529→    """Record a progress callback error during parallel execution."""
   530→    with lock:
   531→        progress_failures.add(idx)
   532→    if not callable(error_log_fn):
   533→        return
   534→    try:
   535→        error_log_fn(idx, err)
   536→    except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   537→        _ = exc  # error-logging callback failed; don't crash the batch
   538→
   539→
   540→def execute_batches(
   541→    *,
   542→    tasks: dict[int, object],
   543→    run_parallel: bool,
   544→    progress_fn=None,
   545→    error_log_fn=None,
   546→    max_parallel_workers: int | None = None,
   547→    heartbeat_seconds: float | None = 15.0,
   548→    clock_fn=time.monotonic,
   549→) -> list[int]:
   550→    """Run indexed tasks and return failed index list.
   551→
   552→    Each value in *tasks* is a zero-arg callable returning an int exit code.
   553→    All domain knowledge (files, prompts, etc.) is pre-bound by the caller.
   554→    """
   555→    indexes = sorted(tasks)
   556→    if run_parallel:
   557→        return _execute_parallel(
   558→            tasks=tasks,
   559→            indexes=indexes,
   560→            progress_fn=progress_fn,
   561→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   562→            max_parallel_workers=max_parallel_workers,
   563→            heartbeat_seconds=heartbeat_seconds,
   564→            clock_fn=clock_fn,
   565→        )
   566→    return _execute_serial(
   567→        tasks=tasks,
   568→        indexes=indexes,
   569→        progress_fn=progress_fn,
   570→        error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   571→        clock_fn=clock_fn,
   572→    )
   573→
   574→
   575→def _execute_serial(*, tasks, indexes, progress_fn, error_log_fn, clock_fn) -> list[int]:
   576→    """Run tasks one at a time — no threads, no closures."""
   577→    failures: set[int] = set()
   578→    for idx in indexes:
   579→        t0 = float(clock_fn())
   580→        start_error = _emit_progress(
   581→            progress_fn, idx, "start", None, details={"max_workers": 1}
   582→        )
   583→        if start_error is not None:
   584→            _record_execution_error(
   585→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   586→                failures=failures,
   587→                idx=idx,
   588→                exc=start_error,
   589→            )
   590→        try:
   591→            code = tasks[idx]()
   592→        except _RUNNER_TASK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   593→            _record_execution_error(
   594→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   595→                failures=failures,
   596→                idx=idx,
   597→                exc=exc,
   598→            )
   599→            code = 1
   600→        if code != 0:
   601→            failures.add(idx)
   602→        done_error = _emit_progress(
   603→            progress_fn, idx, "done", code,
   604→            details={"elapsed_seconds": int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - t0))},
   605→        )
   606→        if done_error is not None:
   607→            _record_execution_error(
   608→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   609→                failures=failures,
   610→                idx=idx,
   611→                exc=done_error,
   612→            )
   613→    return sorted(failures)
   614→
   615→
   616→def _execute_parallel(
   617→    *, tasks, indexes, progress_fn, error_log_fn,
   618→    max_parallel_workers, heartbeat_seconds, clock_fn,
   619→) -> list[int]:
   620→    """Run tasks in a thread pool with optional heartbeat monitoring.
   621→
   622→    Two closures (_run_one, _on_complete) share mutable executor state
   623→    (started_at, failures) under a lock — the natural pattern for thread-pool
   624→    work.
   625→    """
   626→    requested = (
   627→        int(max_parallel_workers)
   628→        if isinstance(max_parallel_workers, int) and max_parallel_workers > 0
   629→        else 8
   630→    )
   631→    max_workers = max(1, min(len(indexes), requested))
   632→    heartbeat = (
   633→        float(heartbeat_seconds)
   634→        if isinstance(heartbeat_seconds, int | float) and heartbeat_seconds > 0
   635→        else None
   636→    )
   637→
   638→    failures: set[int] = set()
   639→    progress_failures: set[int] = set()
   640→    started_at: dict[int, float] = {}
   641→    lock = threading.Lock()
   642→
   643→    def _run_one(idx: int) -> int:
   644→        with lock:
   645→            started_at[idx] = float(clock_fn())
   646→        progress_error = _emit_progress(
   647→            progress_fn, idx, "start", None,
   648→            details={"max_workers": max_workers},
   649→        )
   650→        if progress_error is not None:
   651→            _record_parallel_progress_error(
   652→                idx=idx,
   653→                err=progress_error,
   654→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   655→                lock=lock,
   656→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   657→            )
   658→        return tasks[idx]()
   659→
   660→    def _on_complete(future) -> None:
   661→        idx = futures[future]
   662→        with lock:
   663→            t0 = started_at.get(idx, float(clock_fn()))
   664→        elapsed = int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - t0))
   665→        try:
   666→            code = future.result()
   667→        except _RUNNER_TASK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   668→            _record_execution_error(
   669→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   670→                failures=failures,
   671→                idx=idx,
   672→                exc=exc,
   673→            )
   674→            done_error = _emit_progress(
   675→                progress_fn, idx, "done", 1, details={"elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   676→            )
   677→            if done_error is not None:
   678→                _record_parallel_progress_error(
   679→                    idx=idx,
   680→                    err=done_error,
   681→                    progress_failures=progress_failures,
   682→                    lock=lock,
   683→                    error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   684→                )
   685→            return
   686→        done_error = _emit_progress(
   687→            progress_fn, idx, "done", code, details={"elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   688→        )
   689→        if done_error is not None:
   690→            _record_parallel_progress_error(
   691→                idx=idx,
   692→                err=done_error,
   693→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   694→                lock=lock,
   695→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   696→            )
   697→        with lock:
   698→            had_progress_failure = idx in progress_failures
   699→        if code != 0 or had_progress_failure:
   700→            failures.add(idx)
   701→
   702→    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
   703→        futures: dict = {}
   704→        for idx in indexes:
   705→            queue_error = _emit_progress(
   706→                progress_fn, idx, "queued", None,
   707→                details={"max_workers": max_workers},
   708→            )
   709→            if queue_error is not None:
   710→                _record_parallel_progress_error(
   711→                    idx=idx,
   712→                    err=queue_error,
   713→                    progress_failures=progress_failures,
   714→                    lock=lock,
   715→                    error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   716→                )
   717→                failures.add(idx)
   718→            futures[executor.submit(_run_one, idx)] = idx
   719→
   720→        pending = set(futures.keys())
   721→
   722→        if heartbeat is None:
   723→            for future in as_completed(pending):
   724→                _on_complete(future)
   725→            return failures
   726→
   727→        while pending:
   728→            try:
   729→                future = next(as_completed(pending, timeout=heartbeat))
   730→            except FuturesTimeoutError:
   731→                _heartbeat(
   732→                    pending,
   733→                    futures,
   734→                    started_at,
   735→                    lock,
   736→                    indexes,
   737→                    progress_fn,
   738→                    clock_fn,
   739→                    error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   740→                )
   741→                continue
   742→            pending.discard(future)
   743→            _on_complete(future)
   744→    return sorted(failures)
   745→
   746→
   747→def _heartbeat(
   748→    pending,
   749→    futures,
   750→    started_at,
   751→    lock,
   752→    indexes,
   753→    progress_fn,
   754→    clock_fn,
   755→    *,
   756→    error_log_fn=None,
   757→):
   758→    """Build and emit a heartbeat with active/queued batch status."""
   759→    with lock:
   760→        active = sorted(futures[f] for f in pending if futures[f] in started_at)
   761→    active_set = set(active)
   762→    queued = sorted(futures[f] for f in pending if futures[f] not in active_set)
   763→    elapsed = {
   764→        idx: int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - started_at.get(idx, clock_fn())))
   765→        for idx in active
   766→    }
   767→    heartbeat_error = _emit_progress(
   768→        progress_fn, -1, "heartbeat", None,
   769→        details={
   770→            "active_batches": active,
   771→            "queued_batches": queued,
   772→            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   773→            "active_count": len(active),
   774→            "queued_count": len(queued),
   775→            "total_count": len(indexes),
   776→        },
   777→    )
   778→    if heartbeat_error is not None and callable(error_log_fn):
   779→        try:
   780→            error_log_fn(-1, heartbeat_error)
   781→        except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   782→            _ = exc  # error-logging callback failed; don't crash the batch
   783→
   784→
   785→def _extract_payload_from_log(
   786→    batch_index: int, raw_path: Path, extract_fn,
   787→) -> dict[str, object] | None:
   788→    """Try to recover a batch payload from the runner log file."""
   789→    log_path = raw_path.parent.parent / "logs" / f"batch-{batch_index + 1}.log"
   790→    if not log_path.exists():
   791→        return None
   792→    try:
   793→        log_text = log_path.read_text()
   794→    except OSError:
   795→        return None
   796→
   797→    # Prefer the final STDOUT section for the attempt; if that fails, scan the full log.
   798→    stdout_marker = "\nSTDOUT:\n"
   799→    stderr_marker = "\n\nSTDERR:\n"
   800→    stdout_start = log_text.rfind(stdout_marker)
   801→    if stdout_start == -1 and log_text.startswith("STDOUT:\n"):
   802→        stdout_start = 0
   803→        stdout_offset = len("STDOUT:\n")
   804→    elif stdout_start >= 0:
   805→        stdout_offset = len(stdout_marker)
   806→    else:
   807→        stdout_offset = 0
   808→    if stdout_start >= 0:
   809→        start_idx = stdout_start + stdout_offset
   810→        stdout_end = log_text.find(stderr_marker, start_idx)
   811→        stdout_text = (
   812→            log_text[start_idx:] if stdout_end == -1 else log_text[start_idx:stdout_end]
   813→        )
   814→        payload = extract_fn(stdout_text)
   815→        if payload is not None:
   816→            return payload
   817→        # If the batch log has a concrete STDOUT section but it contains no parseable
   818→        # payload, do not fallback to parsing the whole log. Full logs include the
   819→        # prompt template (often with JSON examples), which can generate misleading
   820→        # decode errors and hide the true runner failure in STDERR.
   821→        return None
   822→
   823→    return extract_fn(log_text)

   826→def collect_batch_results(
   827→    *,
   828→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   829→    failures: list[int],
   830→    output_files: dict[int, Path],
   831→    allowed_dims: set[str],
   832→    extract_payload_fn,
   833→    normalize_result_fn,
   834→) -> tuple[list[BatchResult], list[int]]:
   835→    """Parse and normalize batch outputs, preserving prior failures."""
   836→    batch_results: list[BatchResult] = []
   837→    failure_set = set(failures)
   838→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   839→        had_execution_failure = idx in failure_set
   840→        raw_path = output_files[idx]
   841→        payload = None
   842→        parsed_from_log = False
   843→        if raw_path.exists():
   844→            try:
   845→                payload = extract_payload_fn(raw_path.read_text())
   846→            except OSError:
   847→                payload = None
   848→        if payload is None:
   849→            payload = _extract_payload_from_log(idx, raw_path, extract_payload_fn)
   850→            parsed_from_log = payload is not None
   851→        if payload is None:
   852→            failure_set.add(idx)
   853→            continue
   854→        if parsed_from_log:
   855→            try:
   856→                safe_write_text(raw_path, json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   857→            except OSError as exc:
   858→                _ = exc
   859→        try:
   860→            assessments, issues, dimension_notes, quality = normalize_result_fn(
   861→                payload,
   862→                allowed_dims,
   863→            )
   864→        except ValueError:
   865→            failure_set.add(idx)
   866→            continue
   867→        if had_execution_failure:
   868→            failure_set.discard(idx)
   869→        batch_results.append(
   870→            BatchResult(
   871→                batch_index=idx + 1,
   872→                assessments=assessments,
   873→                dimension_notes=dimension_notes,
   874→                issues=issues,
   875→                quality=quality,
   876→            )
   877→        )
   878→    return batch_results, sorted(failure_set)

   934→def _summarize_failure_categories(*, failures: list[int], logs_dir: Path) -> dict[str, int]:
   935→    """Return counts by failure category for failed batches."""
   936→    categories: dict[str, int] = {}
   937→    for idx in sorted(set(failures)):

   950→def _runner_failure_hints(*, failures: list[int], logs_dir: Path) -> list[str]:

  1015→                    "Re-run `desloppify review --run-batches ...` from a host shell with "
  1016→                    "outbound network access, or allow unsandboxed execution in your agent."
  1017→                )
  1018→                if hint not in hints:

  1020→        if "failed to load skill" in text and "missing yaml frontmatter" in text:

  1030→def _any_restricted_sandbox_failures(*, failures: list[int], logs_dir: Path) -> bool:
  1031→    """Return True when any failed batch log shows restricted sandbox indicators."""
  1032→    for idx in sorted(set(failures)):

  1034→        text = ""
  1035→        try:

  1037→        except OSError as exc:

  1039→        if not text:

  1041→        if _looks_like_restricted_sandbox(text):

  1046→def _print_failures_report(
  1047→    *,
  1048→    failures: list[int],
  1049→    packet_path: Path,
  1050→    logs_dir: Path,
  1051→    colorize_fn,
  1052→) -> None:
  1053→    """Render retry guidance for failed batches."""
  1054→    failed_1 = sorted({idx + 1 for idx in failures})
  1055→    failed_csv = ",".join(str(i) for i in failed_1)
  1056→    print(colorize_fn(f"\n  Failed batches: {failed_1}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
  1057→    categories = _summarize_failure_categories(failures=failures, logs_dir=logs_dir)
  1058→    if categories:
  1059→        labels = {
  1060→            "timeout": "timeout",
  1061→            "stream_disconnect": "stream disconnect",
  1062→            "usage_limit": "usage limit",
  1063→            "runner_missing": "runner missing",
  1064→            "runner_auth": "runner auth",
  1065→            "runner_exception": "runner exception",
  1066→            "missing_log": "missing log",
  1067→            "log_read_error": "log read error",
  1068→            "unknown": "unknown",
  1069→        }
  1070→        category_segments = [
  1071→            f"{labels.get(name, name)}={count}"
  1072→            for name, count in sorted(categories.items())
  1073→        ]
  1074→        print(
  1075→            colorize_fn(
  1076→                f"  Failure categories: {', '.join(category_segments)}",
  1077→                "yellow",
  1078→            ),
  1079→            file=sys.stderr,
  1080→        )
  1081→        if categories.get("timeout", 0) > 0:
  1082→            print(
  1083→                colorize_fn(
  1084→                    "  Timeout tuning: lower concurrency with `--max-parallel-batches 1..3` "
  1085→                    "or increase `--batch-timeout-seconds` for long-running reviews.",
  1086→                    "yellow",
  1087→                ),
  1088→                file=sys.stderr,
  1089→            )
  1090→        if categories.get("stream_disconnect", 0) > 0:
  1091→            print(
  1092→                colorize_fn(
  1093→                    "  Connectivity tuning: enable retries with `--batch-max-retries 2` "
  1094→                    "and `--batch-retry-backoff-seconds 2`, then retry failed batches.",
  1095→                    "yellow",
  1096→                ),
  1097→                file=sys.stderr,
  1098→            )
  1099→            if _any_restricted_sandbox_failures(failures=failures, logs_dir=logs_dir):
  1100→                print(
  1101→                    colorize_fn(
  1102→                        "  Sandbox hint: logs indicate restricted sandbox execution. "
  1103→                        "Re-run from a host shell with outbound network access, or "
  1104→                        "allow unsandboxed execution in your agent.",
  1105→                        "yellow",
  1106→                    ),
  1107→                    file=sys.stderr,
  1108→                )
  1109→    print(colorize_fn("  Retry command:", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
  1110→    print(
  1111→        colorize_fn(
  1112→            f"    desloppify review --run-batches --packet {packet_path} --only-batches {failed_csv}",
  1113→            "yellow",
  1114→        ),
  1115→        file=sys.stderr,
  1116→    )
  1117→    for idx_1 in failed_1:
  1118→        log_file = logs_dir / f"batch-{idx_1}.log"
  1119→        print(colorize_fn(f"    log: {log_file}", "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
  1120→    hints = _runner_failure_hints(failures=failures, logs_dir=logs_dir)
  1121→    if hints:
  1122→        print(colorize_fn("  Environment hints:", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
  1123→        for hint in hints:
  1124→            print(colorize_fn(f"    {hint}", "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
  1125→
  1126→
  1127→def print_failures(
  1128→    *,
  1129→    failures: list[int],
  1130→    packet_path: Path,
  1131→    logs_dir: Path,
  1132→    colorize_fn,
  1133→) -> None:
  1134→    """Render retry guidance for failed batches without exiting."""
  1135→    normalized_failures = sorted({int(idx) for idx in failures})
  1136→    if not normalized_failures:
  1137→        print(colorize_fn("  Failed batches: []", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
  1138→        return
  1139→    _print_failures_report(
  1140→        failures=normalized_failures,
  1141→        packet_path=packet_path,
  1142→        logs_dir=logs_dir,
  1143→        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
  1144→    )
  1145→
  1146→
  1147→def print_failures_and_raise(
  1148→    *,
  1149→    failures: list[int],
  1150→    packet_path: Path,
  1151→    logs_dir: Path,
  1152→    colorize_fn,
  1153→) -> None:
  1154→    """Render retry guidance for failed batches and raise CommandError."""
  1155→    if not failures:
  1156→        print(colorize_fn("  Failed batches: []", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
  1157→    _print_failures_report(
  1158→        failures=failures,
  1159→        packet_path=packet_path,
  1160→        logs_dir=logs_dir,
  1161→        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
  1162→    )
  1163→    failed_1 = sorted({idx + 1 for idx in failures})
  1164→    raise CommandError(f"batch execution failed: {failed_1}", exit_code=1)

   170→            continue
   171→        dim_key = entry.get("dimension_key", "")
   172→        if not dim_key:
   173→            continue
   174→        fid = f"{SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX}{slugify(dim_key)}"
   175→        if fid not in stale_ids and fid not in unscored_ids:
   176→            under_target.add(fid)
   177→    return under_target
   178→
   179→
   180→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181→# Promoted-aware insertion helper
   182→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   183→
   184→def _after_promoted(order: list[str], plan: PlanModel) -> int:
   185→    """Return the insertion index just after the last promoted item in *order*.
   186→
   187→    When no promoted items are present (or none are in *order*), returns 0
   188→    so callers fall back to existing front-of-queue behavior.
   189→    """
   190→    promoted = set(plan.get("promoted_ids", []))
   191→    if not promoted:
   192→        return 0
   193→    last_idx = -1
   194→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   195→        if fid in promoted:
   196→            last_idx = i
   197→    return last_idx + 1 if last_idx >= 0 else 0
   198→
   199→
   200→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   201→# Unscored dimension sync (front of queue, unconditional)
   202→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   203→
   204→def sync_unscored_dimensions(
   205→    plan: PlanModel,
   206→    state: StateModel,
   207→) -> UnscoredDimensionSyncResult:
   208→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions.
   209→
   210→    1. **Prune** — remove ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are
   211→       no longer unscored AND not stale (avoids pruning stale IDs — that is
   212→       ``sync_stale_dimensions``' responsibility).
   213→    2. **Inject** — unconditionally prepend currently-unscored IDs to the
   214→       *front* of ``queue_order`` so initial reviews are the first priority.
   215→    """
   216→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   217→    result = UnscoredDimensionSyncResult()
   218→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   219→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   220→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   221→
   222→    # --- Cleanup: prune subjective IDs that are no longer unscored --------
   223→    # Only prune IDs that are neither unscored nor stale (stale sync owns those).
   224→    to_remove: list[str] = [
   225→        fid for fid in order
   226→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   227→        and fid not in unscored_ids
   228→        and fid not in stale_ids
   229→    ]
   230→    for fid in to_remove:
   231→        order.remove(fid)
   232→        result.pruned.append(fid)
   233→
   234→    # --- Inject: prepend unscored IDs after any promoted items -------------
   235→    existing = set(order)
   236→    insert_at = _after_promoted(order, plan)
   237→    for uid in reversed(sorted(unscored_ids)):
   238→        if uid not in existing:
   239→            order.insert(insert_at, uid)
   240→            result.injected.append(uid)
   241→
   242→    return result
   243→
   244→
   245→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   246→# Stale dimension sync (back of queue, conditional)
   247→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   248→
   249→def sync_stale_dimensions(
   250→    plan: PlanModel,
   251→    state: StateModel,
   252→    *,
   253→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   254→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   255→) -> StaleDimensionSyncResult:
   256→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with stale and under-target subjective dimensions.
   257→
   258→    1. Remove any ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are no
   259→       longer stale/under-target and not unscored (avoids pruning IDs owned
   260→       by ``sync_unscored_dimensions``).
   261→    2. Inject stale and under-target dimension IDs when either:
   262→       a. No objective items remain (mid-cycle: append to back), OR
   263→       b. A cycle just completed (post-cycle: insert at front so subjective
   264→          review takes priority over new objective issues).
   265→    """
   266→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   267→    result = StaleDimensionSyncResult()
   268→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   269→    under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state)
   270→    injectable_ids = stale_ids | under_target_ids
   271→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   272→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   273→
   274→    # --- Cleanup: prune resolved subjective IDs --------------------------
   275→    # Only prune IDs that are no longer injectable and not unscored.
   276→    to_remove: list[str] = [
   277→        fid for fid in order
   278→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   279→        and fid not in injectable_ids
   280→        and fid not in unscored_ids
   281→    ]
   282→    for fid in to_remove:
   283→        order.remove(fid)
   284→        result.pruned.append(fid)
   285→
   286→    # --- Inject or evict stale + under-target dimensions -----------------
   287→    if policy is not None:
   288→        has_real_items = policy.has_objective_backlog
   289→    else:
   290→        has_real_items = any(
   291→            f.get("status") == "open"
   292→            and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   293→            and not f.get("suppressed")
   294→            for f in state.get("issues", {}).values()
   295→        )
   296→
   297→    should_inject = not has_real_items or cycle_just_completed
   298→
   299→    if not should_inject:
   300→        # Mid-cycle with objective backlog: evict any stale/under-target IDs
   301→        # that are present in the queue.  They may have been grandfathered from
   302→        # the unscored phase and should not be visible until the objective
   303→        # backlog clears or a cycle completes.
   304→        to_evict = [
   305→            fid for fid in order
   306→            if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   307→            and fid in injectable_ids
   308→        ]
   309→        for fid in to_evict:
   310→            order.remove(fid)
   311→            result.pruned.append(fid)
   312→
   313→    if should_inject and injectable_ids:
   314→        existing = set(order)
   315→        if cycle_just_completed and has_real_items:
   316→            # Post-cycle: front-of-queue after promoted items so subjective
   317→            # review happens before the new objective cycle begins.
   318→            insert_at = _after_promoted(order, plan)
   319→            for sid in reversed(sorted(injectable_ids)):
   320→                if sid not in existing:
   321→                    order.insert(insert_at, sid)
   322→                    result.injected.append(sid)
   323→        else:
   324→            # Mid-cycle or no objective backlog: append to back.
   325→            for sid in sorted(injectable_ids):
   326→                if sid not in existing:
   327→                    order.append(sid)
   328→                    result.injected.append(sid)
   329→
   330→    return result
   331→
   332→
   333→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   334→# Triage snapshot hash + sync
   335→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   336→
   337→def review_issue_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
   338→    """Hash open review issue IDs to detect changes.
   339→
   340→    Returns empty string when there are no open review issues.
   341→    """
   342→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   343→    review_ids = sorted(
   344→        fid for fid, f in issues.items()
   345→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   346→        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   347→    )
   348→    if not review_ids:
   349→        return ""
   350→    return hashlib.sha256("|".join(review_ids).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
   351→
   352→
   353→@dataclass
   354→class TriageSyncResult:
   355→    """What changed during a triage sync."""
   356→
   357→    injected: bool = False
   358→    pruned: bool = False
   359→
   360→    @property
   361→    def changes(self) -> int:
   362→        return int(self.injected) + int(self.pruned)
   363→
   364→
   365→def sync_triage_needed(
   366→    plan: PlanModel,
   367→    state: StateModel,
   368→) -> TriageSyncResult:
   369→    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review issues change.
   370→
   371→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
   372→
   373→    When stages are already present but all new issues have been resolved
   374→    since injection, auto-prunes the stale stages and updates the hash.
   375→
   376→    When issues are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   377→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   378→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   379→    """
   380→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   381→    result = TriageSyncResult()
   382→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   383→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   384→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   385→
   386→    # Check if any triage stage is already in queue
   387→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   388→
   389→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   390→    last_hash = meta.get("issue_snapshot_hash", "")
   391→
   392→    if already_present:
   393→        # Stages present — check if the reason for injection still applies.
   394→        # Only auto-prune when triage was completed before (hash exists),
   395→        # all new issues have been resolved, and no triage work is in
   396→        # progress.  This avoids pruning the initial triage or a
   397→        # user-started triage session.
   398→        if last_hash and not confirmed:
   399→            issues = state.get("issues", {})
   400→            current_review_ids = {
   401→                fid for fid, f in issues.items()
   402→                if f.get("status") == "open"
   403→                and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   404→            }
   405→            triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   406→            new_since_triage = current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   407→
   408→            if not new_since_triage:
   409→                # No new issues remain — prune stale stages
   410→                for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
   411→                    while sid in order:
   412→                        order.remove(sid)
   413→                if current_hash:
   414→                    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   415→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   416→                result.pruned = True
   417→        return result
   418→
   419→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash:
   420→        # Distinguish "new issues appeared" from "issues were resolved".
   421→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new issues exist.
   422→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   423→        current_review_ids = {
   424→            fid for fid, f in issues.items()
   425→            if f.get("status") == "open"
   426→            and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   427→        }
   428→        triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   429→        new_since_triage = current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   430→
   431→        if new_since_triage:
   432→            # New review issues appeared — re-triage needed
   433→            insert_at = _after_promoted(order, plan)
   434→            stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit")
   435→            existing = set(order)
   436→            injected_count = 0
   437→            for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names):
   438→                if name not in confirmed and sid not in existing:
   439→                    order.insert(insert_at + injected_count, sid)
   440→                    injected_count += 1
   441→            if injected_count:
   442→                result.injected = True
   443→        else:
   444→            # Only resolved issues changed the hash — update silently
   445→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   446→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   447→
   448→    return result
   449→

   451→@dataclass
   452→class ScoreCheckpointSyncResult:
   453→    """What changed during a score-checkpoint sync."""
   454→
   455→    injected: bool = False
   456→
   457→    @property
   458→    def changes(self) -> int:
   459→        return int(self.injected)
   460→
   461→
   462→def sync_score_checkpoint_needed(
   463→    plan: PlanModel,
   464→    state: StateModel,
   465→    *,
   466→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   467→) -> ScoreCheckpointSyncResult:
   468→    """Inject ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` when all initial reviews complete.
   469→
   470→    Injects when:
   471→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   472→    - ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` is not already in the queue
   473→
   474→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan
   475→    so the user sees their updated strict score right after reviews finish.
   476→    """
   477→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   478→    result = ScoreCheckpointSyncResult()
   479→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   480→
   481→    if WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   482→        return result
   483→
   484→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   485→    if policy is not None:
   486→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   487→            return result
   488→    else:
   489→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   490→        if unscored:
   491→            return result
   492→
   493→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   494→    insert_at = 0
   495→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   496→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   497→            insert_at = i + 1
   498→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID)
   499→    result.injected = True
   500→    return result

   503→@dataclass
   504→class CreatePlanSyncResult:
   505→    """What changed during a create-plan sync."""
   506→
   507→    injected: bool = False
   508→
   509→    @property
   510→    def changes(self) -> int:
   511→        return int(self.injected)
   512→
   513→
   514→def sync_create_plan_needed(
   515→    plan: PlanModel,
   516→    state: StateModel,
   517→    *,
   518→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   519→) -> CreatePlanSyncResult:
   520→    """Inject ``workflow::create-plan`` when reviews complete + objective backlog exists.
   521→
   522→    Only injects when:
   523→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   524→    - At least one objective issue exists
   525→    - ``workflow::create-plan`` is not already in the queue
   526→    - No triage stages are pending
   527→    """
   528→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   529→    result = CreatePlanSyncResult()
   530→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   531→
   532→    if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID in order:
   533→        return result
   534→
   535→    # Don't inject if triage stages are pending
   536→    if any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS):
   537→        return result
   538→
   539→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   540→    if policy is not None:
   541→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   542→            return result
   543→        has_objective = policy.has_objective_backlog
   544→    else:
   545→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   546→        if unscored:
   547→            return result
   548→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   549→        has_objective = any(
   550→            f.get("status") == "open"
   551→            and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   552→            for f in issues.values()
   553→        )
   554→    if not has_objective:
   555→        return result
   556→
   557→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items, at the end of the
   558→    # synthetic block (so create-plan comes after score-checkpoint).
   559→    insert_at = 0
   560→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   561→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(TRIAGE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   562→            insert_at = i + 1
   563→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)
   564→    result.injected = True
   565→    return result
   566→
   567→
   568→def compute_new_issue_ids(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   569→    """Return the set of open review/concerns issue IDs added since last triage.
   570→
   571→    Returns an empty set when no prior triage has recorded ``triaged_ids``.
   572→    """
   573→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   574→    triaged = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", meta.get("synthesized_ids", [])))
   575→    current = {
   576→        fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   577→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   578→    }
   579→    return current - triaged if triaged else set()
   580→
   581→
   582→def is_triage_stale(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> bool:
   583→    """Side-effect-free check: is triage needed?
   584→
   585→    Returns True when genuinely *new* review issues appeared since the
   586→    last triage.  Triage stage IDs being in the queue alone is not
   587→    sufficient — the new issues that triggered injection may have been
   588→    resolved since then.
   589→
   590→    When issues are merely resolved (current IDs are a subset of
   591→    previously triaged IDs), triage is NOT stale — the user is working
   592→    through the plan.
   593→    """
   594→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   595→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   596→
   597→    # Always check for genuinely new issues (same logic regardless of
   598→    # whether triage stages are in the queue).
   599→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   600→    current_review_ids = {
   601→        fid for fid, f in issues.items()
   602→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   603→        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   604→    }
   605→    triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   606→    new_since_triage = current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   607→    if new_since_triage:
   608→        return True
   609→
   610→    # If triage stages are in queue but there's in-progress triage work,
   611→    # still consider it stale so the user finishes what they started.
   612→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   613→    if confirmed:
   614→        order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   615→        if order & TRIAGE_IDS:
   616→            return True
   617→
   618→    return False

   632→def sync_import_scores_needed(
   633→    plan: PlanModel,
   634→    state: StateModel,
   635→    *,
   636→    assessment_mode: str | None = None,
   637→) -> ImportScoresSyncResult:
   638→    """Inject ``workflow::import-scores`` after issues-only import.
   639→
   640→    Only injects when:
   641→    - Assessment mode was ``issues_only`` (scores were skipped)
   642→    - ``workflow::import-scores`` is not already in the queue
   643→    - There are assessments in the payload that could be imported
   644→
   645→    Positioned after score-checkpoint, before create-plan.
   646→    """
   647→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   648→    result = ImportScoresSyncResult()
   649→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   650→
   651→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID in order:
   652→        return result
   653→
   654→    # Only inject when scores were skipped (issues-only mode)
   655→    if assessment_mode != "issues_only":
   656→        return result
   657→
   658→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items
   659→    insert_at = 0
   660→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   661→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   662→            insert_at = i + 1
   663→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID)
   664→    result.injected = True
   665→    return result

   668→@dataclass
   669→class CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   670→    """What changed during a communicate-score sync."""
   671→
   672→    injected: bool = False
   673→
   674→    @property
   675→    def changes(self) -> int:

   677→
   678→
   679→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   680→    plan: PlanModel,
   681→    state: StateModel,
   682→    *,
   683→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   684→    scores_just_imported: bool = False,
   685→) -> CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   686→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` when scores should be shown.
   687→
   688→    Injects when either:
   689→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dimensions), OR
   690→    - Scores were just imported (trusted/attested/override)
   691→
   692→    And ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue.
   693→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan.
   694→    """
   695→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   696→    result = CommunicateScoreSyncResult()
   697→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   698→
   699→    # Also treat legacy score-checkpoint as already-present
   700→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order or WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   701→        return result
   702→
   703→    # Trigger 1: scores just imported
   704→    should_inject = scores_just_imported
   705→
   706→    # Trigger 2: all initial reviews complete (no unscored dimensions)
   707→    if not should_inject:
   708→        if policy is not None:
   709→            should_inject = not policy.unscored_ids
   710→        else:
   711→            should_inject = not current_unscored_ids(state)
   712→
   713→    if not should_inject:
   714→        return result
   715→
   716→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   717→    insert_at = 0
   718→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   719→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   720→            insert_at = i + 1
   721→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   722→    result.injected = True
   723→    return result

     4→resolves contradictions, and orders by dependency. The triage is incremental:
     5→it updates existing triage-clusters rather than recreating from scratch.

    34→ISSUE_ID_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z_]+::[a-f0-9]{8,}")
    35→
    36→
    37→def extract_issue_citations(text: str, valid_ids: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    38→    """Extract issue IDs cited in free text.
    39→
    40→    Matches full issue IDs (e.g. ``review::abcdef12``) or bare 8+ char
    41→    hex suffixes that correspond to a known issue.
    42→    """
    43→    cited: set[str] = set()
    44→    # Match full issue IDs
    45→    for match in ISSUE_ID_RE.finditer(text):
    46→        candidate = match.group()
    47→        if candidate in valid_ids:
    48→            cited.add(candidate)
    49→    # Match 8+ char hex suffixes
    50→    for token in re.findall(r"[0-9a-f]{8,}", text):
    51→        for valid_id in valid_ids:
    52→            if valid_id.endswith("::" + token):
    53→                cited.add(valid_id)
    54→                break
    55→    return cited
    56→
    57→
    58→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    59→# Completed-work helpers

    61→
    62→def last_real_review_timestamp(state: dict) -> str | None:
    63→    """ISO timestamp of most recent genuine review import (not manual override/scan reset)."""
    64→    REAL_MODES = {"holistic", "per_file", "trusted_internal", "attested_external"}
    65→    audit = state.get("assessment_import_audit", [])
    66→    if isinstance(audit, list):
    67→        for entry in reversed(audit):
    68→            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("mode") in REAL_MODES:
    69→                ts = entry.get("timestamp")
    70→                if ts:
    71→                    return str(ts)
    72→    holistic = (state.get("review_cache") or {}).get("holistic")
    73→    if isinstance(holistic, dict):
    74→        return holistic.get("reviewed_at")
    75→    return None
    76→
    77→
    78→def detect_recurring_patterns(
    79→    open_issues: dict[str, dict],
    80→    resolved_issues: dict[str, dict],
    81→) -> dict[str, dict]:
    82→    """Detect dimensions with both resolved AND current open issues.
    83→
    84→    Returns ``{dimension: {"open": [ids], "resolved": [ids]}}``.
    85→    A dimension with both resolved and open issues signals a potential
    86→    loop — similar issues recur after previous fixes.
    87→    """
    88→    def _dimension(f: dict) -> str:
    89→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
    90→        if isinstance(detail, dict):
    91→            return detail.get("dimension", "")
    92→        return ""
    93→
    94→    open_by_dim: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    95→    for fid, f in open_issues.items():
    96→        dim = _dimension(f)
    97→        if dim:
    98→            open_by_dim.setdefault(dim, []).append(fid)
    99→
   100→    resolved_by_dim: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   101→    for fid, f in resolved_issues.items():
   102→        dim = _dimension(f)
   103→        if dim:
   104→            resolved_by_dim.setdefault(dim, []).append(fid)
   105→
   106→    recurring: dict[str, dict] = {}
   107→    for dim in set(open_by_dim) & set(resolved_by_dim):
   108→        recurring[dim] = {
   109→            "open": open_by_dim[dim],
   110→            "resolved": resolved_by_dim[dim],
   111→        }
   112→    return recurring

     8→from desloppify.core.registry import DETECTORS, DetectorMeta

    21→
    22→AUTO_PREFIX = "auto/"
    23→_MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE = 2
    24→_STALE_KEY = "subjective::stale"
    25→_STALE_NAME = "auto/stale-review"
    26→_UNSCORED_KEY = "subjective::unscored"
    27→_UNSCORED_NAME = "auto/initial-review"
    28→_UNDER_TARGET_KEY = "subjective::under-target"
    29→_UNDER_TARGET_NAME = "auto/under-target-review"
    30→_MIN_UNSCORED_CLUSTER_SIZE = 1
    31→
    32→
    33→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    34→# Grouping key computation
    35→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    36→
    37→def _extract_subtype(issue: dict) -> str | None:
    38→    """Extract the subtype/kind from a issue.
    39→
    40→    Checks detail.kind first, then falls back to parsing the issue ID
    41→    (format: ``detector::file::subtype`` or ``detector::file::symbol::subtype``).
    42→    """
    43→    detail = issue.get("detail") or {}
    44→    kind = detail.get("kind")
    45→    if kind:
    46→        return kind
    47→
    48→    # Parse from issue ID — third segment is often the subtype
    49→    fid = issue.get("id", "")
    50→    parts = fid.split("::")
    51→    if len(parts) >= 3:
    52→        # For IDs like smells::file.py::silent_except, the subtype is parts[2]
    53→        # For IDs like dict_keys::file.py::key::phantom_read, subtype is last part
    54→        candidate = parts[-1]
    55→        # Skip if it looks like a file path or symbol name (contains / or .)
    56→        if "/" not in candidate and "." not in candidate:
    57→            return candidate
    58→    return None
    59→
    60→
    61→def _grouping_key(issue: dict, meta: DetectorMeta | None) -> str | None:
    62→    """Compute a deterministic grouping key for a issue.
    63→
    64→    Returns None if the issue should not be auto-clustered.
    65→    """
    66→    detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    67→
    68→    if meta is None:
    69→        # Unknown detector — group by detector name
    70→        return f"detector::{detector}"
    71→
    72→    # Review issues → group by dimension
    73→    if detector in ("review", "subjective_review"):
    74→        detail = issue.get("detail") or {}
    75→        dimension = detail.get("dimension", "")
    76→        if dimension:
    77→            return f"review::{dimension}"
    78→        return f"detector::{detector}"
    79→
    80→    # Per-file detectors (structural, responsibility_cohesion)
    81→    if meta.needs_judgment and detector in (
    82→        "structural", "responsibility_cohesion",
    83→    ):
    84→        file = issue.get("file", "")
    85→        if file:
    86→            basename = os.path.basename(file)
    87→            return f"file::{detector}::{basename}"
    88→
    89→    # Needs-judgment detectors — group by subtype when available
    90→    if meta.needs_judgment:
    91→        subtype = _extract_subtype(issue)
    92→        if subtype:
    93→            return f"typed::{detector}::{subtype}"
    94→
    95→    # Pure auto-fix (no judgment needed) → all issues by detector
    96→    if meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and not meta.needs_judgment:
    97→        return f"auto::{detector}"
    98→
    99→    # Everything else → by detector
   100→    return f"detector::{detector}"
   101→
   102→
   103→def _cluster_name_from_key(key: str) -> str:
   104→    """Convert a grouping key to a cluster name with auto/ prefix."""
   105→    # auto::unused → auto/unused
   106→    # typed::dict_keys::phantom_read → auto/dict_keys-phantom_read
   107→    # file::structural::big_file.py → auto/structural-big_file.py
   108→    # review::abstraction_fitness → auto/review-abstraction_fitness
   109→    # detector::security → auto/security
   110→    parts = key.split("::")
   111→    if len(parts) == 2:
   112→        prefix_type = parts[0]
   113→        # For review keys, keep the prefix for clarity
   114→        if prefix_type == "review":
   115→            return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}review-{parts[1]}"
   116→        return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}{parts[1]}"
   117→    if len(parts) == 3:
   118→        return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}{parts[1]}-{parts[2]}"
   119→    return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}{key.replace('::', '-')}"
   120→
   121→
   122→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   123→# Description and action generation
   124→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   125→
   126→def _generate_description(
   127→    cluster_name: str,
   128→    members: list[dict],
   129→    meta: DetectorMeta | None,
   130→    subtype: str | None,
   131→) -> str:
   132→    """Generate a human-readable cluster description."""
   133→    count = len(members)
   134→    detector = members[0].get("detector", "") if members else ""
   135→
   136→    if detector in ("review", "subjective_review"):
   137→        detail = (members[0].get("detail") or {}) if members else {}
   138→        dimension = detail.get("dimension", detector)
   139→        return f"Address {count} {dimension} review issues"
   140→
   141→    if detector == "structural":
   142→        files = {os.path.basename(m.get("file", "")) for m in members}
   143→        if len(files) == 1:
   144→            return f"Decompose {next(iter(files))}"
   145→        return f"Decompose {count} large files"
   146→
   147→    display = meta.display if meta else detector
   148→    if subtype:
   149→        label = subtype.replace("_", " ")
   150→        return f"Fix {count} {label} issues"

    42→from desloppify.state import StateModel
    43→
    44→# Sentinel: "read scan_path from state" (the safe default).
    45→# Callers that want to override can pass an explicit str or None.
    46→_SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE = object()
    47→
    48→
    49→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    50→class QueueBuildOptions:
    51→    """Configuration for queue construction.
    52→
    53→    ``scan_path`` defaults to reading from ``state["scan_path"]`` so callers
    54→    don't need to thread it manually.  Pass an explicit ``str`` or ``None``
    55→    to override (``None`` disables scope filtering).
    56→    """
    57→
    58→    # Output control
    59→    count: int | None = 1
    60→    explain: bool = False
    61→
    62→    # Scope filtering
    63→    scan_path: str | None | object = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
    64→    scope: str | None = None
    65→    status: str = "open"
    66→    chronic: bool = False
    67→
    68→    # Subjective gating
    69→    include_subjective: bool = True
    70→    subjective_threshold: float = 100.0
    71→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None
    72→
    73→    # Plan integration
    74→    plan: dict | None = None
    75→    include_skipped: bool = False
    76→    cluster: str | None = None
    77→
    78→    # Pre-computed context (overrides plan/policy)
    79→    context: QueueContext | None = None
    80→
    81→
    82→class WorkQueueResult(TypedDict):
    83→    """Typed shape of the dict returned by :func:`build_work_queue`."""
    84→
    85→    items: list[dict]
    86→    total: int
    87→    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]]
    88→    new_ids: set[str]
    89→
    90→
    91→def build_work_queue(
    92→    state: StateModel,
    93→    *,
    94→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
    95→) -> WorkQueueResult:
    96→    """Build a ranked work queue from state issues.
    97→
    98→    Pipeline:
    99→    1. Gather — issue items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
   100→    2. Score  — estimate impact from dimension headroom, apply floor
   101→    3. Order  — stamp plan positions, sort, filter to cluster focus
   102→    4. Limit  — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   103→    """
   104→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   105→    plan, scan_path, status, threshold = _resolve_inputs(opts, state)
   106→
   107→    # 1. Gather
   108→    items = build_issue_items(
   109→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   110→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,
   111→    )
   112→    items += _gather_subjective_items(state, opts, plan, threshold)
   113→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)
   114→
   115→    # 2. Score & filter
   116→    enrich_with_impact(items, state.get("dimension_scores", {}))
   117→    items = [i for i in items if _passes_impact_floor(i)]
   118→
   119→    # 3. Plan-aware ordering
   120→    new_ids, skipped = _plan_presort(items, state, plan)
   121→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   122→    _plan_postsort(items, skipped, plan, opts)
   123→
   124→    # 4. Finalize
   125→    if not items:
   126→        items += _empty_queue_fallback(plan)
   127→    total = len(items)
   128→    if opts.count is not None and opts.count > 0:
   129→        items = items[:opts.count]
   130→    if opts.explain:
   131→        for item in items:
   132→            item["explain"] = item_explain(item)
   133→
   134→    return {
   135→        "items": items,
   136→        "total": total,
   137→        "grouped": group_queue_items(items, "item"),
   138→        "new_ids": new_ids,
   139→    }
   140→
   141→
   142→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   143→# Pipeline helpers (private to this module)
   144→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   145→
   146→
   147→def _resolve_inputs(
   148→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   149→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   150→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   151→    ctx = opts.context
   152→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   153→
   154→    scan_path: str | None = (
   155→        state.get("scan_path")
   156→        if opts.scan_path is _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
   157→        else opts.scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]
   158→    )
   159→
   160→    status = opts.status
   161→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   162→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   163→
   164→    try:
   165→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   166→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   167→        threshold = 100.0
   168→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   169→
   170→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold
   171→
   172→
   173→def _gather_subjective_items(
   174→    state: StateModel,
   175→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   176→    plan: dict | None,
   177→    threshold: float,
   178→) -> list[dict]:
   179→    """Build synthetic subjective items, gated by SubjectiveVisibility policy."""
   180→    if not opts.include_subjective:
   181→        return []
   182→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:
   183→        return []
   184→    if opts.chronic:
   185→        return []
   186→
   187→    ctx = opts.context
   188→    policy = (
   189→        (ctx.policy if ctx is not None else None)
   190→        or opts.policy
   191→        or compute_subjective_visibility(state, plan=plan)
   192→    )
   193→
   194→    candidates = build_subjective_items(
   195→        state, state.get("issues", {}), threshold=threshold,
   196→    )
   197→
   198→    # When a plan explicitly includes a subjective item in queue_order,
   199→    # surface it regardless of policy — the plan is authoritative.
   200→    plan_queue_set: set[str] = (
   201→        set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   202→        if plan
   203→        else set()
   204→    )
   205→
   206→    result: list[dict] = []
   207→    for item in candidates:
   208→        if not scope_matches(item, opts.scope):
   209→            continue
   210→        item_id = item.get("id", "")
   211→        if not policy.should_surface(item) and item_id not in plan_queue_set:
   212→            continue
   213→        result.append(item)
   214→    return result
   215→

   217→def _gather_workflow_items(
   218→    state: StateModel, plan: dict | None, status: str,
   219→) -> list[dict]:
   220→    """Inject triage stages, checkpoints, and create-plan when plan is active."""
   221→    if not plan or status not in {"open", "all"}:

   223→
   224→    items: list[dict] = list(build_triage_stage_items(plan, state))
   225→    for builder in (
   226→        build_score_checkpoint_item,
   227→        build_import_scores_item,
   228→        build_communicate_score_item,
   229→    ):
   230→        item = builder(plan, state)
   231→        if item is not None:
   232→            items.append(item)
   233→    plan_item = build_create_plan_item(plan)
   234→    if plan_item is not None:
   235→        items.append(plan_item)
   236→    return items

   239→_MIN_STANDALONE_IMPACT = 0.05

   241→
   242→def _passes_impact_floor(item: dict) -> bool:
   243→    """Return True if item should survive the impact floor filter."""
   244→    if item.get("kind") != "issue":
   245→        return True
   246→    if item.get("is_review") or item.get("is_subjective"):
   247→        return True
   248→    impact = item.get("estimated_impact")
   249→    return not impact or impact >= _MIN_STANDALONE_IMPACT
   250→

   252→def _plan_presort(
   253→    items: list[dict], state: StateModel, plan: dict | None,
   254→) -> tuple[set[str], list[dict]]:
   255→    """Enrich plan metadata and stamp sort keys before sorting.
   256→
   257→    Returns ``(new_ids, skipped)`` — skipped items are removed from
   258→    ``items`` in place and returned separately for post-sort re-append.
   259→    """
   260→    if not plan:
   261→        return set(), []
   262→
   263→    new_ids = _new_item_ids(state)
   264→    enrich_plan_metadata(items, plan)
   265→    stamp_plan_sort_keys(items, plan, new_ids)
   266→    remaining, skipped = separate_skipped(items, plan)
   267→    items[:] = remaining
   268→    return new_ids, skipped

   272→    items: list[dict],

   276→) -> None:
   277→    """Re-append skipped items, stamp positions, filter to cluster focus."""
   278→    if not plan:
   279→        return
   280→
   281→    if opts.include_skipped:
   282→        items.extend(skipped)
   283→    stamp_positions(items, plan)
   284→    focused = filter_cluster_focus(items, plan, opts.cluster)
   285→    items[:] = focused

   288→def _empty_queue_fallback(plan: dict | None) -> list[dict]:
   289→    """Return a 'run scan' nudge when an active plan cycle has cleared."""
   290→    if not plan:

   292→    plan_scores = plan.get("plan_start_scores", {})
   293→    if plan_scores.get("strict") is None:
   294→        return []
   295→    return [{

   151→def _get_detail(issue: dict, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   152→    detail = issue.get("detail", {})
   153→    if not isinstance(detail, dict):

   158→def _get_signals(issue: dict) -> dict:
   159→    """Return the metrics dict for a issue.
   160→
   161→    Structural issues store metrics directly in ``detail`` (e.g. ``loc``,
   162→    ``complexity_score``).  Fall back to ``detail`` itself when the nested
   163→    ``signals`` key is absent so hotspot aggregation sees real values.
   164→    """
   165→    detail = issue.get("detail", {})
   166→    if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   167→        return {}
   168→    signals = detail.get("signals")
   169→    if isinstance(signals, dict):
   170→        return signals
   171→    return detail
   172→

   174→def _safe_num(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
   175→    if isinstance(value, bool):
   176→        return default
   177→    if isinstance(value, int | float):
   178→        return float(value)
   179→    return default
