    52→def _validate_fixed_note(args: argparse.Namespace) -> bool:
    53→    if args.status != "fixed":
    54→        return True
    55→    note = getattr(args, "note", None)
    56→    if validate_note_length(note):
    57→        return True
    58→    show_note_length_requirement(note)
    59→    return False
    60→
    61→
    62→def _update_living_plan_after_resolve(
    63→    *,
    64→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    65→    all_resolved: list[str],
    66→    attestation: str | None,
    67→) -> dict | None:
    68→    plan = None
    69→    try:
    70→        if not has_living_plan():
    71→            return None
    72→        plan = load_plan()
    73→        purged = purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)
    74→        append_log_entry(
    75→            plan,
    76→            "resolve",
    77→            issue_ids=all_resolved,
    78→            actor="user",
    79→            note=getattr(args, "note", None),
    80→            detail={"status": args.status, "attestation": attestation},
    81→        )
    82→        # Commit tracking: add to uncommitted on fix, remove on reopen
    83→        if args.status == "fixed":
    84→            add_uncommitted_issues(plan, all_resolved)
    85→        elif args.status == "open":
    86→            purge_uncommitted_ids(plan, all_resolved)
    87→        save_plan(plan)
    88→        if purged:
    89→            print(colorize(f"  Plan updated: {purged} item(s) removed from queue.", "dim"))
    90→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    91→        _logger.debug("plan update failed after resolve", exc_info=True)
    92→        print(colorize("  Warning: could not update living plan.", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
    93→    return plan
    94→
    95→
    96→def cmd_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    97→    """Resolve issue(s) matching one or more patterns."""
    98→    attestation = getattr(args, "attest", None)
    99→    _validate_resolve_inputs(args, attestation)
   100→    if not _validate_fixed_note(args):
   101→        return
   102→
   103→    state_file = state_path(args)
   104→    state = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   105→
   106→    if _check_queue_order_guard(state, args.patterns, args.status):
   107→        return
   108→
   109→    if args.status == "fixed":
   110→        require_triage_current_or_exit(
   111→            state=state,
   112→            bypass=bool(getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)),
   113→            attest=getattr(args, "attest", "") or "",
   114→        )
   115→
   116→    _enforce_batch_wontfix_confirmation(
   117→        state,
   118→        args,
   119→        attestation=attestation,
   120→        resolve_all_patterns_fn=_resolve_all_patterns,
   121→    )
   122→    prev = _previous_score_snapshot(state)
   123→    prev_subjective_scores = {
   124→        str(dim): (coerce_assessment_score(payload) or 0.0)
   125→        for dim, payload in (state.get("subjective_assessments") or {}).items()
   126→        if isinstance(dim, str)
   127→    }
   128→
   129→    all_resolved = _resolve_all_patterns(state, args, attestation=attestation)
   130→    if not all_resolved:
   131→        status_label = "resolved" if args.status == "open" else "open"
   132→        print(colorize(f"No {status_label} issues matching: {' '.join(args.patterns)}", "yellow"))
   133→        return
   134→
   135→    _save_state_or_exit(state, state_file)
   136→
   137→    plan = _update_living_plan_after_resolve(
   138→        args=args,
   139→        all_resolved=all_resolved,
   140→        attestation=attestation,
   141→    )
   142→
   143→    _print_resolve_summary(status=args.status, all_resolved=all_resolved)
   144→    _print_wontfix_batch_warning(
   145→        state,
   146→        status=args.status,
   147→        resolved_count=len(all_resolved),
   148→    )
   149→    show_score_with_plan_context(state, prev)
   150→    render_commit_guidance(state, plan, all_resolved, args.status)
   151→    _print_subjective_reset_hint(
   152→        args=args,
   153→        state=state,
   154→        all_resolved=all_resolved,
   155→        prev_subjective_scores=prev_subjective_scores,
   156→    )
   157→
   158→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   159→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   160→    narrative = narrative_mod.compute_narrative(
   161→        state,
   162→        context=narrative_mod.NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="resolve"),
   163→    )
   164→    if narrative.get("milestone"):
   165→        print(colorize(f"  → {narrative['milestone']}", "green"))
   166→
   167→    next_command = _print_next_command(state)
   168→    _write_resolve_query_entry(
   169→        ResolveQueryContext(
   170→            patterns=args.patterns,
   171→            status=args.status,
   172→            resolved=all_resolved,
   173→            next_command=next_command,
   174→            prev_overall=prev.overall,
   175→            prev_objective=prev.objective,
   176→            prev_strict=prev.strict,
   177→            prev_verified=prev.verified,
   178→            attestation=attestation,
   179→            narrative=narrative,
   180→            state=state,
   181→        )
   182→    )
   183→

  "command": "python3 -c \"\nimport ast, os, sys\n\nroot = [REDACTED]\nresults = []\n\nfor dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):\n    if '__pycache__' in dirpath:\n        continue\n    for fname in filenames:\n        if fname != '__init__.py':\n            continue\n        fpath = os.path.join(dirpath, fname)\n        try:\n            src = open(fpath).read()\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n        try:\n            tree = ast.parse(src)\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n\n        has_from_import = any(isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) for n in ast.walk(tree))\n        has_all = any(\n            isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and any(\n                isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == '__all__'\n                for t in n.targets\n            )\n            for n in ast.walk(tree)\n        )\n\n        if has_from_import and not has_all:\n            # collect the from-import names\n            imports = []\n            for node in ast.walk(tree):\n                if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):\n                    names = [a.asname or a.name for a in node.names]\n                    imports.append(f'from {node.module} import {names}')\n            rel = fpath[len(root):]\n            results.append((rel, imports))\n\nfor rel, imps in sorted(results):\n    print(f'FILE: {rel}')\n    for i in imps:\n        print(f'  {i}')\n    print()\n\"\n",
  "description": "Find all __init__.py files with from-imports but no __all__"
}

1→"""Dict key flow analysis — detect dead writes, phantom reads, typos, and schema drift."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations

     5→import ast
     6→import importlib
     7→import logging
     8→from collections import defaultdict
     9→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    10→from pathlib import Path

    12→from desloppify.core.text.text_api import PROJECT_ROOT

    17→# ── Data structures ───────────────────────────────────────
    18→
    19→
    20→@dataclass
    21→class TrackedDict:
    22→    """A dict variable tracked within a single scope."""
    23→
    24→    name: str
    25→    created_line: int
    26→    locally_created: bool
    27→    returned_or_passed: bool = False
    28→    has_dynamic_key: bool = False
    29→    has_star_unpack: bool = False
    30→    writes: dict[str, list[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(list))
    31→    reads: dict[str, list[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(list))
    32→    bulk_read: bool = False  # .keys(), .values(), .items(), for x in d
    33→
    34→
    35→# Variable name patterns that suppress dead-write warnings
    36→_CONFIG_NAMES = {
    37→    "config",
    38→    "settings",
    39→    "defaults",
    40→    "options",
    41→    "kwargs",
    42→    "context",
    43→    "ctx",
    44→    "env",
    45→    "params",
    46→    "metadata",
    47→    "headers",
    48→    "attrs",
    49→    "attributes",
    50→    "props",
    51→    "properties",
    52→}
    53→
    54→# Dict method → effect
    55→_READ_METHODS = {"get", "pop", "setdefault", "__getitem__", "__contains__"}
    56→_WRITE_METHODS = {"update", "setdefault", "__setitem__"}
    57→_BULK_READ_METHODS = {"keys", "values", "items", "copy", "__iter__"}
    58→
    59→
    60→def _levenshtein(s1: str, s2: str) -> int:
    61→    """Compute Levenshtein edit distance between two strings."""
    62→    if len(s1) < len(s2):
    63→        return _levenshtein(s2, s1)
    64→    if len(s2) == 0:
    65→        return len(s1)
    66→    prev = list(range(len(s2) + 1))
    67→    for i, c1 in enumerate(s1):
    68→        curr = [i + 1]
    69→        for j, c2 in enumerate(s2):
    70→            cost = 0 if c1 == c2 else 1
    71→            curr.append(min(curr[j] + 1, prev[j + 1] + 1, prev[j] + cost))
    72→        prev = curr
    73→    return prev[-1]
    74→
    75→
    76→def _is_singular_plural(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    77→    """Check if a and b are singular/plural variants of each other."""
    78→    return (
    79→        a + "s" == b
    80→        or b + "s" == a
    81→        or a + "es" == b
    82→        or b + "es" == a
    83→        or (a.endswith("ies") and a[:-3] + "y" == b)
    84→        or (b.endswith("ies") and b[:-3] + "y" == a)
    85→    )
    86→
    87→
    88→# ── AST Visitor ───────────────────────────────────────────
    89→
    90→
    91→def _load_dict_key_visitor():
    92→    module = importlib.import_module(".visitor", package=__package__)
    93→    return module.DictKeyVisitor
    94→
    95→
    96→def _get_name(node: ast.expr) -> str | None:
    97→    """Extract variable name from a Name or Attribute(self.x) node."""
    98→    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
    99→        return node.id
   100→    return (
   101→        f"{node.value.id}.{node.attr}"
   102→        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name)
   103→        else None
   104→    )
   105→
   106→
   107→def _get_str_key(node: ast.expr) -> str | None:
   108→    """Extract a string literal from a subscript slice."""
   109→    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str):
   110→        return node.value
   111→    return None
   112→
   113→
   114→# ── Pass 1: Single-scope dict key analysis ────────────────
   115→
   116→
   117→def detect_dict_key_flow(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   118→    """Walk all .py files, run DictKeyVisitor. Returns (entries, files_checked)."""
   119→    dict_key_visitor = _load_dict_key_visitor()
   120→    files = find_py_files(path)
   121→    all_issues: list[dict] = []
   122→    all_literals: list[dict] = []
   123→
   124→    for filepath in files:
   125→        try:
   126→            p = (
   127→                Path(filepath)
   128→                if Path(filepath).is_absolute()
   129→                else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
   130→            )
   131→            source = p.read_text()
   132→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   133→            logger.debug(
   134→                "Skipping unreadable python file %s in dict-key pass: %s", filepath, exc
   135→            )
   136→            continue
   137→
   138→        try:
   139→            tree = ast.parse(source, filename=filepath)
   140→        except SyntaxError as exc:
   141→            logger.debug(
   142→                "Skipping unparseable python file %s in dict-key pass: %s",
   143→                filepath,
   144→                exc,
   145→            )
   146→            continue
   147→
   148→        visitor = dict_key_visitor(filepath)
   149→        visitor.visit(tree)
   150→        all_issues.extend(visitor._issues)
   151→        all_literals.extend(visitor._dict_literals)
   152→
   153→    return all_issues, len(files)
   154→
   155→
   156→# ── Pass 2: Schema drift clustering ──────────────────────
   157→
   158→
   159→def _jaccard(a: frozenset, b: frozenset) -> float:
   160→    if not a and not b:
   161→        return 1.0
   162→    return len(a & b) / len(a | b)
   163→
   164→
   165→def _read_python_file(filepath: str, *, path: Path) -> str | None:
   166→    try:
   167→        file_path = (
   168→            Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
   169→        )
   170→        return file_path.read_text()
   171→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   172→        logger.debug(
   173→            "Skipping unreadable python file %s in schema-drift pass: %s", filepath, exc
   174→        )
   175→        return None
   176→
   177→
   178→def _parse_python_ast(source: str, *, filepath: str) -> ast.AST | None:
   179→    try:
   180→        return ast.parse(source, filename=filepath)
   181→    except SyntaxError as exc:
   182→        logger.debug(
   183→            "Skipping unparseable python file %s in schema-drift pass: %s",
   184→            filepath,
   185→            exc,
   186→        )
   187→        return None
   188→
   189→
   190→def _extract_literal_keyset(node: ast.Dict) -> frozenset[str] | None:
   191→    if len(node.keys) < 3:
   192→        return None
   193→    if any(key is None for key in node.keys):
   194→        return None  # Has **spread
   195→    literal_keys: list[str] = []
   196→    for key in node.keys:
   197→        if key is None:
   198→            continue
   199→        if not isinstance(key, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(key.value, str):
   200→            return None
   201→        literal_keys.append(key.value)
   202→    return frozenset(literal_keys)
   203→
   204→
   205→def _collect_schema_literals(path: Path, files: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
   206→    literals: list[dict] = []
   207→    for filepath in files:
   208→        source = _read_python_file(filepath, path=path)
   209→        if source is None:
   210→            continue
   211→        tree = _parse_python_ast(source, filepath=filepath)
   212→        if tree is None:
   213→            continue
   214→
   215→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   216→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Dict):
   217→                continue
   218→            keyset = _extract_literal_keyset(node)
   219→            if keyset is None:
   220→                continue
   221→            literals.append({"file": filepath, "line": node.lineno, "keys": keyset})
   222→    return literals
   223→
   224→
   225→def _cluster_by_jaccard(
   226→    literals: list[dict], *, threshold: float = 0.8
   227→) -> list[list[dict]]:
   228→    """Greedy single-linkage clustering by Jaccard similarity threshold."""
   229→    clusters: list[list[dict]] = []
   230→    assigned = [False] * len(literals)
   231→
   232→    for index, literal in enumerate(literals):
   233→        if assigned[index]:
   234→            continue
   235→        cluster = [literal]
   236→        assigned[index] = True
   237→        for probe_idx in range(index + 1, len(literals)):
   238→            if assigned[probe_idx]:
   239→                continue
   240→            candidate = literals[probe_idx]
   241→            if any(
   242→                _jaccard(member["keys"], candidate["keys"]) >= threshold
   243→                for member in cluster
   244→            ):
   245→                cluster.append(candidate)
   246→                assigned[probe_idx] = True
   247→        clusters.append(cluster)
   248→
   249→    return clusters
   250→
   251→
   252→def _cluster_key_frequency(cluster: list[dict]) -> dict[str, int]:
   253→    freq: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   254→    for member in cluster:
   255→        for key in member["keys"]:
   256→            freq[key] += 1
   257→    return freq
   258→
   259→
   260→def _closest_consensus_key(outlier_key: str, consensus: set[str]) -> str | None:
   261→    for consensus_key in consensus:
   262→        distance = _levenshtein(outlier_key, consensus_key)
   263→        if distance <= 2 or _is_singular_plural(outlier_key, consensus_key):
   264→            return consensus_key
   265→    return None
   266→
   267→
   268→def _build_schema_drift_issues(clusters: list[list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   269→    issues: list[dict] = []
   270→    for cluster in clusters:
   271→        if len(cluster) < 3:
   272→            continue
   273→
   274→        key_freq = _cluster_key_frequency(cluster)
   275→        threshold = 0.3 * len(cluster)
   276→        consensus = {key for key, count in key_freq.items() if count >= threshold}
   277→
   278→        for member in cluster:
   279→            outlier_keys = member["keys"] - consensus
   280→            for outlier_key in outlier_keys:
   281→                close_match = _closest_consensus_key(outlier_key, consensus)
   282→                present = key_freq[outlier_key]
   283→                tier = 2 if len(cluster) >= 5 else 3
   284→                confidence = "high" if len(cluster) >= 5 else "medium"
   285→                suggestion = f' Did you mean "{close_match}"?' if close_match else ""
   286→                issues.append(
   287→                    {
   288→                        "file": member["file"],
   289→                        "kind": "schema_drift",
   290→                        "key": outlier_key,
   291→                        "line": member["line"],
   292→                        "tier": tier,
   293→                        "confidence": confidence,
   294→                        "summary": (
   295→                            f"Schema drift: {len(cluster) - present}/{len(cluster)} dict literals use different "
   296→                            f'key, but {member["file"]}:{member["line"]} uses "{outlier_key}".{suggestion}'
   297→                        ),
   298→                        "detail": (
   299→                            f'Cluster of {len(cluster)} similar dict literals. Key "{outlier_key}" appears in '
   300→                            f"only {present}. Consensus keys: {sorted(consensus)}"
   301→                        ),
   302→                    }
   303→                )
   304→    return issues
   305→
   306→
   307→def detect_schema_drift(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   308→    """Cluster dict literals by key similarity, report outlier keys.
   309→
   310→    Returns (entries, literals_checked).
   311→    """
   312→    files = find_py_files(path)
   313→    all_literals = _collect_schema_literals(path, files)
   314→
   315→    if len(all_literals) < 3:
   316→        return [], len(all_literals)
   317→
   318→    clusters = _cluster_by_jaccard(all_literals, threshold=0.8)
   319→    issues = _build_schema_drift_issues(clusters)
   320→
   321→    return issues, len(all_literals)
   322→

## 1. scan_reporting duplication — which copy is canonical?

The relationship is a clean delegation, not a duplication:

**`scan_reporting_presentation.py` is the canonical implementation.** It contains all actual logic with dependency-injected parameters (protocol stubs for `state_mod`, `narrative_mod`, `registry_mod`, and `colorize_fn`). This makes it unit-testable in isolation.

**`scan_reporting_dimensions.py` is the thin facade.** It imports from `scan_reporting_presentation` and wraps every call by supplying the concrete module dependencies:

```python
# scan_reporting_dimensions.py line 7
from . import scan_reporting_presentation as presentation_mod

def show_detector_progress(state: dict):
    return presentation_mod.show_detector_progress(
        state, state_mod=state_mod, narrative_mod=narrative_mod,
        registry_mod=registry_mod, colorize_fn=colorize,
    )

def show_score_model_breakdown(state, *, dim_scores=None):
    return presentation_mod.show_score_model_breakdown(
        state, scoring_mod=scoring_mod, colorize_fn=colorize, dim_scores=dim_scores,
    )

def show_dimension_deltas(prev, current):
    return presentation_mod.show_dimension_deltas(
        prev, current, scoring_mod=scoring_mod, colorize_fn=colorize,
    )

def show_low_dimension_hints(dim_scores):
    return presentation_mod.show_low_dimension_hints(
        dim_scores, scoring_mod=scoring_mod, colorize_fn=colorize,
    )
```

None of the four functions are duplicated — `scan_reporting_dimensions.py` delegates 100% to `scan_reporting_presentation.py`. The import direction is one-way: `dimensions` imports `presentation`, never the reverse.

---

## 2. Helper naming collision — `helpers.py` vs `shared.py` in `plan/triage/`

Both files exist. They serve **different purposes** and should not be merged:

**`helpers.py`** — Low-level triage business logic (pure functions):
- `_has_triage_in_queue`, `_inject_triage_stages`, `_purge_triage_stage`
- `_cascade_clear_later_confirmations`, `_print_cascade_clear_feedback`
- `_observe_dimension_breakdown`, `_open_review_ids_from_state`
- `_triage_coverage`, `_manual_clusters_with_issues`
- `_apply_completion` (the completion-state writer)
- `_find_cluster_for`, `_count_log_activity_since`

**`shared.py`** — A re-export compatibility shim. It has **no logic of its own** — it only re-exports names from four other submodules:
- From `progress_render`: `_print_progress`, `_print_stage_progress`
- From `reflect_dashboard`: `_print_reflect_dashboard`
- From `stage_helpers`: `_manual_clusters_with_issues`, `_require_triage_pending`, `_triage_coverage`, `_unenriched_clusters`, `_validate_stage_report`
- From `stage_persistence`: `record_triage_stage`, `refresh_stage_snapshot`

Note that `shared.py` re-exports `_manual_clusters_with_issues` and `_triage_coverage`, which are also defined directly in `helpers.py`. These appear to be maintained in parallel in `stage_helpers.py` as well. `shared.py` is a compatibility surface for callers that import from a single `shared` namespace; merging it into `helpers.py` would break those callers.

**Where logic lives by package:**
- `app/` — pure CLI surface: argument parsing, rendering, command entry points. No business logic.
- `core/` — wide flat package of shared utilities: config, registry, enums, discovery, output.
- `engine/` — all analysis logic: work queue, scoring, state persistence, detectors, plan operations.
- `intelligence/` — narrative coaching + LLM review preparation. Deepest sub-structure here.
- `languages/` — plugin system with `_framework/` base + 27 language directories (22 stubs, 5 full implementations: python, typescript, csharp, go, dart/gdscript partial).
- `tests/` — closely mirrors source structure; `tests/commands/` is the widest test directory at 47 files.

## 5. `git mv` / `next.py` → `next/` gotcha

This is a real filesystem constraint, not just a git quirk. The issue:

- On every OS filesystem, a file and a directory **cannot share the same name at the same path**. `next.py` is a file; `next/` is a directory — these are at different paths so there is no direct collision.
- The actual gotcha is different: `git mv next.py next/` fails if the directory `next/` does not yet exist. Git's `mv` is not `mkdir -p`; it requires the destination directory to already exist.
- The workflow you'd need:
  1. Rename `next.py` to a temporary name first (e.g., `git mv next.py next_cmd.py`) so the name `next` is free — **but this is only necessary if you want to create a directory also called `next` at the same level**. Since `next.py` has the `.py` extension, a directory `next/` (no extension) can coexist beside it with no conflict. On a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux), `next.py` and `next/` are completely distinct names. On macOS (case-insensitive by default), they are also distinct because `next.py != next`.
  2. Create the directory first: `mkdir desloppify/app/commands/next` and add an `__init__.py` (or git won't track the empty dir). Then `git mv next.py next/next.py` (or whatever the target name is).
- **Bottom line:** You do NOT need to rename `next.py` before creating a `next/` directory — the `.py` extension makes them unambiguously different names on all filesystems. The only real requirement is that the destination directory must exist before you run `git mv`.

     6→class CommandError(Exception):
     7→    """Raised by command helpers to signal a user-facing CLI error.
     8→
     9→    The CLI entrypoint catches this and prints ``message`` to stderr
    10→    before exiting with ``exit_code``.  Helpers should raise this instead

1→"""Pure coercion helpers for CLI/config input parsing."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→
     6→def coerce_positive_int(value: object, *, default: int, minimum: int = 1) -> int:
     7→    """Parse positive integer CLI/config inputs with a safe default."""
     8→    if value is None:
     9→        return default
    10→    if not isinstance(value, int | float | str):
    11→        return default
    12→    try:
    13→        parsed = int(value)
    14→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    15→        return default
    16→    return parsed if parsed >= minimum else default
    17→
    18→
    19→def coerce_positive_float(value: object, *, default: float, minimum: float = 0.1) -> float:
    20→    """Parse positive float CLI/config inputs with a safe default."""
    21→    if value is None:
    22→        return default
    23→    if not isinstance(value, int | float | str):
    24→        return default
    25→    try:
    26→        parsed = float(value)
    27→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    28→        return default
    29→    return parsed if parsed >= minimum else default
    30→

"""Canonical public path and file-write helpers for non-core layers."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from desloppify.core import file_paths as file_paths_mod


def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *rel_path* matches exclusion pattern."""
    return file_paths_mod.matches_exclusion(rel_path, exclusion)


def rel(path: str) -> str:
    """Return slash-normalized project-relative path when possible."""
    return file_paths_mod.rel(path)


def resolve_path(filepath: str) -> str:
    """Resolve *filepath* against project root when it is relative."""
    return file_paths_mod.resolve_path(filepath)


def resolve_scan_file(
    filepath: str | Path,
    *,
    scan_root: str | Path | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Resolve scan-time file paths with scan-root-first semantics."""

==> desloppify/core/source_scan_api.py <==
"""Canonical public source-discovery and file-cache API."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from desloppify.core import source_discovery as source_discovery_mod

DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS = source_discovery_mod.DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS


def _normalize_patterns(patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    normalized: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for raw in patterns:
        text = str(raw).strip()
        if not text or text in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(text)
        normalized.append(text)
    return normalized


def _normalize_extensions(extensions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    normalized: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for raw in extensions:
        text = str(raw).strip()
        if not text:
            continue

1→"""Path resolution and exclusion matching helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→import tempfile
     7→import fnmatch
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from desloppify.core.text.text_api import get_project_root
    11→
    12→
    13→def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    14→    """Check if a relative path matches an exclusion pattern."""
    15→    parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    16→    if exclusion in parts:
    17→        return True
    18→    if "*" in exclusion:
    19→        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(part, exclusion) for part in parts):
    20→            return True
    21→        # Full-path glob match for patterns with directory separators
    22→        # (e.g. "Wan2GP/**" should match "Wan2GP/models/rf.py").
    23→        if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    24→            normalized_path = rel_path.lstrip("./")
    25→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(normalized_path, exclusion):
    26→                return True
    27→    if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    28→        normalized = exclusion.rstrip("/").rstrip(os.sep)
    29→        return rel_path == normalized or rel_path.startswith(normalized + "/") or rel_path.startswith(
    30→            normalized + os.sep
    31→        )
    32→    return False
    33→
    34→
    35→def normalize_path_separators(path: str) -> str:
    36→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    37→
    38→
    39→def safe_relpath(path: str | Path, start: str | Path) -> str:
    40→    try:
    41→        return os.path.relpath(str(path), str(start))
    42→    except ValueError:
    43→        return str(Path(path).resolve())
    44→
    45→
    46→def rel(path: str) -> str:
    47→    root = get_project_root()
    48→    resolved = Path(path).resolve()
    49→    try:
    50→        return normalize_path_separators(str(resolved.relative_to(root)))
    51→    except ValueError:
    52→        return normalize_path_separators(safe_relpath(resolved, root))
    53→
    54→
    55→def resolve_path(filepath: str) -> str:
    56→    """Resolve a filepath to absolute, handling both relative and absolute."""
    57→    p = Path(filepath)
    58→    if p.is_absolute():
    59→        return str(p.resolve())
    60→    return str((get_project_root() / filepath).resolve())
    61→
    62→
    63→def resolve_scan_file(
    64→    filepath: str | Path,
    65→    *,
    66→    scan_root: str | Path | None = None,
    67→) -> Path:
    68→    """Resolve a scan file path with explicit scan-root-first semantics.
    69→
    70→    Relative file paths are resolved against ``scan_root`` first (when provided)
    71→    and then against the process project root as a fallback.
    72→    """
    73→    p = Path(filepath)
    74→    if p.is_absolute():
    75→        return p.resolve()
    76→
    77→    root = get_project_root()
    78→    if scan_root is not None:
    79→        scan_root_path = Path(scan_root)
    80→        scan_root_abs = (
    81→            scan_root_path.resolve()
    82→            if scan_root_path.is_absolute()
    83→            else (root / scan_root_path).resolve()
    84→        )
    85→        scan_candidate = (scan_root_abs / p).resolve()
    86→        if scan_candidate.exists():
    87→            return scan_candidate
    88→
    89→    return (root / p).resolve()
    90→
    91→
    92→def safe_write_text(filepath: str | Path, content: str) -> None:
    93→    """Atomically write text to a file using temp+rename."""
    94→    p = Path(filepath)
    95→    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    96→    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=p.parent, suffix=".tmp")
    97→    try:
    98→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
    99→            f.write(content)
   100→        os.replace(tmp, str(p))
   101→    except OSError:
   102→        if os.path.exists(tmp):
   103→            os.unlink(tmp)
   104→        raise
   105→
   106→
   107→def count_lines(path: Path) -> int:
   108→    """Count lines in a file without loading full contents into memory."""
   109→    count = 0
   110→    try:
   111→        with path.open("rb") as handle:
   112→            for _ in handle:
   113→                count += 1
   114→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   115→        return 0
   116→    return count
   117→

   124→    "resolve_path",
   125→    "resolve_scan_file",

    20→DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS = frozenset(

    46→def set_exclusions(patterns: list[str]) -> None:

    73→def file_cache_scope():
    74→    """Temporarily enable file cache within a context, with nested safety."""
    75→    runtime = current_runtime_context()
    76→    was_enabled = runtime.cache_enabled
    77→    if not was_enabled:
    78→        enable_file_cache()
    79→    try:
    80→        yield
    81→    finally:
    82→        if not was_enabled:
    83→            disable_file_cache()

    99→
   100→def collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root: Path) -> list[str]:
   101→    """All exclusion directories as absolute paths, for passing to external tools.
   102→
   103→    Combines DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS (non-glob entries) + get_exclusions() (runtime/config),
   104→    resolves each against *scan_root*. Filters out glob patterns (``*`` in name)
   105→    since most CLI tools want plain directory paths.
   106→    """
   107→    patterns = set()
   108→    for pat in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS:
   109→        if "*" not in pat:
   110→            patterns.add(pat)
   111→    patterns.update(p for p in get_exclusions() if p and "*" not in p)
   112→    return [str(scan_root / p) for p in sorted(patterns) if p]
   113→
   114→
   115→def _is_excluded_dir(name: str, rel_path: str, extra: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
   116→    in_default_exclusions = name in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS or name.endswith(".egg-info")
   117→    is_virtualenv_dir = name.startswith(".venv") or name.startswith("venv")
   118→    matches_extra_exclusion = bool(
   119→        extra
   120→        and any(
   121→            matches_exclusion(rel_path, exclusion)
   122→            or exclusion == name
   123→            or exclusion == name + "/**"
   124→            or exclusion == name + "/*"
   125→            for exclusion in extra
   126→        )
   127→    )
   128→    return in_default_exclusions or is_virtualenv_dir or matches_extra_exclusion
   129→
   130→
   131→def _find_source_files_cached(
   132→    path: str,
   133→    extensions: tuple[str, ...],
   134→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
   135→    extra_exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = (),
   136→) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   137→    """Cached file discovery using os.walk with traversal-time pruning."""
   138→    cache_key = (path, extensions, exclusions, extra_exclusions)
   139→    cache = current_runtime_context().source_file_cache
   140→    cached = cache.get(cache_key)
   141→    if cached is not None:
   142→        return cached
   143→
   144→    project_root = get_project_root()
   145→    root = Path(path)
   146→    if not root.is_absolute():
   147→        root = project_root / root
   148→    all_exclusions = (exclusions or ()) + extra_exclusions
   149→    ext_set = set(extensions)
   150→    files: list[str] = []
   151→    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
   152→        rel_dir = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(dirpath, project_root))
   153→        dirnames[:] = sorted(
   154→            d
   155→            for d in dirnames
   156→            if not _is_excluded_dir(d, rel_dir + "/" + d, all_exclusions)
   157→        )
   158→        for fname in filenames:
   159→            if any(fname.endswith(ext) for ext in ext_set):
   160→                full = os.path.join(dirpath, fname)
   161→                rel_file = _normalize_path_separators(_safe_relpath(full, project_root))
   162→                if all_exclusions and any(
   163→                    matches_exclusion(rel_file, ex) for ex in all_exclusions
   164→                ):
   165→                    continue
   166→                files.append(rel_file)
   167→    result = tuple(sorted(files))
   168→    cache.put(cache_key, result)
   169→    return result
   170→
   171→
   172→def find_source_files(
   173→    path: str | Path, extensions: list[str], exclusions: list[str] | None = None
   174→) -> list[str]:
   175→    """Find all files with given extensions under a path, excluding patterns."""
   176→    return list(
   177→        _find_source_files_cached(
   178→            str(path),
   179→            tuple(extensions),
   180→            tuple(exclusions) if exclusions else None,
   181→            get_exclusions(),
   182→        )
   183→    )
   184→
   185→
   186→def find_ts_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   187→    return find_source_files(path, [".ts", ".tsx"])
   188→
   189→
   190→def find_tsx_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   191→    return find_source_files(path, [".tsx"])
   192→
   193→
   194→def find_py_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   195→    return find_source_files(path, [".py"])

    12→def _normalize_patterns(patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    13→    normalized: list[str] = []
    14→    seen: set[str] = set()
    15→    for raw in patterns:
    16→        text = str(raw).strip()
    17→        if not text or text in seen:
    18→            continue
    19→        seen.add(text)
    20→        normalized.append(text)
    21→    return normalized
    22→
    23→
    24→def _normalize_extensions(extensions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    25→    normalized: list[str] = []
    26→    seen: set[str] = set()
    27→    for raw in extensions:
    28→        text = str(raw).strip()
    29→        if not text:
    30→            continue
    31→        if not text.startswith("."):
    32→            text = "." + text
    33→        text = text.lower()
    34→        if text in seen:
    35→            continue
    36→        seen.add(text)
    37→        normalized.append(text)
    38→    return normalized
    39→

    46→        f"({source} review, {assessed_at})"
    47→    )
    48→    lines.append(
    49→        "Fixing this issue and re-reviewing should improve the "
    50→        f"{display_dimension} score.\n"
    51→    )
    52→
    53→
    54→def _append_evidence(lines: list[str], detail: dict) -> None:
    55→    evidence = detail.get("evidence", [])
    56→    if evidence:
    57→        lines.append("## Evidence\n")
    58→        for item in evidence:
    59→            lines.append(f"- {item}")
    60→        lines.append("")
    61→
    62→    evidence_lines = detail.get("evidence_lines", [])
    63→    if evidence_lines:
    64→        lines.append("## Code References\n")
    65→        for item in evidence_lines:
    66→            lines.append(f"- {item}")
    67→        lines.append("")
    68→
    69→
    70→def _append_files(
    71→    lines: list[str], issue: dict, detail: dict, is_holistic: bool
    72→) -> None:
    73→    if is_holistic:
    74→        related_files = detail.get("related_files", [])
    75→        if not related_files:
    76→            return
    77→        lines.append("## Files\n")
    78→        for related in related_files:
    79→            lines.append(f"- `{related}`")
    80→        lines.append("")
    81→        return
    82→
    83→    file_path = issue.get("file", "")
    84→    if file_path and file_path != ".":
    85→        lines.append("## Files\n")
    86→        lines.append(f"- `{file_path}`")
    87→        lines.append("")
    88→
    89→
    90→def _append_investigation(lines: list[str], issue_id: str, detail: dict) -> bool:
    91→    investigation = detail.get("investigation")
    92→    if not investigation:
    93→        return False
    94→
    95→    investigated_at = detail.get("investigated_at", "")
    96→    date_suffix = ""
    97→    if investigated_at:
    98→        try:
    99→            date_suffix = (
   100→                f" ({datetime.fromisoformat(investigated_at).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')})"
   101→            )
   102→        except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
   103→            logger.debug(
   104→                "Invalid investigated_at value %r on %s: %s",
   105→                investigated_at,
   106→                issue_id,
   107→                exc,
   108→            )
   109→            date_suffix = " (invalid date)"
   110→
   111→    lines.append(f"## Investigation{date_suffix}\n")
   112→    lines.append(f"{investigation}\n")
   113→    return True
   114→
   115→
   116→def _append_footer(
   117→    lines: list[str],
   118→    *,
   119→    has_investigation: bool,
   120→    lang_name: str,
   121→    issue_id: str,
   122→    number: int | None,
   123→) -> None:
   124→    if has_investigation:
   125→        lines.append("## Ready to Fix\n")
   126→        lines.append("When done:\n")
   127→        lines.append("```bash")
   128→        lines.append(f'desloppify plan resolve "{issue_id}"')
   129→        lines.append("```\n")
   130→        return
   131→
   132→    lines.append("## Status: Needs Investigation\n")
   133→    lines.append("Investigate the files above, then resolve with a note:\n")
   134→    lines.append("```bash")
   135→    lines.append(
   136→        f'desloppify plan resolve "{issue_id}" --note "description of fix"'
   137→    )
   138→    lines.append("```\n")
   139→    lines.append("Or save detailed analysis first:\n")
   140→    lines.append("```bash")
   141→    lines.append(
   142→        f'desloppify show "{issue_id}" --notes analysis.md'
   143→    )
   144→    lines.append("```\n")
   145→
   146→
   147→def render_issue_detail(
   148→    issue: dict,
   149→    lang_name: str,
   150→    number: int | None = None,
   151→    subjective_assessments: dict | None = None,
   152→) -> str:
   153→    """Render one issue as a markdown work order from state."""
   154→    issue_id = issue["id"]
   155→    detail = issue.get("detail", {})
   156→    detector = issue.get("detector", "")
   157→    is_holistic = detail.get("holistic", False)
   158→    is_review = detector in ("review", "concerns")
   159→
   160→    # Derive dimension: from detail for review, from registry for mechanical.
   161→    raw_dimension = detail.get("dimension", "")
   162→    if raw_dimension:
   163→        dimension = raw_dimension.replace("_", " ")
   164→    else:
   165→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   166→        dimension = meta.dimension.replace("_", " ") if meta else "unknown"
   167→
   168→    confidence = issue.get("confidence", "low")
   169→
   170→    parts = issue_id.split("::")
   171→    identifier = parts[-2] if len(parts) >= 3 else issue.get("file", "unknown")
   172→    weight, impact_pts, _ = issue_weight(issue)
   173→    label = "+++" if weight >= 8 else "++" if weight >= 5 else "+"
   174→
   175→    lines: list[str] = []
   176→    lines.append(f"# {dimension}: {identifier}\n")
   177→    lines.append(f"**Issue**: `{issue_id}`  ")
   178→    if not is_review:
   179→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   180→        detector_display = meta.display if meta else detector
   181→        lines.append(f"**Detector**: {detector_display} | **Confidence**: {confidence}  ")
   182→    else:
   183→        lines.append(f"**Dimension**: {dimension} | **Confidence**: {confidence}  ")
   184→    lines.append(f"**Score impact**: {label} (~{impact_pts:.1f} pts)\n")
   185→
   186→    _append_assessment_context(lines, issue, subjective_assessments)
   187→
   188→    lines.append("## Problem\n")
   189→    lines.append(f"{issue.get('summary', '')}\n")
   190→
   191→    _append_evidence(lines, detail)
   192→
   193→    suggestion = detail.get("suggestion", "")
   194→    if suggestion:
   195→        lines.append("## Suggested Fix\n")
   196→        lines.append(f"{suggestion}\n")
   197→
   198→    _append_files(lines, issue, detail, is_holistic)
   199→
   200→    reasoning = detail.get("reasoning", "")
   201→    if reasoning:
   202→        lines.append("## Why This Matters\n")
   203→        lines.append(f"{reasoning}\n")
   204→
   205→    has_investigation = _append_investigation(lines, issue_id, detail)
   206→    _append_footer(
   207→        lines,
   208→        has_investigation=has_investigation,
   209→        lang_name=lang_name,
   210→        issue_id=issue_id,
   211→        number=number,
   212→    )
   213→    return "\n".join(lines)
   214→

1→"""Cross-platform grep-style helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→import re
     7→
     8→from desloppify.core.text.text_api import get_project_root
     9→from desloppify.search import grep_files_containing as _search_grep_files_containing
    10→from desloppify.core.source_discovery import read_file_text as _read_file_text
    11→
    12→
    13→def grep_files(
    14→    pattern: str, file_list: list[str], *, flags: int = 0
    15→) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    16→    """Search files for a regex pattern. Returns (filepath, lineno, line_text)."""
    17→    compiled = re.compile(pattern, flags)
    18→    results: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    19→    for filepath in file_list:
    20→        abs_path = filepath if os.path.isabs(filepath) else str(get_project_root() / filepath)
    21→        content = _read_file_text(abs_path)
    22→        if content is None:
    23→            continue
    24→        for lineno, line in enumerate(content.splitlines(), 1):
    25→            if compiled.search(line):
    26→                results.append((filepath, lineno, line))
    27→    return results
    28→
    29→
    30→def grep_files_containing(
    31→    names: set[str], file_list: list[str], *, word_boundary: bool = True
    32→) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    33→    r"""Find which files contain which names. Returns {name: set(filepaths)}."""
    34→    return _search_grep_files_containing(
    35→        names,
    36→        file_list,
    37→        word_boundary=word_boundary,
    38→    )
    39→
    40→
    41→def grep_count_files(
    42→    name: str, file_list: list[str], *, word_boundary: bool = True
    43→) -> list[str]:
    44→    """Return list of files containing name."""
    45→    if word_boundary:
    46→        pat = re.compile(r"\b" + re.escape(name) + r"\b")
    47→    else:
    48→        pat = re.compile(re.escape(name))
    49→    matching: list[str] = []
    50→    for filepath in file_list:
    51→        abs_path = filepath if os.path.isabs(filepath) else str(get_project_root() / filepath)
    52→        content = _read_file_text(abs_path)
    53→        if content is None:
    54→            continue
    55→        if pat.search(content):
    56→            matching.append(filepath)
    57→    return matching
    58→
    59→
    60→__all__ = [
    61→    "grep_count_files",
    62→    "grep_files",
    63→    "grep_files_containing",
    64→]
    65→

1→"""Terminal output helpers shared across commands."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import os
     7→import sys
     8→from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
     9→from typing import Any
    10→
    11→LOC_COMPACT_THRESHOLD = 10000  # Switch from "1,234" to "1K" format
    12→
    13→COLORS = {
    14→    "reset": "\033[0m",
    15→    "bold": "\033[1m",
    16→    "dim": "\033[2m",
    17→    "red": "\033[31m",
    18→    "green": "\033[32m",
    19→    "yellow": "\033[33m",
    20→    "blue": "\033[34m",
    21→    "cyan": "\033[36m",
    22→}
    23→
    24→NO_COLOR = os.environ.get("NO_COLOR") is not None
    25→
    26→
    27→def colorize(text: str, color: str) -> str:
    28→    if NO_COLOR or not sys.stdout.isatty():
    29→        return str(text)
    30→    return f"{COLORS.get(color, '')}{text}{COLORS['reset']}"
    31→
    32→
    33→def log(msg: str) -> None:
    34→    """Print a dim status message to stderr."""
    35→    print(colorize(msg, "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
    36→
    37→
    38→def print_table(
    39→    headers: list[str], rows: list[list[str]], widths: list[int] | None = None
    40→) -> None:
    41→    if not rows:
    42→        return
    43→    if not widths:
    44→        widths = [
    45→            max(len(str(h)), *(len(str(r[i])) for r in rows))
    46→            for i, h in enumerate(headers)
    47→        ]
    48→    header_line = "  ".join(h.ljust(w) for h, w in zip(headers, widths, strict=False))
    49→    print(colorize(header_line, "bold"))
    50→    print(colorize("─" * (sum(widths) + 2 * (len(widths) - 1)), "dim"))
    51→    for row in rows:
    52→        print("  ".join(str(v).ljust(w) for v, w in zip(row, widths, strict=False)))
    53→
    54→
    55→def display_entries(
    56→    args: object,
    57→    entries: Sequence[Any],
    58→    *,
    59→    label: str,
    60→    empty_msg: str,
    61→    columns: Sequence[str],
    62→    widths: list[int] | None,
    63→    row_fn: Callable[[Any], list[str]],
    64→    json_payload: dict | None = None,
    65→    overflow: bool = True,
    66→) -> bool:
    67→    """Standard JSON/empty/table display for detect commands."""
    68→    if getattr(args, "json", False):
    69→        payload = json_payload or {"count": len(entries), "entries": entries}
    70→        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    71→        return True
    72→    if not entries:
    73→        print(colorize(empty_msg, "green"))
    74→        return False
    75→    print(colorize(f"\n{label}: {len(entries)}\n", "bold"))
    76→    top = getattr(args, "top", 20)
    77→    rows = [row_fn(e) for e in entries[:top]]
    78→    print_table(list(columns), rows, widths)
    79→    if overflow and len(entries) > top:
    80→        print(f"\n  ... and {len(entries) - top} more")
    81→    return True
    82→
    83→
    84→__all__ = [
    85→    "LOC_COMPACT_THRESHOLD",
    86→    "COLORS",
    87→    "NO_COLOR",
    88→    "colorize",
    89→    "display_entries",
    90→    "log",
    91→    "print_table",
    92→]
    93→

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import sys
     6→from dataclasses import dataclass
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from desloppify.core.search.search_query_paths import query_file_path
    10→from desloppify.core.output_contract import OutputResult
    11→from desloppify.core.search.search_query import write_query as _core_write_query
    12→from desloppify.core.output import colorize
    13→
    14→
    15→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    16→class QueryWriter:
    17→    """Command-level query artifact writer with explicit failure policy."""
    18→
    19→    query_file: Path
    20→
    21→    def write(self, data: dict) -> OutputResult:
    22→        return _core_write_query(data, query_file=self.query_file)
    23→
    24→    def write_best_effort(self, data: dict, *, context: str) -> OutputResult:
    25→        result = self.write(data)
    26→        if not result.ok:
    27→            detail = result.message or "unknown write failure"
    28→            print(
    29→                colorize(
    30→                    f"  Warning: {context} succeeded but query artifact was not written ({detail}).",
    31→                    "yellow",
    32→                ),
    33→                file=sys.stderr,
    34→            )
    35→        return result
    36→
    37→
    38→def query_writer() -> QueryWriter:
    39→    """Construct a writer bound to the active runtime query path."""
    40→    return QueryWriter(query_file=query_file_path())
    41→
    42→
    43→def write_query(data: dict) -> OutputResult:
    44→    """Write structured query output using default best-effort policy."""
    45→    return write_query_best_effort(data, context="query payload update")
    46→
    47→
    48→def write_query_best_effort(data: dict, *, context: str) -> OutputResult:
    49→    """Write query payload and emit a contextual warning on failure."""
    50→    return query_writer().write_best_effort(data, context=context)
    51→
    52→
    53→__all__ = [

    55→    "query_file_path",

1→"""File writing and rollback-safe application helpers for move command."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import shutil
     6→import sys
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from desloppify.core.fallbacks import restore_files_best_effort, warn_best_effort
    10→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import rel, safe_write_text
    11→from desloppify.core.output import colorize
    12→
    13→
    14→def _rollback_written_files(written_files: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    15→    failed = restore_files_best_effort(written_files, safe_write_text)
    16→    for filepath in failed:
    17→        warn_best_effort(f"Could not restore {rel(filepath)}")
    18→
    19→
    20→def _rollback_move_target(dest_abs: str, source_abs: str, *, target_name: str) -> None:
    21→    if not (Path(dest_abs).exists() and not Path(source_abs).exists()):
    22→        return
    23→    try:
    24→        shutil.move(dest_abs, source_abs)
    25→    except OSError:
    26→        warn_best_effort(f"Could not move {target_name} back to {rel(source_abs)}")
    27→
    28→
    29→def apply_file_move(
    30→    source_abs: str,
    31→    dest_abs: str,
    32→    importer_changes: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
    33→    self_changes: list[tuple[str, str]],
    34→) -> None:
    35→    """Move a file and apply import replacements with rollback on failure."""
    36→    new_contents: dict[str, str] = {}
    37→    if self_changes:
    38→        content = Path(source_abs).read_text()
    39→        for old_str, new_str in self_changes:
    40→            content = content.replace(old_str, new_str)
    41→        new_contents[dest_abs] = content
    42→
    43→    for filepath, replacements in importer_changes.items():
    44→        content = Path(filepath).read_text()
    45→        for old_str, new_str in replacements:
    46→            content = content.replace(old_str, new_str)
    47→        new_contents[filepath] = content
    48→
    49→    Path(dest_abs).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    50→    written_files: dict[str, str] = {}
    51→    try:
    52→        shutil.move(source_abs, dest_abs)
    53→
    54→        if dest_abs in new_contents:
    55→            written_files[dest_abs] = Path(dest_abs).read_text()
    56→            safe_write_text(dest_abs, new_contents[dest_abs])
    57→
    58→        for filepath in importer_changes:
    59→            if filepath in new_contents:
    60→                written_files[filepath] = Path(filepath).read_text()
    61→                safe_write_text(filepath, new_contents[filepath])
    62→
    63→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, shutil.Error) as ex:
    64→        print(colorize(f"\n  Error during move: {ex}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
    65→        print(colorize("  Rolling back...", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
    66→        _rollback_written_files(written_files)
    67→        _rollback_move_target(dest_abs, source_abs, target_name="file")
    68→        raise
    69→
    70→
    71→def apply_directory_move(
    72→    source_abs: str,
    73→    dest_abs: str,
    74→    source_path: Path,
    75→    external_changes: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
    76→    internal_changes: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
    77→) -> None:
    78→    """Move a directory and apply external/internal import replacements."""
    79→    Path(dest_abs).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    80→    written_files: dict[str, str] = {}
    81→    try:
    82→        shutil.move(source_abs, dest_abs)
    83→
    84→        for src_file, changes in internal_changes.items():
    85→            rel_in_dir = Path(src_file).relative_to(source_path)
    86→            dest_file = Path(dest_abs) / rel_in_dir
    87→            original = dest_file.read_text()
    88→            content = original
    89→            for old_str, new_str in changes:
    90→                content = content.replace(old_str, new_str)
    91→            written_files[str(dest_file)] = original
    92→            safe_write_text(dest_file, content)
    93→
    94→        for filepath, replacements in external_changes.items():
    95→            original = Path(filepath).read_text()
    96→            content = original
    97→            for old_str, new_str in replacements:
    98→                content = content.replace(old_str, new_str)
    99→            written_files[filepath] = original
   100→            safe_write_text(filepath, content)
   101→
   102→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, shutil.Error) as ex:
   103→        print(
   104→            colorize(f"\n  Error during directory move: {ex}", "red"), file=sys.stderr
   105→        )
   106→        print(colorize("  Rolling back...", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
   107→        _rollback_written_files(written_files)
   108→        _rollback_move_target(dest_abs, source_abs, target_name="directory")

   131→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   132→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   133→    completed = [s for s in ("observe", "reflect", "organize") if s in stages]
   134→    if completed:
   135→        return (
   136→            f"TRIAGE MODE ({len(completed)}/4 stages complete) — "
   137→            "complete all stages to exit. Run: desloppify plan triage"
   138→        )
   139→    return (
   140→        "TRIAGE MODE — review issues need analysis before fixing. "

1→"""Canonical public source-discovery and file-cache API."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.core import source_discovery as source_discovery_mod
     8→
     9→DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS = source_discovery_mod.DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS
    10→
    11→
    12→def _normalize_patterns(patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    13→    normalized: list[str] = []
    14→    seen: set[str] = set()
    15→    for raw in patterns:
    16→        text = str(raw).strip()
    17→        if not text or text in seen:
    18→            continue
    19→        seen.add(text)
    20→        normalized.append(text)
    21→    return normalized
    22→
    23→
    24→def _normalize_extensions(extensions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    25→    normalized: list[str] = []
    26→    seen: set[str] = set()
    27→    for raw in extensions:
    28→        text = str(raw).strip()
    29→        if not text:
    30→            continue
    31→        if not text.startswith("."):
    32→            text = "." + text
    33→        text = text.lower()
    34→        if text in seen:
    35→            continue
    36→        seen.add(text)
    37→        normalized.append(text)
    38→    return normalized
    39→
    40→
    41→def set_exclusions(patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    42→    source_discovery_mod.set_exclusions(_normalize_patterns(patterns))
    43→
    44→
    45→def get_exclusions() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    46→    return source_discovery_mod.get_exclusions()
    47→
    48→
    49→def enable_file_cache() -> None:
    50→    source_discovery_mod.enable_file_cache()
    51→
    52→
    53→def disable_file_cache() -> None:
    54→    source_discovery_mod.disable_file_cache()
    55→
    56→
    57→def is_file_cache_enabled() -> bool:
    58→    return source_discovery_mod.is_file_cache_enabled()
    59→
    60→
    61→def read_file_text(filepath: str) -> str | None:
    62→    return source_discovery_mod.read_file_text(filepath)
    63→
    64→
    65→def clear_source_file_cache_for_tests() -> None:
    66→    source_discovery_mod.clear_source_file_cache_for_tests()
    67→
    68→
    69→def collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root: Path) -> list[str]:
    70→    return source_discovery_mod.collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root.resolve())
    71→
    72→
    73→def find_source_files(
    74→    path: str | Path,
    75→    extensions: list[str],
    76→    exclusions: list[str] | None = None,
    77→) -> list[str]:
    78→    normalized_exts = _normalize_extensions(extensions)
    79→    if not normalized_exts:
    80→        return []
    81→    normalized_exclusions = (
    82→        _normalize_patterns(exclusions) if exclusions is not None else None
    83→    )
    84→    return source_discovery_mod.find_source_files(
    85→        path,
    86→        normalized_exts,
    87→        normalized_exclusions,
    88→    )
    89→
    90→
    91→def find_ts_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
    92→    return find_source_files(path, [".ts", ".tsx"])
    93→
    94→
    95→def find_tsx_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
    96→    return find_source_files(path, [".tsx"])
    97→
    98→
    99→def find_py_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
   100→    return find_source_files(path, [".py"])
   101→
   102→

1→"""Text-oriented utility helpers split from the main utils facade."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.core.runtime_state import current_runtime_context
     9→
    10→_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_ROOT", Path.cwd())).resolve()
    11→
    12→
    13→def get_project_root() -> Path:
    14→    """Return the active project root, checking RuntimeContext first.
    15→
    16→    Tests set ``RuntimeContext.project_root`` to point at a tmp directory.
    17→    Production code uses the process-level default from $DESLOPPIFY_ROOT / cwd.
    18→    """
    19→    override = current_runtime_context().project_root
    20→    if override is not None:
    21→        return override
    22→    return _DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROOT
    23→
    24→
    25→def read_code_snippet(
    26→    filepath: str,
    27→    line: int,
    28→    context: int = 1,
    29→    *,
    30→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
    31→) -> str | None:
    32→    """Read ±context lines around a line number. Returns formatted string or None."""
    33→    try:
    34→        root = (
    35→            Path(project_root).resolve()
    36→            if project_root is not None
    37→            # Runtime-aware default; preserves RuntimeContext/project-root overrides.
    38→            else get_project_root()
    39→        )
    40→        full = Path(filepath)
    41→        if not full.is_absolute():
    42→            full = root / full
    43→        content = full.read_text(errors="replace")
    44→    except OSError:
    45→        return None
    46→    lines = content.splitlines()
    47→    if line < 1 or line > len(lines):
    48→        return None
    49→    start = max(0, line - 1 - context)
    50→    end = min(len(lines), line + context)
    51→    parts = []
    52→    for i in range(start, end):
    53→        ln = i + 1
    54→        marker = "→" if ln == line else " "
    55→        text = lines[i]
    56→        if len(text) > 120:
    57→            text = text[:117] + "..."
    58→        parts.append(f"    {marker} {ln:>4} │ {text}")
    59→    return "\n".join(parts)
    60→
    61→
    62→def get_area(filepath: str, *, min_depth: int = 2) -> str:
    63→    """Derive an area name from a file path (generic: first 2 path components).
    64→
    65→    *min_depth* controls the minimum number of path components required before
    66→    the two-component area is returned.  The default (2) means a path like
    67→    ``"a/b"`` already qualifies.  Python uses ``min_depth=3`` so that
    68→    ``"pkg/mod.py"`` returns just ``"pkg"`` while ``"pkg/sub/mod.py"`` returns
    69→    ``"pkg/sub"``.
    70→    """
    71→    text = (filepath or "").strip()
    72→    if not text:
    73→        return "(unknown)"
    74→    parts = Path(text).parts
    75→    if not parts:
    76→        return "(unknown)"
    77→    return "/".join(parts[:2]) if len(parts) >= min_depth else parts[0]
    78→
    79→
    80→def _consume_escaped_char(text: str, index: int, out: list[str]) -> int | None:
    81→    if text[index] != "\\" or index + 1 >= len(text):
    82→        return None
    83→    out.append(text[index : index + 2])
    84→    return index + 2
    85→
    86→
    87→def _skip_comment(text: str, index: int) -> int | None:
    88→    if text[index] != "/" or index + 1 >= len(text):
    89→        return None
    90→    next_char = text[index + 1]
    91→    if next_char == "/":
    92→        newline_at = text.find("\n", index)
    93→        return -1 if newline_at == -1 else newline_at
    94→    if next_char == "*":
    95→        end = text.find("*/", index + 2)
    96→        return -1 if end == -1 else end + 2
    97→    return None
    98→
    99→
   100→def strip_c_style_comments(text: str) -> str:
   101→    """Strip // and /* */ comments while preserving string literals."""
   102→    result: list[str] = []
   103→    i = 0
   104→    in_str = None
   105→    while i < len(text):
   106→        ch = text[i]
   107→        if in_str:
   108→            escaped_next = _consume_escaped_char(text, i, result)
   109→            if escaped_next is not None:
   110→                i = escaped_next
   111→                continue
   112→            if ch == in_str:
   113→                in_str = None
   114→            result.append(ch)
   115→            i += 1
   116→            continue
   117→
   118→        if ch in ('"', "'", "`"):
   119→            in_str = ch
   120→            result.append(ch)
   121→            i += 1
   122→            continue
   123→
   124→        skipped_to = _skip_comment(text, i)
   125→        if skipped_to is not None:
   126→            if skipped_to == -1:
   127→                break
   128→            i = skipped_to
   129→            continue
   130→
   131→        result.append(ch)
   132→        i += 1
   133→    return "".join(result)
   134→
   135→
   136→def is_numeric(value: object) -> bool:
   137→    """Return True if *value* is an int or float but NOT a bool.
   138→
   139→    Python's ``bool`` is a subclass of ``int``, so ``isinstance(True, int)``
   140→    is ``True``.  Many JSON-derived payloads need to distinguish real numbers
   141→    from booleans; this helper centralises that guard.
   142→    """
   143→    return isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool)
   144→
   145→
   146→__all__ = [
   147→    "get_area",
   148→    "get_project_root",
   149→    "is_numeric",
   150→    "read_code_snippet",
   151→    "strip_c_style_comments",
   152→]

1→"""Pure coercion helpers for CLI/config input parsing."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→
     6→def coerce_positive_int(value: object, *, default: int, minimum: int = 1) -> int:
     7→    """Parse positive integer CLI/config inputs with a safe default."""
     8→    if value is None:
     9→        return default
    10→    if not isinstance(value, int | float | str):
    11→        return default
    12→    try:
    13→        parsed = int(value)
    14→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    15→        return default
    16→    return parsed if parsed >= minimum else default
    17→
    18→
    19→def coerce_positive_float(value: object, *, default: float, minimum: float = 0.1) -> float:
    20→    """Parse positive float CLI/config inputs with a safe default."""
    21→    if value is None:
    22→        return default
    23→    if not isinstance(value, int | float | str):
    24→        return default
    25→    try:
    26→        parsed = float(value)
    27→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    28→        return default
    29→    return parsed if parsed >= minimum else default
    30→
    31→
    32→def coerce_non_negative_float(value: object, *, default: float) -> float:
    33→    """Parse non-negative float CLI/config inputs with a safe default."""
    34→    if value is None:
    35→        return default
    36→    if not isinstance(value, int | float | str):
    37→        return default
    38→    try:
    39→        parsed = float(value)
    40→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    41→        return default

    47→    if value is None:

    51→    try:

    60→    try:

    62→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    63→        return default
    64→    return max(0.0, min(1.0, parsed))

1→"""Path resolution and exclusion matching helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import fnmatch
     6→import os
     7→import tempfile
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from desloppify.core.text.text_api import get_project_root
    11→
    12→
    13→def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    14→    """Check if a relative path matches an exclusion pattern."""
    15→    parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    16→    if exclusion in parts:
    17→        return True
    18→    if "*" in exclusion:
    19→        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(part, exclusion) for part in parts):
    20→            return True
    21→        # Full-path glob match for patterns with directory separators
    22→        # (e.g. "Wan2GP/**" should match "Wan2GP/models/rf.py").
    23→        if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    24→            normalized_path = rel_path.lstrip("./")
    25→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(normalized_path, exclusion):
    26→                return True
    27→    if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    28→        normalized = exclusion.rstrip("/").rstrip(os.sep)
    29→        return rel_path == normalized or rel_path.startswith(normalized + "/") or rel_path.startswith(
    30→            normalized + os.sep
    31→        )
    32→    return False
    33→
    34→
    35→def normalize_path_separators(path: str) -> str:
    36→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    37→
    38→
    39→def safe_relpath(path: str | Path, start: str | Path) -> str:
    40→    try:
    41→        return os.path.relpath(str(path), str(start))
    42→    except ValueError:
    43→        return str(Path(path).resolve())
    44→
    45→
    46→def rel(path: str) -> str:
    47→    root = get_project_root()
    48→    resolved = Path(path).resolve()
    49→    try:
    50→        return normalize_path_separators(str(resolved.relative_to(root)))
    51→    except ValueError:
    52→        return normalize_path_separators(safe_relpath(resolved, root))
    53→
    54→
    55→def resolve_path(filepath: str) -> str:
    56→    """Resolve a filepath to absolute, handling both relative and absolute."""
    57→    p = Path(filepath)
    58→    if p.is_absolute():
    59→        return str(p.resolve())
    60→    return str((get_project_root() / filepath).resolve())
    61→
    62→
    63→def resolve_scan_file(
    64→    filepath: str | Path,
    65→    *,
    66→    scan_root: str | Path | None = None,
    67→) -> Path:
    68→    """Resolve a scan file path with explicit scan-root-first semantics.
    69→
    70→    Relative file paths are resolved against ``scan_root`` first (when provided)
    71→    and then against the process project root as a fallback.
    72→    """
    73→    p = Path(filepath)
    74→    if p.is_absolute():
    75→        return p.resolve()
    76→
    77→    root = get_project_root()
    78→    if scan_root is not None:
    79→        scan_root_path = Path(scan_root)
    80→        scan_root_abs = (
    81→            scan_root_path.resolve()
    82→            if scan_root_path.is_absolute()
    83→            else (root / scan_root_path).resolve()
    84→        )
    85→        scan_candidate = (scan_root_abs / p).resolve()
    86→        if scan_candidate.exists():
    87→            return scan_candidate
    88→
    89→    return (root / p).resolve()
    90→
    91→
    92→def safe_write_text(filepath: str | Path, content: str) -> None:
    93→    """Atomically write text to a file using temp+rename."""
    94→    p = Path(filepath)
    95→    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    96→    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=p.parent, suffix=".tmp")
    97→    try:
    98→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
    99→            f.write(content)
   100→        os.replace(tmp, str(p))
   101→    except OSError:
   102→        if os.path.exists(tmp):
   103→            os.unlink(tmp)
   104→        raise
   105→
   106→
   107→def count_lines(path: Path) -> int:
   108→    """Count lines in a file without loading full contents into memory."""
   109→    count = 0
   110→    try:
   111→        with path.open("rb") as handle:
   112→            for _ in handle:
   113→                count += 1
   114→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   115→        return 0
   116→    return count
   117→

   124→    "resolve_path",
   125→    "resolve_scan_file",
   126→    "safe_relpath",

1→"""Language registry: plugin registration and language resolution."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import inspect
     6→from collections.abc import Callable
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→from typing import TypeVar
     9→
    10→from desloppify.languages._framework import (
    11→    discovery,
    12→    registry_state,
    13→    resolution,
    14→    runtime,
    15→)
    16→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    17→from desloppify.languages._framework.contract_validation import validate_lang_contract
    18→from desloppify.languages._framework.policy import REQUIRED_DIRS, REQUIRED_FILES
    19→from desloppify.languages._framework.resolution import (
    20→    auto_detect_lang,
    21→    available_langs,
    22→    get_lang,
    23→    make_lang_config,
    24→)
    25→from desloppify.languages._framework.structure_validation import validate_lang_structure
    26→
    27→T = TypeVar("T")
    28→
    29→
    30→def register_lang(name: str) -> Callable[[T], T]:
    31→    """Decorator to register a language config class.
    32→
    33→    Validates structure, instantiates the class, validates the contract,
    34→    and stores the *instance* in the registry.
    35→    """
    36→
    37→    def decorator(cls: T) -> T:
    38→        module = inspect.getmodule(cls)
    39→        if module and hasattr(module, "__file__"):
    40→            validate_lang_structure(Path(module.__file__).parent, name)
    41→        if isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, LangConfig):
    42→            cfg = make_lang_config(name, cls)  # instantiate + validate
    43→            registry_state.register(name, cfg)  # store instance
    44→        else:
    45→            registry_state.register(name, cls)  # test doubles
    46→        return cls
    47→
    48→    return decorator
    49→
    50→
    51→def register_generic_lang(name: str, cfg: LangConfig) -> None:
    52→    """Register a pre-built language plugin instance (no package structure required)."""
    53→    validate_lang_contract(name, cfg)
    54→    registry_state.register(name, cfg)
    55→
    56→
    57→def reload_lang_plugins() -> list[str]:
    58→    """Force plugin rediscovery and return refreshed language names."""
    59→    discovery.load_all(force_reload=True)
    60→    return sorted(registry_state.all_keys())
    61→
    62→
    63→__all__ = [
    64→    "REQUIRED_FILES",
    65→    "REQUIRED_DIRS",
    66→    "register_lang",

    74→    "validate_lang_contract",

1→"""Canonical public source-discovery and file-cache API."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.core import source_discovery as source_discovery_mod
     8→
     9→DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS = source_discovery_mod.DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS
    10→
    11→
    12→def _normalize_patterns(patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    13→    normalized: list[str] = []
    14→    seen: set[str] = set()
    15→    for raw in patterns:
    16→        text = str(raw).strip()
    17→        if not text or text in seen:
    18→            continue
    19→        seen.add(text)
    20→        normalized.append(text)
    21→    return normalized
    22→
    23→
    24→def _normalize_extensions(extensions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    25→    normalized: list[str] = []
    26→    seen: set[str] = set()
    27→    for raw in extensions:
    28→        text = str(raw).strip()
    29→        if not text:
    30→            continue
    31→        if not text.startswith("."):
    32→            text = "." + text
    33→        text = text.lower()
    34→        if text in seen:
    35→            continue
    36→        seen.add(text)
    37→        normalized.append(text)
    38→    return normalized
    39→
    40→
    41→def set_exclusions(patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    42→    source_discovery_mod.set_exclusions(_normalize_patterns(patterns))
    43→
    44→
    45→def get_exclusions() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    46→    return source_discovery_mod.get_exclusions()
    47→
    48→
    49→def enable_file_cache() -> None:
    50→    source_discovery_mod.enable_file_cache()
    51→
    52→
    53→def disable_file_cache() -> None:
    54→    source_discovery_mod.disable_file_cache()
    55→
    56→
    57→def is_file_cache_enabled() -> bool:
    58→    return source_discovery_mod.is_file_cache_enabled()
    59→
    60→
    61→def read_file_text(filepath: str) -> str | None:
    62→    return source_discovery_mod.read_file_text(filepath)
    63→
    64→
    65→def clear_source_file_cache_for_tests() -> None:
    66→    source_discovery_mod.clear_source_file_cache_for_tests()
    67→
    68→
    69→def collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root: Path) -> list[str]:
    70→    return source_discovery_mod.collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root.resolve())
    71→
    72→
    73→def find_source_files(
    74→    path: str | Path,
    75→    extensions: list[str],
    76→    exclusions: list[str] | None = None,
    77→) -> list[str]:
    78→    normalized_exts = _normalize_extensions(extensions)
    79→    if not normalized_exts:
    80→        return []
    81→    normalized_exclusions = (
    82→        _normalize_patterns(exclusions) if exclusions is not None else None
    83→    )
    84→    return source_discovery_mod.find_source_files(
    85→        path,
    86→        normalized_exts,
    87→        normalized_exclusions,
    88→    )
    89→
    90→
    91→def find_ts_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
    92→    return find_source_files(path, [".ts", ".tsx"])
    93→
    94→
    95→def find_tsx_files(path: str | Path) -> list[str]:
    96→    return find_source_files(path, [".tsx"])
    97→
    98→
